Survey End Page

SurveyMonkey
Survey End Page

Paid Feature: The features listed below are paid features. Some are only available on particular paid plans—see what's on your plan.

The Survey End Page collector option lets you choose what respondents see after they complete your survey.

The Survey End Page you select is specific to a collector. If you’re sending your survey using multiple collectors, you need to update the Survey End Page option on each collector.

Tip! For a more personalized survey taking experience, use Advanced branching to redirect respondents to various URLs after completing more of your survey.

Choosing a Survey End Page

To choose your Survey End Page:

From the Publish survey section, select the name of the collector and find the collector options.
Select Survey End Page. You may need to select Show advanced options.
Choose a Survey End Page option.

The Survey End Page option isn't available if you embed your survey using the Website collector.

Survey End Page Options

Depending on the collector type you're using to send your survey, you can choose one of the following options for people to see after completing your survey:

Option	Description
Show the default end page	

Respondents see a SurveyMonkey webpage. It thanks them for taking the survey and either provides information about our site or invites them to take another optional survey offered by our SurveyMonkey research team.

Some Enterprise customers will have a custom end page that has been set by their Primary Admin. Reach out to your Admin or Customer Success Manager to learn about your team's default end page.
Redirect to a URL	

Respondents are redirected to a webpage of your choice.


Loop to start and allow another response	The first page of your survey opens so it can be taken again. To use this option, you need to use the Web Link collector and turn on Multiple Responses.
Close the window or tab	The survey window or tab automatically closes. Depending on a respondent's browser settings, they may see a blank page or be asked to confirm they want to close the window.
Removing SurveyMonkey Branding

If you don't want SurveyMonkey branding to show on the Survey End Page, you can change the domain to a White Label URL.

Comparing Survey Results

SurveyMonkey
Comparing Survey Results

Compare rules let you choose two or more answer options from a single question and view them side-by-side. For example, if you include a question in your survey asking people what age they are, you can create a compare rule to view the survey results for each age range. This can help you understand how different age groups responded to questions in your survey.

TIP! To compare results from multiple surveys, create a multi-survey analysis dashboard. To do more complex comparisons using answer choices from multiple questions, create a Crosstab report.

Creating Compare Rules

You can create a compare rule using the following closed-ended question types: Multiple Choice, Checkboxes, Star Rating, Dropdown, Matrix/Rating Scale, Image Choice, or Ranking.

If you create a compare rule using a Matrix/Rating Scale question, you won't be able to combine or hide its answer choices.

To create a compare rule:

Go to the Analyze Results section of your survey.
Select Rules from the toolbar, then click + Compare.
Select a compare rule type.
Choose the criteria you want to focus on.
Click Apply.

You'll see any active rules at the top of the page. We'll also show the number of responses included in your rule, compared to the number of responses in your survey.

You can turn on statistical significance to automatically calculate when your results show differences that are statistically unlikely to be due to random chance.

When you use a Slider question in your survey and a compare rule is applied, the Slider charts won’t display in your results.

Types of Compare Rules
Rule Type
	
Description

Question & Answer	Focus on people who answered a question with a specific answer choice.
A/B Test	If you used an A/B test in your survey, compare responses from people who saw each variable.
Collector	If you used multiple collectors, see a side-by-side comparison of how people from different collectors responded to your survey.
Time Period	Compare responses between date ranges.
Managing Compare Rules

To manage your compare rules:

Select Rules from the toolbar.
Click the three dots menu next to a rule to unapply, edit, rename, copy, or delete it.

Click the name of the rule to turn it on or off. A green check mark ✅ next to a rule means that the rule is active. You'll also see any active rules at the top of the page.

Exporting & Sharing Rules

You can export your results with a rule applied or share your survey results with other people.

Save multiple rules together as a view to easily access different sections of your data.

Exporting to XLS: When you use a compare rule on a Checkboxes question, the XLS file will show the number of people who submitted your survey, not the number of responses.

SurveyMonkey
Dropdown Question

Dropdown is a closed-ended question that allows respondents to choose one answer choice from a list of choices presented in a dropdown menu.

Video Overview
Creating a Dropdown Question

To add this question type:

Drag and drop Dropdown into your survey from the Build section.
In the Answers fields, enter each answer choice. If you have a long list, you can copy and paste the answer options.
Configure any additional options.
Click Save.
Options & Settings
Score This Question (enable quiz mode)

You can score your question to make your survey into a quiz. Learn more: Quizzes

Additional Options

Under the Edit, Options, and Logic tabs, you can further customize the question in the following ways:

Add an "Other" Answer Option or Comment Field
Require an Answer
Change the Question Size & Layout
Sort, Randomize, or Flip Choices
Add Question Skip Logic
Add Question & Answer Piping

Learn more: Editing Questions

Survey Behavior

Before you send out your survey, preview your survey design to see what your survey will look like to respondents.

Respondents can only select one answer from the Dropdown question.

Analyzing Results

See example results (English only) »

Dropdown questions are easy to analyze since they only allow one answer. You can create Filter and Compare rules to break down your survey results, and every chart type is available for this question.

Designing Your Survey

Question Types, Page Elements, and Survey Options

SurveyMonkey
Question Types, Page Elements, and Survey Options

Start your survey from Home or Create survey from the header.

Once in the Design survey section, also called the full editor, select Build to add and edit questions and page elements in your survey. 

The Build menu shows our most-used question types, when selected. To see and choose from all question types or page elements, select View more. 

Once you see the full questions and page elements menu, hover over a question as we Show tooltips with an example to help you select the right question for your needs.
Click the toggle to disable the question tooltips from displaying. 

For more info on building your survey, check out adding questions and editing your survey.

Available Questions
Selection Questions
Question type	Description
Multiple choice	Let people choose a single answer from a list of answer choices.
Checkboxes	Let people choose multiple answers from a list of answer choices.
Dropdown	Answer choices display in a dropdown letting people select a single answer.
Tip! This question’s great when you have a long list of answer options.
Matrix of dropdown menus	People can evaluate several items (rows) against a consistent set of criteria (columns), displayed in a matrix of dropdowns.
Image choice	People can select one or more image answers from your image answer choices.
Rating Questions
Question type	Description
Star rating	People can evaluate a statement using a visual scale of stars, hearts, thumbs, or smilies.
Slider	People can drag an interactive slider to rate an item or statement on a numerical scale.
Ranking	People rank a list of options in the order they prefer using numeric dropdown menus or drag-and-drop.
Matrix / rating scale	People can evaluate one or more items (rows) using the same set of column choices. The matrix question can collect only a single answer or multiple answers per row. 

You have the option to turn the matrix question into a rating scale if you choose to assign weights to answer choices.
Best worst scale	People can select the best and worst option from a list of items to find out what respondents value.

Textbox Questions
Question type	Description
Comment box	People can respond with a longer, open-ended answer.
Single textbox	People can respond with a short text or numerical answer. 

Validate the question to specify an answer length, or require and validate a number value, date format, or email address.
Multiple textboxes	Collect multiple short text or numerical answers with a single question. 

Validate the question to specify an answer length, or require and validate a number value, date format, or email address.
Forms Questions
Question type	Description
Name	People can enter a First name, Last name, Middle name, Title, and Suffix from a single question.
Email address	People can enter an email address.
Phone	People can enter phone numbers and extensions.
Address	People can enter a street address, city/town, state/province, zip/postal code, or country.
Date / time	People can enter a specific date and/or time.
Other
Question type	Description
Net promoter® score	People can measure their satisfaction with your organization, brand, product, or service. 
SurveyMonkey calculates NPS score automatically in Analyze Results.
Click map	Get feedback about an image by asking people to click on a part of your image.
File upload	People can attach a file with their survey response.
Text A/B test	Learn how people react to two or more different messages. Enter the text variables you want to compare, then specify the percentage of respondents who should see each message.
Image A/B test	Learn how people react to two or more different images. Provide the images to compare, then specify the percentage of respondents who should see each image.
Use Pre-Written, Question Bank Questions

The Question bank tab offers a library of certified questions created by survey methodologists to minimize respondent bias. You can select questions from question bank.

Page Elements

In addition to question types, surveys have page elements which you can build with.

Page element	Description
Intro page	People can add an intro page at the beginning of your survey briefly explaining the topic and purpose of the survey. 

Tip! Your introduction only needs to be three or four sentences, or a couple of short paragraphs at most.
New page	People can add another blank survey page to the end of your survey.
Text	People can add Text to provide extra context or description to your respondents. 

Tip! To create a consent form, add terms and conditions to your survey, add footers, and more.
Image	Insert an image into your survey by uploading an image file from your computer.
Survey Options

The Options menu lets you adjust your survey experience and look by showing or hiding options.

Check the table below for details on survey options.

Option	Description
Accept Payments	Respondents can make payments via PayPal or Stripe to your survey or form. 
You can assign prices to a single question to charge different prices, or charge a fixed price for your entire form.

Quiz	Quiz mode turns any survey into a quiz. Your can tell respondents whether they got the answer right or simply record scores directly in Analyze results. Your results show overall quiz score statistics and individual scores for each person that took the quiz.
Survey title	Titles should tell people what your survey’s about. You can format the title text, choose the title’s placement on the survey, or add a nickname to organize your surveys within SurveyMonkey.
Progress bar	Progress bars at the bottom of each survey page tell respondents how much of the survey they've finished and how much they still need to complete.
Page titles and descriptions	Page titles and descriptions let you chunk your survey into sections or provide helpful instructions to your respondents.
Page numbers	
Page numbers can be shown or hidden. When shown, they’re by the Page title. 
Question numbers	Question numbers can be shown or hidden. Choose whether to number questions across the entire survey or restart numbering on each survey page.
Required asterisks	equired asterisks are a visual indicator to respondents that a question’s required. 
If you hide required asterisks, respondents see an error message if they try to submit the survey without answering required questions.
Language	Create your survey in 57 supported survey languages.
The default survey text—like navigation buttons and the survey end page—are translated automatically for you. You need to provide text for your survey title, questions, and answers. 
Your survey language is set by your account language, but you can update the language by survey.

Your Account

Your Account
Login & Password

Single Sign-On (SSO)

Single Sign-On (SSO) enables people on your team to use their corporate login credentials to log in to SurveyMonkey. Your organization can control who can access your SurveyMonkey team and create authentication policies for increased security.

Logging in to Your Account

Learn how to log in to SurveyMonkey, all about account verification, and how to troubleshoot login issues.

Your Login Details

Change your login details from My Account. Verify your email to make sure you can get account information from us.

Forgot Login Details

If you can't log in because you forgot your login details, try these troubleshooting steps to get back into your account.

SurveyMonkey Mobile Apps

Learn more about the three mobile apps SurveyMonkey has available for download.

Two-factor Authentication (2FA)

Get added security to your SurveyMonkey account by confirming your identity via mobile device at login.

Device Registration

Managing Your Account

Changing the Language on Your Account

You can easily switch the language you use when browsing SurveyMonkey in the footer. You can also save your language preference from the My Account page.

Contacting Support About an Account

If you need to contact support about an account, we're here to help! To keep your account and data secure, we may need to confirm account ownership or billing details before we send you account information.

Account Response Limits

Free plans have a response limit per survey. Monthly plans have an account-wide response limit per month, and you’ll be billed response overages or billable responses if you exceed the limit. For larger response limits, we recommend an annual plan.

How to Opt Out or Unsubscribe

You can manage the types of marketing emails you receive, the SurveyMonkey accounts that can send you survey invitations, emails you receive from SurveyMonkey Contribute, and the cookies we use.

Allow List Information for SurveyMonkey

If you're having trouble accessing SurveyMonkey or not receiving emails from us, we recommend adding our domains and IP addresses to your allow list (sometimes known as a whitelist).

Canceling or Deleting Your SurveyMonkey Account

To cancel a paid subscription, go to your Billing Details from My Account and cancel auto-renew. Or you can delete your account, if you don't want to keep it or your survey data any longer.

Trying Paid Features

When building your survey on the free plan, you have the chance to try some paid features before sending your survey. To keep the paid features, upgrade your account to send your survey or remove the features and send your survey on the free plan.

AI Features in SurveyMonkey

Learn how to manage access to AI features on your Teams or Enterprise plan.

Contact SurveyMonkey

How to Contact SurveyMonkey

Need to contact SurveyMonkey support? Learn how to reach customer support via live chat, phone, or email based on your account plan, and find immediate answers through the chatbot and Help Center.

Offline Mode

SurveyMonkey
Offline Mode

Enterprise Feature: If you're interested, contact sales. If you already have an Enterprise account, contact your Customer Success Manager.

Use offline mode and the SurveyMonkey Anywhere app to collect responses without an internet connection, then upload them back to SurveyMonkey once you have internet access.

Offline mode is not available for surveys that include Click Map, Name, Email Address, Phone, or Address questions, or that use Market Research solutions.

How It Works

Offline mode lets you collect survey responses in the SurveyMonkey Anywhere app when you don't have an internet connection.

✅ Create your survey in SurveyMonkey and share it with your team

✅ Create a Kiosk Survey Collector in SurveyMonkey

✅ Collect responses in the SurveyMonkey Anywhere app*

✅ Upload your responses from the app to SurveyMonkey

✅ Access your survey, collector, or analyze your results in SurveyMonkey

* Some offline mode functionality is only available to Power seats—learn about Enterprise Team Seats, Roles and Permissions

Creating a Survey

To collect responses using offline mode, first you'll need to create a new survey. If your survey uses any incompatible features, you’ll be prompted to remove them before moving forward.

To share the survey, you must be logged into an Enterprise account with offline mode turned on. You can then register your device slots with any Power seat who will be collecting responses. This lets them download the survey in the SurveyMonkey Anywhere app.

Tip! You can also share surveys with Casual seats or anyone outside of your team—they can only conduct the survey online.

Incompatible Features
Incompatible Question Types	Incompatible Survey Options
File Upload
A/B Test
Payments (Stripe)
Click Map	Block Randomization
Quotas
One Question at a Time
Question & Answer Piping
Advanced Piping
Turning on Offline Mode

To turn on offline mode, first you need to create a Kiosk Survey Collector and validate your survey to make sure it will work offline.

To create a Kiosk Survey collector:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Create a Kiosk Survey collector.
Click Validate the survey to turn on offline mode. If your survey uses any incompatible features, you’ll be prompted to remove them before moving forward.
Click Text a download link to send the SurveyMonkey Anywhere app download link to anyone on your team via a one-time text message, or copy and share the link.

Once offline mode is turned on, your survey is locked and you won’t be able to make edits to it. If you need to edit your survey, make a copy of the survey, edit the copy, and then create a new offline collector.

Using SurveyMonkey Anywhere

Once you're logged in to the SurveyMonkey Anywhere app, you can download a survey to use offline and collect responses without an internet connection, manage responses, then upload them back to SurveyMonkey once you have internet access.

Expand | Collapse
Collecting Responses

You need to be the survey owner, or the survey owner needs to share the survey with you, and your device needs to be connected to the internet to download the survey.

To download a survey:

Go to the My Surveys screen.
Select a survey and tap the down arrow to download it.

Once your survey is downloaded, you can disconnect from the internet and start collecting responses by tapping the title of the survey.

Managing Responses

You can view the Completion Status, Collector Name, Last Entry Date/Time and Time Spent for any collected responses, and edit or delete survey responses while disconnected from the internet.

To edit or delete a survey response:

Go to the My Surveys screen.
Tap the cloud icon with an arrow to see a list of survey responses.
Tap each response in the list to see the response details.
In the upper-right corner of the screen, tap the three vertical dots.

Tap Edit to reopen the survey and edit responses, or tap Delete to remove the response from your device.

Uploading Responses

Your device needs to be connected to the internet to upload the survey responses you collected in offline mode.

To upload responses to SurveyMonkey:

Go to the My Surveys screen.
Tap the speech bubble with a check mark next to the survey you want to upload responses from.
In the bottom-right corner, tap the cloud icon with an arrow and choose to upload All responses or Complete responses only.
Tap Upload.

When you upload responses, they're permanently deleted from the device and moved into the Analyze section of your survey in SurveyMonkey.

You can continue to collect more responses, or tap X to remove the survey from your device.

Turning Off Offline Mode

To turn off offline mode, you’ll need to close any open Kiosk Survey collectors.

To close a collector:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Click the three dots (...) next to an open Kiosk Survey collector and select Close collector.
Choose Flag to Close or Close Now.
Click Confirm.

When you select Flag to Close, everyone who downloaded the survey to the SurveyMonkey Anywhere app is prompted to upload their responses to SurveyMonkey. Once all responses are uploaded, the collector closes automatically.

When you select Close Now, your collector will be closed immediately and anyone answering the survey in the app may be interrupted and unable to complete their response. Any responses that haven’t already been uploaded to SurveyMonkey are permanently deleted.

Device Management
Connected Devices

Once offline mode is turned on, you can see the number of devices that have downloaded the survey for offline collection on the collector page. Clicking View All next to the number of devices will show you:

The device name
The account holder's email address
The date the survey was downloaded to the device
Removing Devices

From the Offline Devices page in the My Teams dropdown, Primary Admins and Admins can see all available device slots and a list of enabled devices across all surveys. To remove an offline-enabled device and free up a device slot, click - next to the device.

Buying Responses with SurveyMonkey Audience

SurveyMonkey
Buying Responses with SurveyMonkey Audience
How It Works

If you don’t have your own list of respondents to get the feedback you need, you can buy responses through SurveyMonkey Audience using the Target audience collector.

1. Create your survey following our design guidelines

2. Choose your audience and buy responses

3. Watch the responses roll in and analyze your results

Plan Requirements

You can buy responses in countries where we offer SurveyMonkey or LaunchPad, but accounts in certain billing countries can't buy SurveyMonkey Audience due to technical limitations.

SurveyMonkey Audience isn't available if your data is stored in our European Data Center. You can see if this applies to you by checking your Account Details.

SurveyMonkey Audience orders are one-time purchases that you can make regardless of a subscription or plan. It's an add-on cost to your SurveyMonkey plan or LaunchPad access, and you don't need to upgrade your plan to use SurveyMonkey Audience.

SurveyMonkey

If you have the free (Basic) SurveyMonkey plan and buy responses using SurveyMonkey Audience, you get access to premium features from our paid plans. These premium features are only available on surveys you launch with Audience—if you want to use the features on additional surveys, you need to upgrade your plan. When you are on a paid SurveyMonkey plan, you will have access to the paid features of that plan.

Premium features available with SurveyMonkey Audience
Design Features	Analyze Features
Add up to 80 questions	View unlimited responses

Remove the survey footer	Exports (PDF, PPT, XLS, CSV, and SPSS)
Question skip logic	Create unlimited rules
Page skip logic	Word cloud
Question randomization	Tag responses
A/B test question types	Password protect Shared Data Pages and Results Dashboards
Matrix/Rating Scale Questions	Print survey PDFs
Advanced piping	Crosstab reports
Advanced branching	
Block randomization	
Custom variables	
Carry forward responses	
Multilingual surveys	
Custom and Premium themes	
Hide the survey title	
Add a logo	

LaunchPad

The LaunchPad access fee gives LaunchPad customers access to SurveyMonkey Audience.

Who's Taking Your Survey

Our respondent panels are representative of a diverse online population that voluntarily joined a program to take surveys.

When you choose the United States as your country, you're buying responses from our Contribute or Rewards panel. When you choose a country other than the United States, you're buying responses from our global panel.

Expand | Collapse
Contribute and Rewards Panels

SurveyMonkey Contribute panelists take surveys for charity and a chance to win a sweepstakes prize.

Rewards panelists earn credits for completing surveys which they can redeem for gift cards or donate to charity.

All panelists share demographic info about themselves like gender, age, and region, and other targeting attributes you might be interested in, like cell phone usage or job type.

We balance Contribute and Rewards panels according to census data of age and gender.

Global Panel

Global panelists are managed by our trusted partners—this means respondent quality and activity must meet a satisfactory level, otherwise panelists are removed from the program.

While our global panel doesn't automatically balance according to age or gender, you can target specific regions within countries and choose the distribution of responses you want from each region, age-range, and gender you select.

TIP! Choose your global audience from any of these supported countries.

Designing Your Survey

Use LaunchPad, SurveyMonkey's pre-built survey frameworks designed with expert methodologies that handle everything from survey logic to analysis, enabling you to quickly validate concepts and launch standout products and campaigns.

Or you can create a custom survey in SurveyMonkey.

Wherever you design your market research solutions survey, be sure to follow our SurveyMonkey Audience design guidelines to make sure your study's a success.

Demographic Information

Your survey results automatically include each respondent's age-range, gender, and type of device used to take the survey. Plus, if you purchased Contribute or Rewards responses, we also include each respondents annual household income and region.

If you want additional demographic info, include questions in your survey to gather this info. You can add pre-written questions from the Demographics category in our Question bank.

Editing a Live Survey

Editing the survey design after you buy responses can cause confuse respondents, create issues in your survey results, and may cause your order to pause. When a live survey is edited, people taking the survey looped back to the start of the survey, and their results may not match the results of your original survey.

Survey Language

Your survey should be in English if you're buying responses from our Contribute and Rewards panel.

If you're buying a global panel, your survey should be in a supported language for the country you're targeting. For example, if you're targeting an audience in Belgium, your survey needs to be in Dutch or French. Here are some tips for creating multilingual surveys.

Buying Responses

If you're part of an Enterprise team, you may use Budgets to manage Audience credits.

How to Buy Responses

To buy responses:

After you create your survey, go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Choose Buy responses.
Select your target audience by choosing Country, Gender, Age, and Income.
Click More targeting options to browse and choose from hundreds of other targeting options.
Choose How many complete responses do you need.
In the Optional settings section, toggle on any options you’d like to use with your study. These settings can improve your targeting and streamline your audience for better results.
You can use any of the following options:
Custom screening questions
Schedule for later
Exclusions
Review Your Estimate. If there aren’t enough panelists for your order, try reducing the number of responses you need or broadening your targeting options.
Click Checkout. You can pay with a credit or debit card, or Audience credits.

Once you complete your payment, we email a standard survey invitation to a random group of respondents who match your targeting options. It's not possible to customize the invitation email and you can't edit your order or change your targeting options after purchase.

Getting More Responses

To target different demographics or get additional responses, you can create multiple Target Audience collectors. Also, you can send your survey to your own list of respondents using other collector types, like a Web link or Email invitation.

If you want to launch multiple projects at the same time, you can create additional Target Audience collectors by selecting +Add Audience at the top right corner of the page. When you proceed to purchase and launch your projects, these collectors will be automatically grouped, resulting in a single invoice.

Excluding Duplicate Panelists

Exclude any panelists who have taken surveys you've launched in the past 100 days on our Contribute and Rewards panel. Simply create a new Target Audience collector for the same survey to apply the exclusions. 

To prevent previous respondents from taking your current survey, toggle on the Exclusions option and select the surveys that you need excluded on the Audience calculator page.

Pricing

The total cost of your order is broken down in Your Estimate on the right side of your Target Audience collector. Your Estimate includes the number of complete responses you need multiplied by the price per response.

Price per response depends on:

Survey length—longer surveys cost more per response since the number of questions directly correlates to length of time it takes to complete a survey and how many people complete it.
Targeting options—cost for each option may increase based on how common the criteria is among our panelists.
Custom balancing
Qualification rate

Any applicable taxes will be added on the checkout page.

Get a Quote View all our targeting options and get an estimated quote for buying responses on the Audience preview page.

Your Survey Results

After you purchase is completed, you can monitor the status of your order, see how many responses you have, and view your estimated completion date in the Target Audience Collector in the Publish survey section of your survey.

To view your responses, go to the Analyze Results section of your survey. There are lots of ways to analyze your data:

View your survey responses
Create rules to break down your results
View and categorize open-ended responses
Download or share your results

When reviewing data from your Audience survey, contact us before deleting responses. We can replace responses that we confirm are low quality.

Expand | Collapse
Filtering by Demographic or Collector

You can create rules to break down your results by demographic info or collector.

We include demographic info as questions at the end of your survey results—filter your results by question to compare your results by demographic.

Or, if you created multiple Target Audience collectors for a single survey, you can filter your results by collector.

Response Status

In the Individual responses tab of your survey results, you'll find each person's response status.

Status	Description	How you're charged
Complete (Finished)	Respondents who answered all required questions they saw, reached the end of the survey, and clicked the Done button. A respondents with a complete response may have skipped required questions due to logic or skipped questions that weren't required.	You're charged for the number of complete responses you ordered. Occasionally, you may collect more responses than you requested—we give you those extra responses for free.

Disqualified	Respondents who answered all required questions they saw but were disqualified by logic in the survey design. Disqualified responses don't count towards the total number of complete responses you ordered, but they do count towards the number of respondents we send the survey to (based on your qualification rate) and they appear in your survey results.
	You're not charged separately for disqualified responses. When you use disqualification logic, you select a qualification rate, which affects the price per response.
Incomplete (Unfinished)	Respondents who started the survey but abandoned or left the survey on their own before completing it. Incomplete responses don't count towards the total number of complete responses you ordered, but these responses still appear in your survey results.
	You're not charged for incomplete responses.
Paused Orders

We automatically pause orders that have a higher than average abandon rate or language disparity. High abandon rate (or low response rate) means many respondents exit or leave your survey after starting it. If your order is paused, an Audience specialist will email the account email address with survey recommendations and give you an opportunity to make changes so you can improve your data quality.

Your order may be paused if a survey is doesn't follow our design guidelines or if you edit a live survey. Complicated Matrix questions, long or unclear introductions, and consent statements can cause respondents to abandon a survey. Respondents may also abandon your survey if they feel it isn't relevant to them, so it's important you're targeting the right people.

We can't reactivate an order if it's paused a second time. This is to ensure that you're receiving quality data and that our respondents continue to receive surveys that are relevant to them.

Response Quality

Response quality automation uses machine learning to scan your survey results, flag poor-quality responses, and delete and replace the flagged responses with new complete responses.

Benchmarks

Benchmarks

SurveyMonkey
Benchmarks

Paid Feature: Benchmarks are available on Advantage plans and higher. 

Benchmarks add context to your survey results by comparing your responses with others who asked the same Question Bank questions. Your survey results include benchmarks for the Question Bank questions you’ve used which have available benchmark data. 

We’re also working to continuously improve the benchmarks experience, which may be available for additional survey questions in the future.

Benchmark Data

Benchmark data comes from SurveyMonkey customers who use benchmark questions in their surveys. To calculate a benchmark, we aggregate the responses across surveys for each benchmarkable question, then average those responses to generate the question’s score.

To preserve privacy, responses for a given question are aggregated and de-identified to create a set of average statistics about that question—we don't disclose any individual responses, personal information, or organization names.

Check out our Privacy Notice for more on how SurveyMonkey handles your personal information and data.

Opting Out of Benchmarks

Opting out of benchmarks excludes your account’s survey responses from benchmark calculations. You’re able to opt out of benchmarks if your account is either:

An Enterprise account with HIPAA or ESDP features enabled
Previously opted out of benchmarks 

If you’re an Enterprise customer and have questions around opting in or out of benchmarks, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

If you’ve previously opted out of benchmarks, you can also use the steps below to opt in to including your responses in future benchmarks.

To opt out of benchmarks:

Log in and go to My Account.
Scroll to the Data Features section.
Select Edit next to Access to Benchmarks.
Select Off.
If you’d like to opt in to using benchmarks instead, select On.
Select Save.

If your responses are currently included, they’ll be removed when benchmark data next refreshes after you opt out. Opting out of contributing your survey responses to benchmark data will also remove your ability to view benchmarks when analyzing survey results.

Using Benchmarkable Questions

You can include benchmarkable questions in your survey by using our Question Bank, or with specific survey templates.

The benchmark icon indicates when a Question Bank question or template is benchmarkable.
Using Question Bank

Our Question Bank contains hundreds of questions created and certified by survey methodologists. 

To see the Question Bank questions with benchmarks available:

Go to the Design Survey section of your survey.
Select Question Bank.
Browse the available questions with the benchmark icon and add it to your survey.

Certain questions from our Question Bank will let you customize text using a dropdown menu. However, editing the question text outside the dropdown can invalidate the benchmark comparison, since respondents might interpret your question differently than the original version.

If you make additional changes to the question type, or the number of answer options for a benchmarkable question, it will remove the option to view that question’s benchmark in Analyze results.

Using Survey Templates

To see the expert templates with benchmarks available:

Select Create survey.
Select Pick a popular template.
Browse the available templates with the Benchmark icon. You can also check the Benchmarks checkbox to filter for Benchmarkable templates.

You don't need to use every question in the expert template, but the more benchmarkable questions you include, the more comparison data you'll see in your results. Some templates may have additional questions that aren't benchmarkable. Feel free to add, edit, or delete questions to customize and style your survey.

Viewing Benchmarks in Survey Results

You can see benchmarks in Analyze Results for any surveys with benchmarkable questions, once your survey has gathered at least one response.

If you use an NPS question in your survey, you’ll automatically see the global benchmark score below your summary data chart. You can use the Benchmarks toggle from the question settings to hide or show benchmarks.

For other benchmark question types, you can select the benchmark icon at the top of the question window to show the available benchmark alongside your survey results.

There are some limitations to keep in mind when using benchmarks with the following analyze features:

Exports — Benchmark data and charts aren’t included in exports of your survey results, results dashboards, or shared data pages.
Add a Filter or Compare rule — Your survey data is impacted by applied rules, but the benchmark data is not.
Save a View — If you save a View with benchmarks turned on, benchmark visibility is not saved as part of the view settings. You can show or hide benchmarks for each question independently when working in your saved view. Filter or Show rules applied are saved as normal.
Shared Surveys

Anyone with shared access to your survey can view benchmarks in Analyze. When you show or hide benchmarks for a question, those changes apply to everyone with access to the survey.

Image Choice Question

SurveyMonkey
Image Choice Question

Image Choice is a simple, closed-ended question type that lets people select one or more image answers from a defined list of image choices. SurveyMonkey auto-formats your uploaded images into consistent boxes with a maximum height of 170px (or maximum width of 225px).

Video Overview
Creating an Image Choice Question

Steps to add the question to your survey:

Go to the Design survey section.
From the Build section, choose Image Choice.
Enter the question text.
In the answer fields, either upload your images or enter the URLs of images from the web. You can add up to 10 images per question.
Set up any additional options and settings:
You can add image captions that will be visible to survey takers.
To make your image accessible for survey takers using a screen reader, check the box to include descriptive text for image.
Click the Options or Logic tabs for more customization options.
Click Save.

Before you send your survey, preview your survey design to see what your survey will look like to people taking it.

Question Options and Settings

Under the Edit, Options, and Logic tabs, you can further customize the question in the following ways:

Allow more than one answer to this question (use checkboxes)
Score the Question (Enable Quiz Mode)
Require an Answer
Require a specific number, range, or limit of choices
Randomize, Sort, or Flip Choices
Add Question Skip Logic
Check the box to Add a "None of the above" Answer Option so people can answer the question without choosing an image. If you allow people to select more than one image and they click None of the above, they won't be able to select any images.

Learn more: Adding & Editing Questions

What Survey Takers See

Survey takers will see the images and captions with the survey question. By default people can choose one answer, but you can check the box to Allow more than one answer to this question (use checkboxes) to allow people to select more than one.

Analyzing and Sharing Data

Image Choice questions are easy to analyze since they are closed-ended. You can create Filter and Compare rules to break down your survey results, and every chart type is available for this question.

Images don't display in the Analyze results page. Instead, if you added captions to the images, you’ll see those displayed in the chart. Otherwise, answer choices will be labeled with a number based on the order they appear in the survey. For example, the first image will be labeled Image 1, and the second image will be labeled Image 2.

Exporting & Sharing Data

All export types are available for Image Choice questions.

If you want to share your results with others, you can share your exports or create a Shared Data page. Learn more about our sharing options: Sharing Survey Results.

Thematic Analysis

SurveyMonkey
Thematic Analysis

Paid Feature: Thematic analysis is available for English surveys on some paid plans and in the US and EU data centers.

Thematic analysis summarizes and groups your survey’s text responses into key themes, allowing you to:

Save time by organizing data into meaningful categories. 
Understand the most common themes across your open-ended responses.
View a summary of your open-ended responses to understand your results faster.
Feature Availability and Settings
Survey Requirements

Thematic analysis is available for surveys that meet the following requirements:

Thematic analysis works with text responses from the Comment box and Single textbox questions.
The survey is in English.
Your survey has between 1 and 10,000 responses. Filtering your dataset to display between 1–10,000 responses doesn’t change the survey's total response limit.
Limitations
Certain survey use cases are not permitted—for details, please see SurveyMonkey's Acceptable Uses Policy, as well as additional third-party provider usage policies.
Thematic analysis isn't available if your data is stored in the Canadian data center.
How Your Data is Processed

Thematic analysis uses a combination of a self-hosted Anthropic model and an Azure OpenAI or OpenAI model to summarize and analyze your survey. Your data is not used to train any of these providers' AI models. Learn more about how this feature processes your data.

Using Thematic Analysis

To turn on Thematic Analysis for your entire survey:

Go to Analyze results.
Select Options from the top toolbar.
From the menu, select Data Options. 
Toggle Thematic analysis.

You can also enable Thematic analysis from the Summary tab of any Comment box or Single-textbox question that has responses.

Once the analysis is complete, the Summary view shows a high-level overview. You can review the themes applied to your responses in the Responses view.

If a response doesn't have enough detail to categorize, we label it as No applied theme*.

You can also use Sentiments to better understand your respondents’ feelings while responding to your survey.

Regenerating Themes

If you collect additional responses, generate themes again to apply them to your new responses and update the summary.

You’ll see this option when you collect new responses to a question. To regenerate, select Refresh in the question tile.

Filtering Responses

Once we generate themes, you can view your open-ended responses and filter them by theme.

Exporting Responses with Themes

To export responses with themes included:

Go to Analyze results.
Select Export from the top toolbar, and select + New export.
Select Question summaries.
Choose XLS or CSV, and select Open-ended responses.
Select Export. When your download is ready, a notification to Download briefly displays to export the file to your computer. You can also find your files for 14 days by selecting Export and choosing Previous exports.

To export an individual question with themes included:

Go to Analyze results.
Find a question that uses Thematic analysis.
Select the Export icon at the top of the tile.
Select XLS, or select More options to select CSV file format.
Select Export. When your download is ready, a notification to Download briefly displays to export the file to your computer. You can also find your files for 14 days by selecting Export and choosing Previous exports.

The export includes the following data:

Respondent ID
Response date
Response text
Tags applied
Themes applied
Response sentiment (if Sentiment analysis is on)

Kiosk Mode

SurveyMonkey
Kiosk Mode

PAID FEATURE: Kiosk mode is available on paid plans on the US, EU, and CA data centers — see what's on your plan.

You can use kiosk mode on the SurveyMonkey Anywhere app to turn your device into a survey-taking station.

Using Kiosk Mode

Kiosk mode runs your survey in a loop—so each time someone finishes a survey, a new survey is ready for the next person to take. When a survey-taker completes a survey, they'll be prompted to Return to Start or Close Kiosk Mode.

The completion of a survey is what causes it to loop, so if you have a Survey End Page, Custom Thank You, Instant Results or Quiz Results enabled, you won't be able to see them when using kiosk mode. Click Map, Name, Email Address, Phone, or Address questions and Market Research solutions surveys are not compatible with kiosk mode.

To use kiosk mode:

Log in to your SurveyMonkey account.
Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Create a Kiosk Survey collector.
Download the SurveyMonkey Anywhere app and sign in.
On the My Surveys page, tap on a survey title to open it.
(optional) Enable offline mode to collect responses without an internet connection.
Collect responses in the app. Responses will automatically sync with your SurveyMonkey account.

To exit kiosk mode, tap the back button or ❌ in the upper-left corner of the survey.

Kiosk Settings

Inactivity Timer

Paid feature

In the SurveyMonkey Anywhere app, tap My Account. You can enable the following kiosk mode settings:

Inactivity Timer: Set an inactivity timer to loop the survey back to the beginning if the survey remains inactive for the set amount of time.
Passcode Lock: Set a passcode to prevent survey-takers from exiting the survey-taking experience. To exit the survey, you need to enter the 4-digit passcode.
Kiosk Mode in the SurveyMonkey App

We're going to be removing Kiosk Mode from the SurveyMonkey app soon. To use the new kiosk mode features, download the SurveyMonkey Anywhere app!

Using Kiosk Mode in the SurveyMonkey App

Kiosk Mode runs your survey in a loop, returning to the beginning of the survey each time a response is collected. In order to run a survey using Kiosk Mode, the survey needs to be set to Allow Multiple Responses.

To run a survey in Kiosk Mode using the SurveyMonkey app:

In the SurveyMonkey app, select the survey you want respondents to take from My Surveys.
Tap Send.
Tap Kiosk Mode.
Select whether you want to enable screen lock. With screen lock on, your SurveyMonkey password needs to be entered into the device to exit Kiosk Mode.
If the survey doesn't already have Allow Multiple Responses setting turned on, allow this setting when prompted.

To exit Kiosk Mode:

Tap the back button or Exit in the top corner of your survey.
Tap Close Kiosk Mode. If you have screen lock on, you’ll be prompted to enter your SurveyMonkey password.

Paste Your Content to Create a Survey

SurveyMonkey
Paste Your Content to Create a Survey

If you drafted your survey in a document and now need to program or import a pre-written survey into SurveyMonkey, you can paste your content all at once, instead of adding each question one by one.

To import a Google Form into a SurveyMonkey survey, use the SurveyMonkey for Google Forms add-on.

Create a Survey with Paste Your Content

You may need to reformat your document to recognize and properly create the Single textbox and Multiple choice questions. After adding questions this way, you can always edit and customize the output survey.

To create a survey via Paste your content:

Click Create survey.
Select Paste your content.
On the Import Questions screen,  copy and paste your Multiple choice or Single textbox questions and answer choices. Each question and answer choice needs to be on their own line.
Press Enter or Return on your keyboard twice to separate your questions. Each question must be separated by a blank line.
In the Preview section, view the questions you add in real time.
Once you have entered your questions, click Add Questions to create your survey.

Once the survey is drafted, you can give the survey a title, add different question types, edit or switch the question type, change the survey theme, add rich text formatting, and more.

Paste Content using AI

If you have your survey questions and answers already written outside of SurveyMonkey, simply Copy and paste your survey into SurveyMonkey and let AI do the rest.

Paste your content is powered by OpenAI/Azure OpenAI. We use machine learning and generative AI to convert your content into a survey to recognize the various survey elements within your document, of any format, and convert it into a survey.

To paste your survey content into SurveyMonkey:

Click Create survey. 
Select Paste your content as your starting point and click Create survey. 
To agree to use AI to create your survey, click Use AI. 
Copy your survey from your document and paste it into SurveyMonkey. Click Create survey.

Once your survey is created, be sure to review your survey. The import may result in inaccuracies and there may be limitations impacting the import. Review your survey design for accuracy, adjust any question types, add logic, or style your survey.

If you’re on the Basic (free) plan and your survey contains paid features, you’ll either need to upgrade to a paid plan or remove the paid features in order to send your survey.

Enabling Paste Your Content

When you choose Paste your content as your creation method, you need to select Use AI to utilize this feature. 

Paste your content will stay enabled and available to you until you clear your browser data. If you use a different device to access your survey, you will need to choose to Use AI from that device too to use Paste your content.

Limitations

At this time, any text formatting, titles or page descriptions, style elements, images or videos, page breaks, logic, and unsupported question types won’t be captured from your document and won't be imported. 

Your survey is created with the following question types: Multiple choice, Checkbox, Single Textbox, Comment box, Matrix/Rating scale, and Text.

A customer can paste and submit your survey up to 50 times per month.

Also, please don’t paste any sensitive information, like names, into SurveyMonkey. 

Usage is subject to SurveyMonkey's Acceptable Uses Policy, as well as additional third-party provider usage policies, and acceptable use and conduct policies.

Errors

If something goes wrong in converting your survey text to a survey, you’ll see an error message to provide you with info about what happened and what you can do.

How We Use Your Data

When Paste your content is enabled and used, your data is processed in the following ways: 

We use machine learning and generative AI to identify survey elements, format, and generate a survey from your pasted content within SurveyMonkey. 
We send the survey text you provide and an encrypted user ID to OpenAI or Azure OpenAI service to extract the survey structure, questions, text, comments, etc. and provide the feature.

Analyzing Results
Understanding Your Results

How to Analyze Results

SurveyMonkey
How to Analyze Results

You can view and analyze your results at any time during the collection process in the Analyze section of the survey. Here you can see a summary view of your data; browse individual responses; create and export dynamic charts; use filter, compare, and show rules to analyze specific data views and segments; view and categorize open-ended responses, and easily download your results in multiple formats.

Viewing Responses

You can view summaries of each survey question, or browse through individual survey responses.

Expand | Collapse
Question Summaries

We're updating the look and feel of your charts, so you may notice some differences over time. We appreciate your patience as we improve SurveyMonkey!

Viewing Question summaries, the default Analyze view, gives you quick insight into the overall results of your survey. For close-ended questions, dynamic charts are generated automatically for visual analysis.

Question summaries only shows responses from the first 10 pages of your survey. If you have more than 10 pages, export your responses to view all results.

Individual Responses

Viewing Individual responses is useful if you'd like to view each respondent's complete set of answers to your survey. You can view all responses in a table or scroll through each response one by one. Additionally, each Individual response includes respondent metadata, giving you more insight into:

Who submitted the response (if you tracked responses)
The collector through which the response was submitted
The start and end date and time
The time spent entering a response
Response completeness
The IP address of the respondent

To browse Individual responses, select the Individual responses tab toward the top of the Analyze page. Scroll through the table to view your responses. Or, switch to Single view, then use the left and right arrows to navigate through each response.

Learn more: Viewing Individual Responses

Open-ended Responses

You can view Open-ended responses under the Question summaries tab and under the Individual Responses tab. When you view an open-ended question in the Question summaries area, you may need to select the Responses link to view all responses.

With some paid plans, you can use the text analysis features to identify and tag recurring words or themes in your responses.

Learn More: Viewing a Specific Comment in the Analysis

Multi-survey Analysis

Compare results from multiple surveys in one dashboard. Create charts, filter results, and track changes over time. Or, compare results from different groups of respondents.

Learn more: Analyze Multiple Surveys Together

Using Rules to Analyze Data

After viewing the overall Question summaries, you can create rules to answer more specific questions about your data. Filter, Compare, and Show rules allow you to focus in on specific subsets of your data, so you can analyze your results in a way that's most meaningful to you.

Paid users may create an unlimited number of rules. Free users may create one rule.

Expand | Collapse
Filter Rules

Use filter rules to focus on a specific subset of your data based on certain criteria that you define. When a filter is applied, only results that meet that criteria will show in the filtered view. Filters carry over to both the Question summaries and Individual responses tabs.

For example, if you only want to view responses submitted within a certain time frame, create a Filter by Time Period. If you only want to see responses from Females who submitted responses within that time frame, create a Filter by Question and Answer and apply both filters at once.

You can filter your results by:

Question & Answer
Collector
Completeness
Time Period
Respondent Metadata

To create a Filter rule, select Rules, then select +Filter in the left sidebar.

Learn More: Filter Rules

Compare Rules

Compare rules allow you to cross-tabulate your data to compare the answer choices to one question across the rest of the survey. In statistical terms, it is a joint distribution between two (or more) discrete variables such as product usage and demographics.

For example, if you included a survey question asking respondents to select their gender, you can create a Compare rule to cross-tabulate and compare the survey results from each gender side by side.

To create a Compare rule, click Rules, then select +Compare in the left sidebar.

Learn More: Compare Rules

Show Rules

You can use Show rules to display only certain survey questions or pages in the result summary. If you're only interested in analyzing certain questions or pages in your survey at a time, creating a Show rule will help you focus on those parts of the survey without the clutter of the rest of your survey.

For example, if you used skip logic in your survey to direct certain respondents to different questions based on their answers to previous questions, you can create a Show rule that contains only the questions included in that logic path for easier analysis.

To create a Show rule, select Rules, then click +Show in the left sidebar.

Learn More: Show Rules

Using Saved Views

A View is a snapshot of your data made up of any Filter, Compare, or Show rules that you apply to the survey results. With any paid plan, you can save views so that you can easily toggle back and forth between different views of your data at any time, without having to constantly recreate them.

Learn More: Views

Exports

With any paid plan, you can download your results in a variety of formats. You can keep an offline copy of your survey results, send the exports to others, download individual responses for printing, or export your raw data for further analysis.

Exports are available on paid plans.

Expand | Collapse
Question Summaries

Question summaries exports contain the response percentages, response counts, and open-ended responses (optional). The PDF, PPT, Excel (XLS), and CSV exports also include presentation-ready graphs and charts.

To export Question summaries, select Export in the upper right corner of the Analyze page, select + New export, and then select Question summaries.

Learn more: Exports

Individual Responses

Exporting Individual responses produces an Excel (XLS), CSV, SPSS, or PDF document that contains each respondent's full answer set, as well as respondent metadata. You can also export one single response under the Individual responses tab in the Analyze section.

To export Individual Responses, select the Export button in the upper right corner of the Analyze page, select + New export, and then select Individual responses.

Learn more: Exports

Exporting Charts

Under the Question summaries tab (the default view), charts are generated for each close-ended or numerical text boxes question in the survey.

To export a chart:

Select Export in the upper right corner of the question.
Choose PNG (chart only)

Learn more: Exports

Managing Your Account

How to Opt Out or Unsubscribe

SurveyMonkey
How to Opt Out or Unsubscribe

You can manage the types of marketing emails you receive, the SurveyMonkey accounts that can send you survey invitations, emails you receive from SurveyMonkey Contribute, and the cookies we use.

These email communications may include monthly newsletters, best practices, data stories and quizzes, product updates, product research and feedback.

Emails and Newsletters

We like sharing how you can get the most out of SurveyMonkey by emailing you about cool new features, interesting customer stories, and advice from expert survey methodologists—and you can easily manage the types of emails we send.

To manage your email and newsletter preferences:

Click Unsubscribe at the bottom of an email. If you have an account, you can also sign in and go to My Account, then scroll down to Emails and Newsletters.
Choose the types of emails you’d like to receive or unsubscribe from.
Click Update Preferences to ensure the changes are applied. It may take up to 48 hours for the changes to go into effect.

If you have a SurveyMonkey account, we’ll continue to send you account-related emails. While you can manage some emails like daily summary notifications, you will continue to receive other emails related to your account, like billing reminders, cancellation notices, and requests or invitations to access or comment on your surveys. These are service linked communications which you cannot opt out from if you wish to continue using our service.

Survey Invitations

SurveyMonkey account holders can create and send surveys to email addresses or phone numbers they add to an Email Invitation or Text Message. Each invitation includes the option to opt out or unsubscribe from receiving further invitations.

Email Invitations
Click the opt out link in the invitation to unsubscribe from future emails sent by that specific SurveyMonkey account. This doesn’t opt you out from all email invitations originating from SurveyMonkey services.
If you have questions or concerns about being on a sender's email list, reply to your email invitation to reach out to the sender directly.
If you want to start receiving email invitations from all users, opt back in. This is a global setting—it's not possible to opt in to a specific account.
Text Messages
Text messages include instructions to reply STOP to unsubscribe from text invitations from all SurveyMonkey users.
If you want to start receiving text invitations, reply START to the text message you unsubscribed from to opt back in. This is a global setting—it's not possible to opt in to a specific account.


TIP! If you're concerned a message you received through SurveyMonkey may be spam, please review our Acceptable Uses Policy to report a complaint.

SurveyMonkey Contribute

If you receive emails from SurveyMonkey Contribute asking you to take surveys, you can choose to unsubscribe. Once you unsubscribe, you won’t get email invitations to take surveys, but you can still log in to Contribute to take surveys.

To unsubscribe from Contribute emails:

Log in to your SurveyMonkey Contribute account.
Click My Account in the upper right corner.
Click Update notification settings.
Click Unsubscribe from email invites.
Complete the form and click Submit.
Cookies

Our Cookies Notice and Privacy Notice outline how we use cookies. Some cookies are used to make our site work. Others are used to help personalize content, tailor and measure our marketing, and improve your user experience.

If you’re in North America, you’ll see a pop-up when you visit one of our webpages that asks you to agree to our use of certain cookies. To opt out of advertising cookies, click Cookies Preferences. You can update your preferences at any time by finding the “Do not sell my personal information" in the footer of our website, or by clearing your cookies in your browser settings, which will re-trigger the pop-up.

If you’re in European Union (EU) or United Kingdom (UK), you’ll see a pop-up when you visit one of our webpages that asks you to agree to our use of certain cookies. You can consent to or reject functional or advertising cookies. It's not possible to opt out of required cookies because they perform essential functions to communicate our site and deliver our service. Update your preferences at any time by finding the “Cookie Preferences" link in the footer of our website, or by clearing your cookies in your browser settings, which will re-trigger the pop-up.

If you’re outside of the EU, UK, or North America, you can clear and manage cookies in your browser settings at any time. If you clear all types of cookies, it might affect how certain features work. Enabling cookies ensures a smoother experience when you use our site, and SurveyMonkey won't function properly if all cookies are disabled.

Quizzes

SurveyMonkey
Quizzes

Turn any survey into a quiz by adding quiz questions! When people answer a quiz question, you can tell them whether they got the answer right, or keep their scores to yourself. When you analyze your results, you'll get overall score statistics, and individual scores for each person that took the quiz.

Creating a Quiz
Add a Quiz Question

You can make any survey into a quiz by adding at least one quiz question to your survey.

TIP! When you create a new survey from scratch and choose the Quiz category, any new Multiple Choice, Checkbox, Image Choice, or Dropdown questions you add will have scoring turned on by default.

To add a quiz question:

Create a Multiple Choice, Checkbox, Image Choice, or Dropdown question and add the question text and answer choices you need. All other question types aren’t compatible with Quizzes.
Select Score this question (enable quiz mode)—this makes it into a quiz question with scoring.
Define which answers are correct by clicking the empty checkmark icon to the left of an answer choice. The checkmark icon fills in to indicate that it's the correct answer. You can choose more than one correct answer.
Adjust the point value of any correct answer choice by clicking the up and down arrows next to the point value.
Click Save.

If your survey has quiz questions, avoid using logic, as it's not compatible with Display Quiz Results. Quiz scores are calculated using the total points in the survey. With skip logic, some people might skip over some questions in the survey which can result in their scores being lower because they didn’t answer all quiz questions.

Scoring Checkbox Questions

If your Checkbox or Image Choice quiz question uses checkboxes to allow more than one answer, you should require people to select a specific number of answer choices.

Otherwise, since points aren't deducted for incorrect answers, even if someone selects a wrong answer in addition to the correct ones, they'd still get the full points for the question—which might lead to a confusing final score.

For example, if there are two correct answers to the question, you should require that respondents select exactly 2 choices.

TIP! In the question text, make sure to tell people how many answer choices they should select.

Add Custom Feedback to a Quiz Question

You can display different feedback to people based on whether their answer is correct, incorrect, or partially correct on the Quiz Results Page. For example, if someone gets a question right, you can tell them “Good job, friend.” If they get it wrong, you can say "Better luck next time" or tell them the right answer.

To add custom feedback to a quiz question:

Click a quiz question to edit it.
Click the Options tab.
Click Add Custom Feedback to Question.
Enter feedback for each outcome.
Assigning Points

You can assign points to answer choices when quiz mode is enabled for a question. The typical point value for a correct answer is 1, but you can assign more than 1 point to any answer choice. It’s not possible to assign negative points to an answer choice.

The points people earn for each question are added up into a total score when they finish the quiz. It's not possible to view or group scores by page or section.

TIP! It's possible to adjust points assigned to quiz questions even after responses are collected. Any changes to point values will be reflected in the existing scores on the Analyze page.

Max Score

When you're editing a quiz question, you can see the maximum number of points someone can earn for that question.

For Dropdown or Multiple Choice questions (where only one answer is allowed), the max score is equal to the highest point value assigned to an answer choice in the question.
For Multiple Choice questions using checkboxes (where respondents can choose more than one answer), the max score is equal to total point value across all answer choices (regardless of whether you require a limit or range of answer choices).

When someone gets the max score for a question, the question is considered correct in the question summary and in their individual response in the results.

Partial Credit

You can set up your quiz so that people can get partial credit for choosing certain answers. For example, you can assign 2 points to the best answer, and 1 point to the answer choice you want to give partial credit for. If the respondent gets partial credit (not the max score possible for the question), their individual response will show that they got the question "partially correct".

Showing People Their Score
Show Quiz Results at the End of the Quiz

You can choose whether you want to show someone their total quiz score, and a summary of how they did on each individual quiz question, when they finish the quiz. The quiz results page only includes quiz questions—questions without scoring aren't included.

Unlike Instant Results, the quiz results page only shows the respondent's own score. No one can see other people's scores.

To display quiz results to respondents at the end of a quiz:

In the left sidebar, click Options.
Make sure quiz mode is enabled.
Select Display Quiz Results.
(Optional) If you don't want respondents to see the correct answers to the questions they got wrong, deselect Show correct answers to incorrect responses.
Limitations

Display Quiz Results is not available when using Kiosk Mode.

The following logic options are not compatible with Display Quiz Results:

Question Skip Logic
Page Skip Logic
Advanced Branching
Carry Forward Responses
Block Randomization
Question & Answer Piping
Advanced Piping

If you add incompatible logic to a survey when Display Quiz Results is turned on, the Quiz Results Page will be automatically disabled.

Show Custom Feedback on the Quiz Results Page

When the Display Quiz Results setting is turned on, you can show custom feedback at the end of a quiz (an image, text, or both). It'll display at the top of the quiz results page, right above the score.

You can either add a general message that everyone sees no matter what score they get, or you can show different feedback for different score ranges. For example, you can tell people that score 95% to 99% "Almost perfect! You should be proud." Custom feedback can be up to 1,000 characters.

Expand | Collapse
Show a General Message for Everyone

To add custom feedback at the end of the quiz:

Go to the Options section of the left sidebar.
Select Show quiz feedback at end.
Select General Message.
Click Enter Feedback.
In the General Message textbox, enter the text you want to show to people after they finish the quiz.
(Optional) Click + Image to add an image.
Click Save.
Show Different Messages Based on Score

To add a custom message based on score:

Go to the Options section of the left sidebar.
Select Show quiz feedback at end.
Select Based on score percentage or points.
Click Configure.
Choose whether you want the score ranges to be based on Percentage or Points.
Click +New Range.
Enter a Range Label and set the points or percentages for the first range of scores that you want to create a custom feedback message for.
In the textbox, enter the message you want to show to people who get a score within that range.
(Optional) Click + Image to add an image.
Click Save.
Click +New Range and repeat the steps to add more custom messages for different score ranges.

TIP! You can filter responses based on the score ranges you set up with a Range filter in the Analyze results section.

Email People Their Quiz Results

If you send your quiz via email invitation, you can turn on the Email Quiz Results collector option to email people their quiz results. When they finish the quiz, we'll email them a link to the quiz results page where they can view their results.

Analyzing Quiz Results
Overall Quiz Summary

The Quiz Summary at the top of the Analyze Results page shows you how everyone performed on the quiz overall.

You can apply filter or compare rules to focus on a subset of your data. Any filter or compare rules applied are reflected in the Quiz Summary. Show rules aren't reflected in the Quiz Summary.

Only responses from the first 10 pages are visible. If you have more than 10 pages, export your responses to view all results.

Learn more about the different parts of your Quiz Summary below.

Expand | Collapse
Average Quiz Score

The average score for all respondents displays as both a percent and as the average number of points over total points possible.

Score Distribution

A bar chart shows the score distribution of respondents. Each bar in the chart represents a range of scores. Hover over a bar in the chart to view the range as point totals.

Quiz Statistics
Statistics	Description
Lowest Score/Highest Score	The lowest and highest score a respondent received.
Mean	The average score among all respondents.
Median	The score that falls in the middle of the score distribution.
Standard Deviation	The amount of spread or distance from the mean.
Question Rankings

The Question Ranking table ranks all quiz questions in your survey so you can sort by difficulty or average score.

Difficulty Ranking: The question that has the lowest average score is considered the most difficult, and is ranked 1. If multiple questions have the same average score, they're assigned the same difficulty ranking.
Average Score: The percent of quiz respondents who correctly answered the question.

You can sort the Question Ranking table in ascending or descending order by clicking the table header.

Stats for Each Question

The summary for each quiz question shows you how people performed on that particular question overall.

Expand | Collapse
Quiz Statistics
Statistic	Description
Percent Correct	Percent or respondents who got the max score for the question.
Average Score	Average as points received over points possible and as a percent.
Standard Deviation	The amount of point spread or distance from the mean among respondents.
Difficulty	The question's difficulty ranking with 1 being the most difficult, out of the total number of quiz questions.
 Answer Choices

Any choices with point values assigned to them have a green check mark next to them so you can tell which answer choices count as correct answers.

Score

The Score column indicates how many points each answer choice was worth, out of the max score for the question.

Responses

The Responses column shows the percentage and number of respondents who chose each answer choice.

Stats for Individual Responses

Individual responses show how each respondent's answered each question in your survey and a Quiz Summary with the following data.

Expand | Collapse
Quiz Summary
Statistic	Description
Score	Their score as a percentage.
Points	The total number of points they got, out of the maximum possible points.
Rank	Where they rank compared to everyone else that took the quiz.
Percentile	The percentile the person falls into. For example, if someone is in the 25% percentile, it means their score is greater than or equal to 25% of respondents.
Quiz Results

Description
Correct	The number of questions where they got max points.
Incorrect	The number of questions where they got zero points.
Partially Correct	The number of questions where they got some points, but not max points.
Skipped	The number of quiz questions the respondent didn't answer.
Total Questions	The total number of quiz questions in the survey.
Exports and Shared Data

The following exports include the overall quiz summary and quiz statistics per question:

PDF (Summary Data and Individual Responses)
XLS (Summary Data and All Response Data)
CSV (Summary Data and All Response Data)

Shared data pages also include the quiz summary, quiz results per question, and the quiz summary for each individual response.
