Teams & Enterprise
Managing Teams

Manage Accounts with SCIM

SurveyMonkey
Manage Accounts with SCIM

Beta Feature: This feature is only for Enterprise teams that have Single Sign-On (SSO) set up.

To keep your team’s SurveyMonkey accounts up to date with information stored in an identity provider (IdP), such as Azure Active Directory, you can link the systems using the System for Cross-Domain Identity Management (SCIM). This helps your IT department keep track of accounts across multiple platforms.

Manage Accounts with SCIM

When you set up account provisioning with SCIM, some account management features will change. Here’s what will be mapped, synced, and managed for each user in the identity provider:

When someone joins or leaves your organization
Username
First and last name
Email address
Divisions (if set up for your team)

Primary Admins and Admins will continue to manage the following within SurveyMonkey:

Account reassignment
Role and seat assignments
Accounts that don’t have SSO enabled
Account deletion

Tip! Deactivate the team user through your IdP before reassigning or deleting the account.

Set Up SCIM Provisioning

Only the Primary Admin can set up SCIM provisioning for your organization. To make sure SCIM is a good fit for your IdP, the Primary Admin should check in with their SurveyMonkey Customer Success Manager (CSM) and their organization’s IT department—only 1 IdP per Enterprise team.

Once the team is aligned, the Primary Admin can:

Go to Settings.
Select User provisioning with SCIM.
Copy the SCIM endpoint link and provide it to your IT partner.
Select Generate token. Treat this unique token as you would your Primary Admin password and only give it to your IT partner.

Your organization’s IT partner will use the SCIM endpoint link and access token during set up of the IdP. They will also need to adjust the default mapping for your team’s needs.

Mapping guide

Below are mapping examples for your IT department to use with Azure Active Directory.

Example IdP attributes	SurveyMonkey SCIM
Attributes*	Mapping in SurveyMonkey
userPrincipalName	userName	Display name
IsSoftDeleted	active	Group member status
mail	emails[type eq "work"].value	Email address
givenName	name.givenName	First name
surname	name.familyName	Last name
mailNickname	externalId	n/a
employeeId	urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:employeeNumber	Employee ID
department	urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:division	Divisions
department	urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:department	Department

* Attributes help you track and monitor team activity in the SurveyMonkey User Report. All SCIM operations will be listed, including errors and failures.

To confirm SCIM is set up properly, your IT partner should manually provision one user through the IdP. Then, have the Primary Admin check the SurveyMonkey Activity page to see if the provision is there.

Revoke SCIM Provisioning

If you need to disconnect Surveymonkey from your IdP so the systems no longer sync, the Primary Admin can revoke SCIM provisioning. As long as SSO is enabled, there will be no impact to users who have already been synced.

To revoke the SCIM provisioning:

Go to Settings.
Select User provisioning with SCIM.
Next to the access token, select Revoke.
SCIM FAQs

Below are common questions with potential solutions to help resolve them.

Why can’t I delete an account?

With SCIM enabled accounts, only deactivated team members can be deleted.

Make sure that the user is deactivated through your IDP. If there's still an issue with deleting deactivated users from your team, reach out to your CSM.

Why are former employees shown as active in my Enterprise team?

Your IDP won't update past changes to SurveyMonkey. User deactivation only begins once SCIM is enabled, and so it won't deactivate users that were removed (former employees) before SCIM was applied.

To remove these users, contact your CSM.

Do deactivated accounts take up a license (seat)?

Yes. An admin must delete a deactivated account to free up a seat.

Why do I see so many invited users on the Manage Users page? 

Unless a user already has an SSO-enabled Enterprise account, any employee allowed to log in to SurveyMonkey using your organization’s corporate login credentials will show as an invited user on the Manage Users tab of My Team.

With SCIM, an invited user isn't sent an invitation to join the Team, and so don't take up a seat. This means that users can join but haven't taken any action yet to convert or create an account.

Why are members of my Enterprise team still showing as an invited user?

Accounts which aren't SSO-enabled are shown as invited by SCIM on the Manage Users tab.

For these users you will see them as both an invited user, and part of the team. Once the user converts their account to SSO, the invited user will be removed.

Tip! Make sure existing users convert their account when joining your Enterprise Team.

Charts & Data Tables

Customizing Charts and Data Tables

SurveyMonkey
Customizing Charts and Data Tables

Charts and data tables are automatically generated for all closed-ended survey questions, and for open-ended questions when Thematic Analysis is on.

If you're using multi-survey analysis, this process looks a little different.

To customize your charts and data tables:

From the Analyze results, go to the Question summaries tab.
Click the visualization name dropdown at the top of the question, e.g., Horizontal bar or Gauge.
Select from the Most common chart types and Display Options in the quick customization menu. Click More options to see all available customizations.
Select an available Chart Type. You can choose one of several chart types for each of your questions. The chart types available depend on the question type.
Explore the options under the Display Options, Colors, and Labels tabs, explained in detail below.
Check Apply to all to apply changes to all charts and data tables. Some might not update because some options aren't available for certain question types.
Click Save.

TIP! Export your custom charts and use them in presentations, send them via email, or share them anywhere else. Custom charts cannot be exported in CSV or XLS.

Display Options

Display options allow you to fine-tune the way your data displays in a chart or data table. The options available depend on both the question type and the chart type.

Option	Description


Chart, Data in Chart, Data Table

	Use the checkboxes to show or hide the question chart, the data table that appears below the question, or the data values (response counts or percentages) on the chart itself.
Zero-Response Answer Choices	Hide any answer choices that received no responses.
Statistical Significance	Show statistically significant differences in the data table below the question chart.
Basic Statistics	Chart the percentage of responses or the absolute number of responses for each answer choice.
Axis Scale	Show either a chart legend or chart labels for pie or donut charts. Chart labels appear alongside the chart itself and a chart legend appears at the bottom of the chart.
Min and Max	Edit the minimum and maximum axis values for the chart. As you collect new responses, the min and max values may adjust—the min value cannot be greater than the lowest value in the chart and the max value cannot be lower than the highest value in the chart.
Depth	Chart the average or weighted average, or chart the distribution of answer choices.
Decimal Places	Choose between 0, 1, or 2 decimal places.
Labels	Show either a chart legend or chart labels for pie or donut charts. Chart labels appear alongside the chart itself and a chart legend appears at the bottom of a chart.
Swap Rows and Columns	Swap the rows and columns in the data table of Ranking, Matrix/Rating Scale, and Matrix of Dropdown Menus question when Depth is set as Distribution.
Colors

You can customize chart colors for individual questions or apply a default color palette to your entire survey.

To edit chart colors:

From Question summaries in Analyze results, click the visualization name dropdown at the top of a question, e.g., Horizontal bar or Gauge.
Click More options, and select the color block to edit the color. You can choose from the color picker or enter your own hex codes.
Drag and drop the color blocks into the order you want reflected in the chart itself. The first color in the row corresponds with the first answer choice in the data table.
Check Apply to all to apply changes to all charts. Some might not update because some options aren't available for certain question types.
Click Save.
Labels

You can edit labels directly in context. To edit a label, click the visualization name dropdown at the top of a question, click More options, and go to the Labels tab. You can also edit labels from the data table by clicking the “...” next to the answer choice header and selecting Edit this label.

Editing labels doesn't affect the question text or answer choices in your survey design.
You can restore the original label by clicking Revert to the right of a label in edit mode.
Global Settings

Save time by applying colors and data settings to your entire survey at once, instead of editing each chart one by one.

Appearance

Change the look of your charts and tables across your entire survey. The color settings available depend on question types. 

To customize your survey appearance:

Select Options from the top toolbar.
From the Appearance tab, choose your color settings:
Team colors: Apply your organization's shared color scheme for consistent branding. If you generated a theme while designing your survey, those AI-generated brand colors also appear here. 
Default color palettes: Apply a pre-set color scheme (such as Heritage or Monochrome colours) to all charts. 
Custom color palettes: Choose your own colors for your results. If you edit a Team palette, those colors will move to your Custom palette for further editing
Data Options

Control how your results are measured and displayed throughout your survey. The Data options available depend on both the question type and the chart type.

To use data options globally:

Select Options from the top toolbar.
From the right-hand menu, select Data options.
Toggle the following on or off:
Option	Description
Data table	Show or hide the data table that appears below the question charts.
Data labels in charts	Show the data values (e.g., response counts or percentages) directly on the charts.
Basic statistics	Show the minimum, maximum, mean, median, and standard deviation in a separate data table below the question chart.
Answer choices with no responses	Show or hide any answer choices that received no responses.
Statistical Significance	Show statistically significant differences in the data table below the question chart. This setting is only relevant when a Compare rule is applied.
Decimal Places	Choose between 0, 1, or 2 decimal places.
Response quality	Show or hide flags on poor-quality responses identified by machine learning.

LLM Connectors

SurveyMonkey
LLM Connectors

SurveyMonkey meets you wherever you work with AI assistants to help you more seamlessly create, edit, and publish surveys, search surveys, review results or generate summaries, and explore trends to help you uncover insights and take actionable next steps to drive your goals. 

Whether you are using Claude or ChatGPT, SurveyMonkey brings real human insights directly into your workflow so you can make your next move confidently.

How It Works
Connect SurveyMonkey to an AI assistant:
Claude
ChatGPT
Type a natural language prompt in the chat to search, build, publish, or analyze surveys.
(Optional): After you sent your survey, if you want to edit the live survey, log into SurveyMonkey.

Tip! Feel free to use multiple AI assistants simultaneously to decide how you want to collect and analyze your survey feedback. 

Availability and Limitations 
Plan Requirements

Connecting to an LLM is available on any plan, as long as your account’s data is stored in the United States. Your specific plan, user seat, or role may limit the output of the connector, and you may need to upgrade to access all response data and paid features.

Language

While our connectors are available in all LLM- supported languages, our connectors deliver the best experience in English.

Enterprise Availability

LLM Connectors aren’t available to HIPAA-enabled Enterprise accounts or those with an Enhanced Sensitive Data Protection account.

If you want your Enterprise team to have access, please contact us.

SurveyMonkey Access Requirements 

To function, the connectors require access to:

View your surveys and those shared with you
Create or edit surveys in your account
Create or edit collectors for surveys in your account
View if surveys in your account have responses and their metadata
View answers along with responses
View your user information
Available Tools
Read-only	Write or delete
- Get page details by ID
- List pages in a survey
- Get question details by ID
- Get available question types and display options
- List questions on a page
- Get number of responses for a survey
- Get survey responses with full answer data
- View information about the SurveyMonkey MCP Server
- Get survey details by ID
- Search and list user's surveys
- Get a statistical summary of survey responses
- Generate an AI-suggested survey plan from a topic description	-  Add a page to a survey
- Add a question to a page
- Create a new survey
- Create a shareable survey link
- Delete a question from a page
- Edit a single question
- Reorder all questions on a page
- Update survey properties


What can you do with an LLM connector?

SurveyMonkey can connect with a variety of LLMs. Here are a few examples of prompts to get you started:

Example action	Example prompt
Search surveys	Find my latest customer satisfaction survey
Create a survey	Create a post-event survey for my webinar
Edit surveys	Update question 3 to be more formal
Generate a shareable link	Give me a shareable link to send out my customer feedback survey
Get response metadata	How many responses has my latest survey received?
Summarizes insights from Analyze results	Summarize the key insights from my latest survey
Disabling the Connection

To disconnect a linked connector (aka Plug-in): 

Go to My account and scroll to Linked Accounts.
Find the SurveyMonkey MCP Server you wish to disconnect, and select Unlink.

Team and Enterprise admins can disable access for their entire team by contacting SurveyMonkey support.

Your Responsibility

When using a connector, you are responsible for reviewing the permissions you grant during connector set up and for monitoring the outputs and actions the AI assistant proposes or takes in your SurveyMonkey account. AI assistants may not always be accurate, complete, or current.

SurveyMonkey doesn’t control the LLM and we aren’t responsible for its availability, security, accuracy, outputs, or actions.

Your use of an LLM connector is subject to our Terms of use, Governing services agreement, as applicable, Privacy notice, and Connector Feature Service-Specific Terms.

Results Dashboards

SurveyMonkey
Results Dashboards

Results Dashboards are a great way to present your survey results. Customize your results, add charts and text, then publish to share your dashboard with anyone.

TIP! Results dashboards are best used to present results to others. Use multi-survey analysis dashboards to compare results from multiple surveys.

Building a Dashboard

To create a new dashboard, start by either adding charts from your survey in bulk or adding charts from individual questions one at a time. On most plans, you can add up to 20 supported questions, and if you're on an Enterprise plan, you can add up to 40.

Unsupported questions and settings
Incompatible Questions	Incompatible Charts and Settings
File Upload

Slider

Matrix of Dropdowns

Multiple Textboxes

Date/Time

Contact Info

Text or Image

A/B Tests

Click Map	Tags to categorize responses

Questions with more than 20 answer options

Questions with a Benchmark showing

Stacked bar charts for questions with more than 4 answer choices

Questions with more than 4 answer choices and a Compare rule applied

Questions with hidden or combined answer choices

"Other" comment fields

To add charts from the first 20 (or 40, on Enterprise plans) supported questions:

Go to the Analyze results section of your survey.
At the top of the page, select Add to > +New dashboard.
Enter a Title, and choose how you want to get started:
Build it for me: Include all compatible questions.
Start from scratch: Choose which questions to include.
Select Create.

To add a chart from an individual question:

Go to the Analyze results section of your survey.
Find a question you'd like to add to the dashboard.
Select the pin icon.
Select +New dashboard.
Enter a name for your dashboard.
Select Create.
Adding Charts

Once the dashboard has been created, you can add more charts to your dashboard.

To add charts:

Go to the Analyze results section of your survey.
Find the chart you want to add.
Select the pin icon.
Choose the dashboard you want to add the chart to.
Customizing Your Dashboard

Once you've added charts to your dashboard, you can customize how it looks.

To customize your dashboard:

From the Analyze results section, select Dashboards and crosstabs at the top of the page.
Find your dashboard, then select Edit.

Here are the things you can customize in your dashboard:

Change layout: Choose between Column and Grid layout in the toolbar.
Rearrange charts: Arrange your dashboard by dragging and dropping cards into rows and adding text cards to give your results more context. You can add up to three cards per row and 20-40 cards per dashboard, depending on your plan.
Customize visualizations: Find a chart, then click the three dots menu in the upper-right corner of the card, then toggle the options. If you are using the Column layout, you can choose to show the chart, the table, or both. If you are using the Grid layout, you can only choose to show the chart or the table.
View open-ended responses: For questions with open-ended responses, you can click the three dots (...) in the upper-right corner of the card to switch between List View to show all text responses at once, or Slide View to show text responses one at a time.
Note: Cards for open-ended responses only show the 50 most recent answers.
Remove charts: To delete a card from your dashboard, click the three dots (...) in the upper-right corner of the card and click the Delete button.

TIP! Customize your chart's display options and colors before adding them to a dashboard to make them stand out.

Sharing a Dashboard

When you're ready to share your results with people, publish and share your dashboard. If your survey is still open and collecting responses, the dashboard will update automatically as more people answer your survey.

When you share the dashboard link in messaging and collaboration apps, we’ll show the survey title, response count, and first chart in the message preview. The preview reflects the title, response count, and first chart from the time you share the link and won’t update automatically.

To publish your dashboard:

In the Analyze results section of your survey, select Dashboards and crosstabs at the top of the page.
Find the dashboard you want to share.
Select More Options.
Select Turn share link ON.
Select Preview to open the dashboard in another window.
Copy the link and share your dashboard anywhere.

It isn't possible to embed a dashboard on your website.

Adding Password Protection

Password Protect Shared Results

Paid feature
Log in to see if this feature is included in your plan.
Log in
Sign up free

You can password protect your dashboard. Anyone you share the link with will need to enter the password to access it.

If password protection is turned on before sharing the link, we won’t show the survey title, response count, or first chart in the message preview.

To password protect your published dashboard:

In the Analyze results section of your survey, select Dashboards and crosstabs at the top of the page.
Find the dashboard you want to password protect.
Select Preview.
At the bottom of the dashboard, select Dashboard Settings.
Select the toggle to turn Password protection on.
Enter a password.
Select Done.

You won't see Dashboard Settings at the bottom of your Dashboard if it isn't published yet. You can select Publish to turn link sharing on and control password protection.

Enforcing Single Sign-on (SSO) Authentication

(Enterprise only—if you're interested, contact sales) Enterprise customers with SSO enabled can enforce SSO authentication for these pages to further secure access beyond a static password. 

To require SSO authentication for your published dashboard:

In the Analyze results section of your survey, select Dashboards and Crosstabs at the top of the page.
Find the dashboard you want to protect.
Select Preview.
At the bottom of the dashboard, select Dashboard Settings.
Toggle on Single Sign-on. This limits access to people in your organization.
Select Done.
Turning Off Sharing

If you need to limit access to your dashboard after you've shared it, you can turn sharing off. Anyone you've previously shared the dashboard with won't be able to access the dashboard if they visit the link or try to refresh their browser.

To turn off sharing:

In the Analyze results section of your survey, select Dashboards and crosstabs at the top of the page.
Find the dashboard.
Select More Options.
Select Turn share link OFF.
Managing Your Dashboards

You can manage all of your dashboards from the Dashboards and crosstabs page.

Option	Description
Preview	After you publish a dashboard, see what it will look like to anyone who gets the link.
Edit	Make changes to your dashboard at any time. Any changes you make will take effect immediately.
More Options	Turn your share link on to publish it, or off to limit access. You can also delete your dashboard here. Deleting a dashboard won't affect or erase any survey results.

Accessibility When Using SurveyMonkey

SurveyMonkey
Accessibility When Using SurveyMonkey

SurveyMonkey encourages web accessibility and provides tools to help you create more accessible  surveys. This article offers tips for creating surveys with Section 508 and Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2 (WCAG2) in mind. 

To start off, get to know some common accessibility terms, and learn how you can create accessible surveys or use assistive technology to navigate SurveyMonkey surveys.

Download SurveyMonkey's Accessibility Conformance Report - VPAT v2.5 - WCAG 2.2 Level AA (updated September 2026) »

Accessibility Terms

Here are common accessibility terms, their acronym, and description:

Term and Acronym	Description
508 Compliance	Section 508 is a United States (US) federal law addressing accessibility of digital technology developed, bought, maintained, or used by federal agencies.

Web Content Accessibility
Guidelines 2
(WCAG2)	WCAG2 is a set of internationally used guidelines for making digital content more accessible to people with disabilities.

The guidelines help you evaluate the accessibility of your survey or form based on 4 accessibility principles:

Is my survey Perceivable? Is info easy to see or hear, or access via other human senses?
Is my survey Operable? Ensure it’s clear to navigate and interact with, since anyone should be able to move around the survey, even if they cannot use a mouse and instead use their voice or a keyboard.
Is my survey Understandable? Make sure survey content and structure isn't confusing, it's easy to read.
Is my survey Robust? Will screen helper technology, like software that reads the screen out loud or magnification tools to zoom in on text, work with your survey.

Voluntary Product 
Accessibility Template
(VPAT)	This is a template companies use to log how their product supports accessibility standards.
A completed VPAT is called an Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR).

The Scope: The product and features evaluated.
The Test: How the product was evaluated against accessibility criteria.
The Results: Which criteria the product supports, partially supports, or does not support, with explanations.
Customers can use a completed VPAT to learn how a product supports accessibility when evaluating software.

Accessibility Conformance Report
(ACR)	The ACR describes how the assessed survey-taking experience supports the accessibility criteria listed in the report. 

Download SurveyMonkey's
Accessibility Conformance Report - VPAT v2.5 - WCAG 2.2 Level AA (updated September 2026) »

Assistive Technology
(AT)	Any software, hardware, or tool that helps a person with a disability use a computer or complete a task.

Some include:

Screen readers which reads the text on a screen out loud for users who are blind or have low vision.
Screen magnifiers zoom in on parts of a screen to make text and images much bigger for users with low vision.


Americans with Disabilities Act
(ADA)	The ADA is another US civil rights law addressing accessibility. SurveyMonkey isn’t evaluated on our ADA accessibility.

Compliance with Section 508 and WCAG2

You can use  SurveyMonkey’s features and the checklist below to help create more accessible surveys with Section 508 and WCAG2 standards in mind. Accessibility also depends on your survey content, questions, and settings. 

What is an accessible SurveyMonkey survey?

An accessible survey:

Is designed so that people with varying hearing, movement, sight, and cognitive abilities can complete it.

Enables respondents using screen magnifiers to successfully complete the survey.

Has the text elements to enable a survey taker to successfully navigate and complete a survey using a screen reader—assistive software that converts on-screen text into audio using a text-to-speech (TTS) system.

Can be completed using voice recognition software.

Doesn't require a mouse or keyboard to complete.

Creating Accessible Surveys
Themes and Color Contrast

Accessible themes are designed with color contrast and brightness in mind to help more people use your survey, including people with colorblindness.

Our default survey theme, Catalyst, along with Heritage or Arctic themes, support accessible survey design. Avoid adjusting the colors or style settings of the theme without checking the effect on color contrast.

Look for the accessible survey icon to help you choose a theme.

Custom Themes

To keep surveys accessible, please don’t make changes to accessible themes. 

If you create a custom theme, you can use a tool like the Tanaguru contrast finder to check whether the color combinations meet  WCAG 2.2 Level AA standards for contrast ratios.

Accessible Surveys Checklist

To help make your survey more accessible, make sure you:

✅ Use an accessible theme, displayed with an accessibility icon.

✅ Choose question types and settings with accessibility in mind.

❌ Avoid these question types and settings:
Matrix of Dropdown menus question type
Click Map question type
Accepting payments page
Multilingual Surveys— People using a screen reader won't be able to select their preferred language from the dropdown menu
Forced Ranking setting for a matrix/rating scale question type

✅ Images and videos need alternative text (alt text). Images can't be seen or read by all, so add a short description of the image to be stored in the code for assistive technology's use
Our various features all let you add alt text:

Image choice question
Freestanding survey images
Image A/B Tests
Logo

Videos in your survey should include closed captions, text displayed on a video showing what people say and describe sounds,like [music playing] or [door slams]) for people who are deaf or hard of hearing.

❌ Don't include images that blink or flash. If using animated content in your survey, check that it meets the time refresh requirements.

✅ Clearly identify required questions in text.
By default, requiring a question adds an asterisk next to the question. Keep the asterisk, but don’t rely on it alone to explain which questions are required.  You can also use a survey introduction to let respondents know that the question is required.

✅ Set your Star rating question icons to black, and check how they appear to respondents.

✅ Write clear error messages for respondents who enter an invalid response to a question with answer validation applied or skip a required question.
This way, an error message appears  to guide them. Customize the error text so that people know specifically how to answer the question, so they can move forward in the survey.

✅ Place text fields close to row labels on Multiple Textboxes or Matrix/Rating Scale questions, adjust the question layout to keep the Labels and Text fields close together.
When a row label is positioned far away from the text field, it may cause issues for screen magnifiers. 

✅ Use Page titles for Heading 2 (H2). If you want to use an H2 in your heading rank, turn on page titles. See below for details on Headings.

✅ Use the Email Invitation or Web Link to send your survey. 

❌ Other ways of sending your survey may not be accessible. Check accessibility before using another method.

❌ Don’t set your Survey Format to the One Question at a Time or Conversation survey format, as these aren’t accessible.

❌ Don't edit default Navigation buttons without checking how the new labels work with a screen reader.
By default, navigation buttons are labeled Previous, Next, and Done, which work well with screen readers.

❌ Don't password protect your survey.
The page to enter a password isn't accessible.

Taking Surveys with a Screen Reader
Screen Readers We Support
JAWS
NVDA
VoiceOver
TalkBack

Screen reader experiences can vary by question type and survey settings - see exceptions listed in the accessible surveys checklist.
For the best survey taking experience, we recommend using the most updated version of one of our supported browsers.

Headings

The table describes what each heading level represents in a SurveyMonkey survey. Some headings may not work as expected with a screen reader. Please check your preferred screen reader's manual to learn how to navigate surveys.

Heading Level	Description
Heading 1	Survey title
Heading 2	Page title
Heading 3	Page description
Heading 4	Navigate between error messages and questions in a survey
When taking a survey, you can use your screen reader to navigate the list of questions by navigating between elements at heading level 4. Heading structure can vary.
If you receive error messages when submitting a page, use your screen reader to navigate heading level 4 to move between questions with error messages. Some error messages may not be announced as expected.

SurveyMonkey surveys don't use heading levels 5 and 6.

Feedback

SurveyMonkey is dedicated to helping people create surveys that are accessible. If you have feedback on how we can do better, please complete the SurveyMonkey Accessibility Feedback Form.

While we may not be able to respond to your feedback directly, your comments can help us identify areas to improve.

Printing a PDF of a Survey

SurveyMonkey
Printing a PDF of a Survey

Print Survey PDF

Paid feature
Log in to see if this feature is included in your plan.
Log in
Sign up free

To download the survey design in PDF format:

Select the Design Survey tab.
Select the printer icon on the right side of the survey design header.
Select your print options—see the options in the table below.
Select Download PDF. A PDF of the survey design in your default survey language downloads to your computer.
Once you open the download, you can print it from the PDF viewer program you use, like Adobe Reader.

TIP! If you don't see the printer icon, go to your browser settings and zoom out your view.

Print Options

You can choose from these options when you print your survey design.

Option	Description
Print style	Choose Optimized for Print to download a grayscale PDF of the survey design, or choose Use Current Theme to download a PDF in your survey's theme colors.
Include images	Include your logo, images, and Image A/B Tests in the PDF.
Include survey title	Even if your display options are set to hide the survey title, checking this box includes the survey title in the PDF.
Include page numbers	Shows the page numbers at the top of each page. If your display options are set to hide page titles, page numbers won't appear in the PDF.
Print without page breaks	All survey questions get downloaded together, without survey page breaks on the PDF.
Orientation	Choose Portrait (Vertical) or Landscape (Horizontal).
Paper Size	Choose Letter (8.5" x 11"), Legal (8.5" x 14"), or A4 (210mm x 297 mm)
Limitations

The PDF of your survey design won't include the following aspects of your survey:

Logic
Menu choices in Dropdown or Matrix of dropdown menus questions
Languages other than your default survey language
SurveyMonkey footer
Navigation buttons

Getting Feedback? You can share an online preview of your survey and invite people to comment. The online preview will let others test the survey experience, and their responses won't be recorded.

Payment Methods

Audience Credits

SurveyMonkey
Audience Credits

Audience credits let you pay for your SurveyMonkey Audience responses in advance, from within SurveyMonkey or LaunchPad.

This is great if you have a set budget for your survey projects since you pay one invoice upfront, then use credits to pay for individual projects.

You can buy credits in all supported currencies, and you need to use your credits within 1 year from the date of purchase.

Buying Audience Credits
How to Buy Credits

To buy Audience credits:

Log in to your SurveyMonkey account and select your Profile circle in the upper-right corner.
Select My Account.
Select the Transaction History tab.
Select Add Credits and enter the amount you want to buy (whole numbers only). Then, enter your billing details.
Review your order details and select Confirm to create the invoice you need to pay.
Open the invoice and select Pay Now. All the details on how to pay and where to send payments are right there on the invoice.

Tip! Once your payment is processed, you can start using credits to pay for responses. If you want to use them right away, select Pay Now on your invoice and pay by credit or debit card.

Taxes on Audience Credits Purchases

Depending on your billing country, taxes may be included when you pay the invoice for your Audience credits. You won’t pay taxes again when you use credits to buy responses—in other words, taxes aren’t included when you use credits to pay for responses, since you already paid taxes when you bought the credits, when applicable.

Invoices with VAT included must be paid within 45 days otherwise the invoice is voided.

Using Credits to Buy Responses
How to Use Credits

Once you have your survey ready to go and you're ready to launch your Audience project, you can use your existing credit balance to pay for responses.

To use Audience credits to buy responses in SurveyMonkey:

Go to the Publish survey section of the survey you're buying responses for.
Select Choose an audience or select Add new collector, then select Buy responses. 
Set up your Targeted audience collector.
When you’re ready, select Checkout.
Under Payment Method, select My Credits and Confirm.

To use credits to pay for Audience responses in Launchpad:

After setting up your project, go to Collect.
Select Target your ideal respondents, and set up your Target audience collector.
When you’re ready, select Checkout.
Under Payment Method, select My Credits and select Confirm.
Don't have enough credits?

You can’t use credits as a partial payment—to use credits, you need enough to cover the total amount. If you don't have enough credits to cover the full cost, you have two options:

Add credits to your account so you can make a full payment using your credit balance. You can select Add Credits from the checkout window, then buy credits. Once your payment is processed, you can go back to your Audience collector to complete the payment with credits. All your settings in the collector are saved for you so you can pick up where you left off.
Pay for your responses with a credit or debit card instead of using credits.
Your Credit Balance and Transaction History

Your credit balance is the total number of credits currently available to you to buy Audience responses. You can find your credit balance in your Transaction history.

To go to your transaction history:

Log in to SurveyMonkey.
Select your profile circle in the upper-right corner.
Select My Account.
Select Transaction History.

From your Transaction History, you can view and print your Audience Credit Activity and your Purchase History with a record of all upcoming and past invoices.

If you have an invoice you need to pay, select Pay Now. All payment methods and bank info you need to make your payment are right on the invoice.

Managing Budgets on Enterprise

Enterprise Optional Add-On: If you're interested, contact sales.

Budgets are an easy, manageable way for Admins to buy targeted SurveyMonkey Audience responses, and share them with a team of selected members. Admins can set up a budget for any project or purpose and allocate credits from the reserve —added members can then spend those credits without needing further permissions.

Admins creating a budget

To create a new budget:

Select My Team from the main navigation.
Select Manage Credits.
Select Create budget.
(Optional): Type the Budget name and Description.
From the Members button, search or select to add members to the budget. You can search for members of your team by name, email, or role.
Select Create.

You can create a budget with no users and add team members after.

Admins managing budgets

Once a budget is created, you can then edit the Budget name, Description and manage members by selecting the More icon (...) to the right of the budget, on the Manage credits page.

Expand | Collapse
Adding or deleting a member

You can also manage members by:

Adding a user: Select the Members button, search or select to add members to the budget. You can search for members of your team by name, email, or role.
Deleting a user: Remove a member from the Team by selecting (-) beside their name.

Users can only be members of one budget. If you aren't able to select a Team member, it means they are already a member of a budget and must be first removed, then added.
Deleting a budget

When deleting a budget, credits in this budget move to your reserve credit balance. Members no longer have access to these credits.

Select the More icon (...) to the right of the budget you'd like to delete.
Review the information shown about the budget.
Select Delete.
Admins managing credits

The Manage credits page has all the details you need to manage your budgets. On the Credit Allocation card, see how many credits are in your reserve and budgets separately. You can use this page to buy and transfer credits.

Expand | Collapse
Buying credits

To buy credits:

Select My Team from the main navigation.
Select Manage credits.
Select Buy credits.

Credits are then added to the reserve.

Transferring credits

To transfer credits into a budget:

Tip! You can transfer credits from one budget to another.

From the Manage Credits page.
Select Transfer Credits.
From the dropdown select From, and To.
Fill in the Amount.
Select Transfer.
Using credits in budgets

Once you have your survey ready to go, and you're ready to launch your Audience project, you can use your credit balance in your budget to pay for responses.

Expand | Collapse
How to use credits

To use credits, you need to belong to a budget.

After setting up your project, navigate to the Checkout page.
Under Payment Method, you see a breakdown of:
Budget Name
Credits Available
Credits required
Select Confirm to complete your purchase.
Need more credits?

If there aren't enough credits available on the Checkout page, you can request the credits you need from an Admin.

Select Request credits.
(Optional) Include a message for your Admin.
Select Send Request. Admins are then sent a notification to review your request.

Tip! When requesting credits, add in the amount you need and your budget name.

Not in a budget?

You can request access straight from the Checkout page, as well as in your Transaction History.

To request access:

Go to your Transaction History.
Select Request access.
(Optional): Include a message for your Admin.
Select Send Request. Admins are then sent a notification to review your request.
Enterprise Teams without Budgets

Previous Enterprise Add-On: Some Enterprise teams manage Audience credits differently from our Budgets feature. If you are interested in Budgets, please contact your CSM.

By default, all users on a team manage their own credit balance and buy responses directly.

On Enterprise teams, the Primary Admin can restrict users from buying responses in Enterprise Settings. Users request credits, and the Primary Admin transfers them to their account.

Expand | Collapse
Transfer Credits

Primary Admins on Enterprise teams can purchase and transfer credits from the Manage Credits page.

To transfer credits from one user on your team to another:

Select My Team from the top navigation.
Select Manage Credits.
Find the user you want to transfer credits to and select +.
Choose the account you want to transfer credits from.
Enter the amount of credits you want to transfer.
Select Transfer Credits.
Request Credits

If you can’t buy your own responses, request the credits you need from your Primary Admin.

To request credits:

Go to your Transaction History.
Select Request Credits.
Enter the amount of credits you need.
(Optional): Include a message for your Admin.
Select Send Request. Your Primary Admin is sent a notification to review your request.

You can also request credits when purchasing Audience responses.
Track and Export Credit Usage

Primary Admins on Enterprise teams can export a credit tracking report from the Manage Credits page.

Each export includes .CSV files for:

Credit balances: Who on the team has credits.
Invoices: How much the credits cost for each project.
Transfers: History of credit transfers between users.
Credit expirations: When your credits will expire.

To get the report:

Select My Team from the top navigation.
Select Manage Credits.
Select Export reports at the top of the table.
(Optional): Set a date range filter.
Select Export.
Open the .CSV file on your computer to view it.

Collaborating With Your Team

Workgroups

SurveyMonkey
Workgroups

Enterprise Feature: If you're interested, contact sales. If you already have an Enterprise account, contact your Customer Success Manager.

Workgroups help organize team members with a shared purpose to work together on survey projects.

Primary Admins and Admins can create workgroups to quickly and easily share surveys with a group of people on your team. Plus, you can manage members, assign roles, and change owner status so each team member has the right level of access to surveys. You can contact your CSM to let Power Users create, own, and manage workgroups, too.

What's the difference between Workgroups and Divisions? Workgroups help organize team members collaborating on survey projects while Divisions help with administrative management of large teams.

Create a Workgroup

To create a new workgroup:

Select My Team from the main navigation.
Select Workgroups.
Click New Workgroup.
Type the Workgroup name and Purpose. Click Create Workgroup.
From the Members tab, search or click to add members to the workgroup. You can search for members of your team by name, email, or role.
From the Surveys tab, add the surveys you want to share with all members of the workgroup.
From the Settings tab, select whether the workgroup is Public or Private. Public workgroups are visible to your entire team, while private workgroups are only visible to its members.

When a team member is added to a workgroup, they're assigned the default role. Manage Members to update the default role and individual member roles.

Workgroup Surveys and Roles
Surveys

Add surveys to a workgroup to share it with all team members. You can add surveys when creating a workgroup or share surveys directly from Home.

Workgroup Roles

Contacts are unique to individual accounts, so only the person who creates an Email Invitation and Text Message collector can edit it, send reminders, or export contacts. All other workgroup members—including Full Access—see those shared collectors as View Only.

A user’s role in a workgroup determines if they can view, access, and edit the workgroup's shared surveys. These roles only apply within the workgroup and a user’s Enterprise seat determines what role they can have.

Workgroup Role	Member Permissions
Full Access	Full permissions to view, create, edit, or delete anything in the Design Survey, Collect Responses, and Analyze sections.
Editor	Full permissions to the Design Survey section. Limited permissions to Collect Responses and Analyze sections.
Collector	Full Access to the Collect Responses section. Limited permissions to the Design Survey section and view-only access to the Analyze section.
Analyzer	

Full permissions to the Analyze section. Limited permissions to view the survey design and collector list.

People you're working with will see any rules, custom charts, shared data pages, exports, or text analysis features created by the survey owner or any others with Full Access or Analyzer permissions. You need to refresh the Analyze Results page to see others' changes.


Viewer	People can view the Design Survey, Collect Responses, and Analyze sections but can’t edit, share surveys with the workgroup, or make changes. This is the only role a Casual User can have in workgroups.
Manage Workgroups
Managing Members

The Members tab displays every workgroup member's name, email, and role. This is also where you can add members to a workgroup, re-assign roles, remove members, or review team requests to join a public workgroup.

Tip! Check out the Notification center to see Workgroup messages from the last 30 days.

Expand | Collapse
Re-assign a member's role

To re-assign an individual member's role:

Select My Team from the top navigation.
Select Workgroups.
From the Members tab, click on . to the right of the member's name you want to re-assign. Click Assign Role.
Select the role from the dropdown. Click Assign.
Remove a member

To remove a member from a workgroup:

Select My Team from the top navigation.
Select Workgroups.
From the Members tab, click on . to the right of the member's name you want to remove. Click Remove member.
Click Remove.

The removed member loses access to the workgroup's shared surveys unless they are the survey owner or the survey is shared with them independently of the workgroup.

Re-assign the default role

To re-assign the default role for a workgroup:

Select My Team from the top navigation.
Select Workgroups.
From the Settings tab, click the Default Role dropdown and select the new default role.
Click Save Changes.
Review a request to join a workgroup

To review a member request to join a workgroup:

Select My Team from the top navigation.
Select Workgroups.
From the Members tab, Accept or Deny a member request to join the workgroup.
Update Owner

A workgroup owner, Primary Admin, or Admin can make any member an owner of the workgroup or remove owner status from an existing owner. Owners can’t remove their own owner status.

To update owner status:

Select My Team from the top navigation.
Select Workgroups.
From the Members tab, click on the three dots (...) to the right of the member you want to update. Select Make this person an owner or Remove owner status.
Delete a Workgroup

If a workgroup is no longer needed, delete the workgroup. When a workgroup is deleted, the shared surveys will no longer be available to members, unless they are owned by the member or the survey is shared independently of the workgroup.

To delete a workgroup:

Select My Team from the top navigation.
Select Workgroups.
Find the workgroup you want to delete and click the three dots (...) to the right of that workgroup.
Select Delete.
Find a Workgroup

Anyone on the team can see the workgroups they're a part of in the My Workgroups tab or view the entire team's public workgroups in the All Workgroups tab—just click My Team on the main navigation and select Workgroups.

If you'd like to join a public workgroup, you can Ask to join. This sends an email notification to the workgroup owner to review.

Sending Surveys
Sending by Email

Embedding Questions in Email Invitations

SurveyMonkey
Embedding Questions in Email Invitations

You can embed the first question of your survey in your Email Invitation, as long as the first question is a supported question type. When a survey taker chooses an answer option in the email, they're sent to the first page of your survey to continue taking the survey.

TIP! If you don't see the Embed first question toggle when you're composing your message then you're not using a supported question type or your survey doesn't meet the design requirements.

How to Embed

To embed a question in an email:

Go to the Design Survey section of your survey.
Add a supported question type to the very beginning of page 1.
Make sure your survey meets the design requirements. Don't enable any option that would disqualify the question or you won't see the option to embed the first question.
Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Create an Email Invitation.
Compose your message and make sure the Embed first question toggle is on.
(Optional) Customize your message.
Click Next.
Select the In-email Response Capture collector option and other collector options.
In-email Response Capture Collector Option

You can choose whether to save the first response from the email instantly or to wait to save the response until the respondent clicks the Next or Done button. By default, the collector option is set to Off and saves the first response upon clicking Next or Done. If the embedded question has an Other Textbox or Comment field, recipient’s responses won’t be recorded from the email instantly—the response is only submitted when clicking the Next or Done button in the browser.

In-Email Response Capture Collector Option is only available while the message is in the draft stage. This setting cannot be changed once the message has been scheduled or sent.

Password Protection isn't available when In-email Response Capture is On. To use Password protection, turn off In-email Response Capture.

When In-email response capture is On, email scanner bots could click the links within your email invitation, as a security measure. These bot clicks record responses to the embedded question before your respondent sees the email. This means a bot response can cause a misleading responses to the embedded question.
When an actual respondent takes the survey, the responses recorded by email scanner bots are replaced by the respondent’s true answer.
If you’re concerned about poor response quality due to email scanner bots, don’t enable In-email response capture.
If you’ve already collected data with this option on, you can clean up your responses in Analyze by identifying and deleting incomplete responses related to the collector that were recorded shortly after sending the invitation. Bot answers will only have recorded responses to the embedded, first question.

Survey Behavior

How the first answer choice is saved depends on the In-email Response Capture collector option selected and whether the embedded question has an Other Textbox or Comment field. Regardless of whether the first answer is saved immediately or not, the respondent is sent to the first page of the survey so they can continue answering the rest of the questions.

They'll see their response to the first question pre-selected in SurveyMonkey. Respondents need to click Next on the first page to save their other responses and trigger any logic in your survey.

If you're sending a test email to preview the survey, we don't pre-populate the response in the survey preview since we don't actually collect any responses in survey previews.

If you modify your survey after the email collector has been sent, but before the respondent opens the email, the in-email response capture will no longer work. Because survey edits may invalidate the embedded question or other conditions, a response will not be saved or pre-populated. Instead, the survey will simply open for the respondent to answer.

When the first question is embedded, the email invitation doesn't have a Begin Survey button. Respondents need to answer the embedded question to open the survey in a browser tab to take the remaining survey questions.

Supported Question Types

To embed a question in an email invitation, use a supported question type as the first question on page 1 of your survey:

Multiple Choice
Net Promoter® Score (NPS)
Star Rating
Survey Design Requirements

To embed a question in an email invitation, your survey needs to meet these survey design requirements:

Use a supported question type as the first question on page 1 of your survey—don't add anything in front of the question, like an Intro Page or Text.
Don't use Page Randomization or Block Randomization on page 1 of your survey.
Don't enable a Quota on your survey.
Setting and Option Requirements

The settings and options applied to the question you want to embed may disqualify it or cause it to render differently in the email than what you see in your survey design.

Expand | Collapse
Multiple Choice Questions
Don't insert an image or video in answer choices.
If you enable the Randomize, Flip, or Sort Choices option on the question, don't randomize or flip answer choices, but you can alphabetize them.
Don't enable the Adjust Question Layout option.
Don't enable the Question Text A/B Test option.
We don't recommend adding an “Other” answer option or comment field on the question you want to embed—the question will render differently in the email. While the full Other answer option or comment field will display once the survey opens in a browser, survey-takers may not notice the additional answer option.
If you changed the layout of the question to 2 columns, 3 columns, or horizontal, it'll be displayed as 1 column in the email.
Star Rating Questions
You can use the Star, Smiley, or Heart icons on the question you want to embed, but, due to email client compatibility, you can't use the Thumb icon.
Don't add Other as an answer option for comments.
Don't enable the Question Text A/B Test option.
Don't use image or video rating labels.
You can choose a scale from 2 to 10, however, questions with larger scales aren't mobile responsive—they'll be static in the email, so people will have to scroll to see the full scale.
Troubleshooting Issues
Why does the email look different than what I see in SurveyMonkey?

If you update your survey design after scheduling your message and it no longer meets the requirements, we'll send the default email template without the embedded question.

Email clients can render HTML messages differently, which can cause HTML Template or Custom HTML messages to display differently than what you expect.

Planned Site Maintenance

SurveyMonkey
Planned Site Maintenance

This maintenance impacts all customers with survey data stored in the United States or Canadian Data Centers.

We perform scheduled site maintenance as part of ongoing efforts to improve the stability of our services. During these maintenance windows, you may experience limited access to the SurveyMonkey website, some of our other products, or your surveys, and respondents may have limited ability to take your surveys.

If you’re taking a survey: Responses are saved when you select Next or Done to submit the page. Responses on pages submitted before maintenance will be saved. However, responses on pages submitted during the scheduled site maintenance may not be saved.

Try taking the survey again after the planned maintenance period has ended. If you’re unable to, contact the person or company who sent you the survey—they might be able to open the survey back up by allowing response editing once maintenance is complete.

When is this happening?

We've selected a date and time to minimize the impact to most businesses, as we've found this is one of the least active periods for surveys and responses.

Date	Time
Saturday, November 7, 2026	Starting at 9 am PDT (5 pm UTC) for approximately 3 hours
After the maintenance

If you're not able to access our site after the planned maintenance has ended:

Clear your browser's cache and cookies.
Restart your browser (not just the tab).

If you're still having trouble viewing the site, you may need to add our domains and IP addresses to your allow list again. If you still need help, please contact us.

What will be impacted?

This planned site maintenance impacts customers whose survey data is stored in the United States or Canadian Data Centers and people taking surveys hosted in the United States or Canadian Data Centers.

Products that might be impacted	Products not impacted
- SurveyMonkey.com
- SurveyMonkey.ca
- help.surveymonkey.com (all products, including SurveyMonkey Apply, GetFeedback and Wufoo)
- SurveyMonkey app (Android, iOS)
- contribute.surveymonkey.com
- SurveyMonkey Anywhere app (Android, iOS)
- SurveyMonkey Rewards app (Android, iOS)
- SurveyMonkey integrations and developer portal(US/CAN)
- SurveyMonkey AudienceMarket Research Solutions
- Wufoo (Billing)
- All Product Marketing Sites (US/CAN)	- Wufoo (Login/Builder/Forms)
- GetFeedback (Direct and Digital)
- SurveyMonkey Apply


How should I plan?

Since SurveyMonkey surveys might be down during this time period, we recommend you postpone sending surveys until after this planned maintenance window. If you have a survey that will be open during this period, you may want to let survey takers know they should check back later if they can't get to your survey.

Scheduled emails: Any email invitations, follow-up, thank you, or reminder emails scheduled to be sent during this time will automatically be sent after the window ends.
Viewing data: Since exports and analyze features may be down, you may want to export your data ahead of time if you plan to present or work with survey data during this window.
What will people trying to take a survey see?

Visitors trying to view or submit a live survey during the maintenance window may see an error message letting them know our site is down and to try back later. This includes anyone trying to submit a survey through kiosk mode.

If you're using a white label url, the messaging won't have SurveyMonkey branding.

If you have your survey embedded on a website, people may see an error message during this window and may be unable to take your survey.

Will survey responses be saved?

All responses gathered before the maintenance window will be in your account afterwards. If someone begins taking your survey before maintenance begins, any survey pages they submit before the site maintenance begins will be saved.

Once maintenance has begun, respondents may briefly see a message letting them know our site is down when they select Next or Done on a survey. If your survey collector has response editing turned on, people can visit your survey after the window to finish their response.

Will this affect my automation, app, or integration with SurveyMonkey?

Yes. SurveyMonkey APIs may be intermittently available during this window, impacting all public, private apps, or integrations built on our developer platform with SurveyMonkey.

If you're a developer, any requests to the API during this window may return 503 errors. If you have workflows that use an automation to create email Invitations, SurveyMonkey may not receive those messages during the maintenance.

If you're a user of one of our partner apps or integrations, you may not be able to access those services or you may see an error message during this time.

Creating Surveys
Ranking & Rating Questions

Ranking Question

SurveyMonkey
Ranking Question

The Ranking question asks respondents to compare items to each other by placing them in order of preference. In the Analyze Results section, an average ranking is calculated for each answer choice, allowing you to quickly evaluate the most preferred answer choice.

Creating a Ranking Question

To add this question type:

Drag and drop Ranking into your survey from the Build section.
In the question text field, write instructions that ask respondents to rank the answer choices in order of preference, 1 being the highest. It may also help to include what all the choices have in common. For instance, "Rank the following ice cream flavors in order of preference, 1 being your most preferred flavor."
In the Ranking Choices fields, enter the answer options you want respondents to rank. You can add up to 250 answer options.
Configure any additional options.
Click Save.

TIP! Try to limit the number of ranking choices to about 5. Asking respondents to rank too many items in relation to each other can be overwhelming.

Add an N/A Option

Under the Edit tab, you can choose to add an N/A column, and customize the label. When you add an N/A option to a Ranking question, it will add an N/A checkbox at the end of each row. If a respondent selects an N/A checkbox, that row will be greyed out and will not be included in that respondent's ranking order.

It's important to make sure that even the lowest ranked options still apply to that respondent. If a respondent doesn't have the option to declare that a ranking item does not apply to them, they will be forced to include that choice in their rankings anyway, which might produce bad data.

Additional Options

Under the Options tab, you can further customize the question in the following ways:

Require an answer
Sort, randomize, or flip rows
Change the question size & layout
Enable question text A/B test

Learn more: Editing Questions

Survey Behavior

Before you send out your survey, preview your survey design to see what your survey will look like to respondents. Respondents can drag and drop answer choices in the order of preference. When the N/A option is enabled, you can also use the dropdowns to rank.

Analyzing Results

See example results (English only) »

Average Ranking

Ranking questions calculate the average ranking for each answer choice so you can determine which answer choice was most preferred overall. The answer choice with the largest average ranking is the most preferred choice.

The average ranking is calculated as follows, where:

w = weight of ranked position
x = response count for answer choice

1w1 + x2w2 + x3w3 ... xnwn
-----------------------
Total response count

Weights are applied in reverse. In other words, the respondent's most preferred choice (which they rank as #1) has the largest weight, and their least preferred choice (which they rank in the last position) has a weight of 1. You can't change the default weights.

For example, if a Ranking question has 5 answer choices, weights are assigned as follows:

The #1 choice has a weight of 5
The #2 choice has a weight of 4
The #3 choice has a weight of 3
The #4 choice has a weight of 2
The #5 choice has a weight of 1

We apply weights in this way to ensure that when the data is presented on a chart, it's clear which answer choice is most preferred.

If you chose to include an N/A option on the Ranking question, any N/A responses will not factor into the average ranking.

Charts

The Depth display option allows you to choose between the following options:

Weighted Average: Charts the average ranking for each answer choice
Distribution: Charts the absolute number or percentage of respondents that selected each answer choice

The chart types available depend on the question type, and the display options you configure. Learn more: Custom Charts & Data Tables

Sending Surveys

Ways to Send Your Survey

SurveyMonkey
Ways to Send Your Survey

Once you've finished your edits and previewed your survey design, access an automatically created Web link by clicking the green Publish survey button. Alternatively, you can select Publish survey in the survey header. Publish survey is where you can create feedback collectors and launch your survey.

Any collectors created on your survey can be managed from your collector list.

Before you can send your survey, you need to verify your account email address.

Video Overview
Ways to Send Your Survey

SurveyMonkey offers multiple collector types to send your survey, whether you're surveying your own respondents or purchasing responses.

Collector type	Description
Web link/
QR code	A URL or QR code linking to your survey so you can send or post your survey anywhere you want. Social icons let you post your survey on Facebook, LinkedIn, X, Whats' App, or Microsoft Teams.
Email invitation	Send customized email invitations to your contacts through SurveyMonkey to track who responds and send follow-up emails.
Website	Embed your survey or show a pop-up invitation to your survey on your website.
Manual data entry	Input responses collected offline or add responses for someone without an internet connection.
Mobile SDK	Get a survey hash used by app developers to add surveys to iOS or Android apps.
Kiosk survey	Collect responses without an internet connection through the SurveyMonkey Anywhere app.
Text message	Text your contacts a link to your survey. Respondents can tap the link to take your survey in their mobile browser.
Target audience*	If you don’t have your own list of respondents to get the feedback you need, you can buy responses through SurveyMonkey Audience.

*If you chose to purchase Audience responses when you initially created your survey, then you’ll automatically be prompted to set up a Target audience collector.

Using Multiple Collectors

You can create multiple collectors for any survey to get responses in various ways. Depending on your plan type, you may be limited to as few as 3 collectors per survey.

Note: If you're on a Basic plan and you've added paid features to your survey, you'll be prompted to Upgrade your account to send your survey as it’s designed. To send your survey without upgrading, you can click Paid features in the survey header to remove any paid features from the survey design, and then you can create a collector. 

Responses from all collectors opened for a survey get stored in the Analyze Responses section of the survey. To view the responses from a specific collector, filter by collector. Or, compare by collector to see a side-by-side comparison of how people responded by collector.

It isn’t recommended to create more than 200 collectors per survey. If you need more collectors, make a copy of your survey to create additional collectors. 

Why are some collectors view only or greyed out?

If a collector is grayed out, it's disabled for your survey. This may be because your survey is accepting payments, the survey was shared and you don't have Collect permissions, or the collector is restricted by Enterprise settings.

Managing Your Collector Options

Collector options are settings that let you customize the respondent's survey-taking experience. They affect who can take your survey, how many times they can take the survey, what people see when they complete it, and whether the results are anonymous.

Each collector type has a different set of options to choose from—specific collector type article have additional details.

TIP! Before you send your survey, create a test collector to make sure the collector options work as you expect.

Managing Your Collector List

Once your survey has collectors, go to the Send survey section to view and manage your collectors.

Click ... to the right of a collector to access these these collector action:

Action	Description
Close collector	Close a collector to stop the survey from collecting further responses from that source. If a respondent tries to access the survey, they'll see a survey closed message. If you have multiple collectors for the same survey, you need to close each collector individually to completely stop the survey from collecting responses.
Open collector	Re-open a collector that was previously closed to accept new survey responses.
Copy collector	Copy a Web link or an Email invitation collector to share past surveys at a different time or with new respondents. Not all collector options are copied—you can review all settings before sending your survey.
Edit collector	Update your collector options and settings to control the survey-taking experience.
Rename collector	Change the nickname of the collector to help you stay organized. The collector name is private—people taking your survey can't see it.
Delete all responses	Permanently delete responses recorded by the collector. If the collector is open, you can continue to use the collector to collect new responses.
Delete collector	Permanently delete the collector from the survey. Before you can delete it, you need to delete all responses.

If a respondent tries to access the survey, they'll see a message saying the URL may have changed or that the survey no longer exists. If you delete a collector with a Custom URL Ending, you may not be able to use it on a future collector.
Invite new recipients	Send an email invitation to new recipients or those who were added to the collector but not yet sent an invitation.
Resume recent draft	If you have an Email invitation drafted, Resume to edit your draft message or contact list.

Show Rules

SurveyMonkey
Show Rules

Show rules let you focus on specific parts of your survey results. Choose which pages or questions you want to see, and we'll hide the rest.

You can only create one show rule at a time.

Creating a Show Rule

To create a show rule:

Go to the Analyze Results section of your survey.
Select Rules from the toolbar, then click + Show.
Choose the criteria you want to focus on.
Click Apply. At the top of the page, you'll see the number of responses included in your rule compared to the total number of responses you received.

You'll see any active rules at the top of the page. We'll also show the number of responses included in your rule, compared to the number of responses in your survey.

Managing Show Rules

To manage show rules:

Select Rules from the toolbar.
Click the three dots menu next to a show rule to unapply, edit, rename, or delete it. You can't copy a show rule.

Click the name of the rule to turn it on or off. A green check mark ✅ next to a rule means that the rule is active. You'll also see any active rules at the top of the page.

Exporting & Sharing Show Rules

You can export your results with rules applied or share your survey results with other people.

Save multiple rules together as a view to easily access different sections of your data.
