Paste Your Content to Create a Survey

SurveyMonkey
Paste Your Content to Create a Survey

If you drafted your survey in a document and now need to program or import a pre-written survey into SurveyMonkey, you can paste your content all at once, instead of adding each question one by one.

To import a Google Form into a SurveyMonkey survey, use the SurveyMonkey for Google Forms add-on.

Create a Survey with Paste Your Content

You may need to reformat your document to recognize and properly create the Single textbox and Multiple choice questions. After adding questions this way, you can always edit and customize the output survey.

To create a survey via Paste your content:

Click Create survey.
Select Paste your content.
On the Import Questions screen,  copy and paste your Multiple choice or Single textbox questions and answer choices. Each question and answer choice needs to be on their own line.
Press Enter or Return on your keyboard twice to separate your questions. Each question must be separated by a blank line.
In the Preview section, view the questions you add in real time.
Once you have entered your questions, click Add Questions to create your survey.

Once the survey is drafted, you can give the survey a title, add different question types, edit or switch the question type, change the survey theme, add rich text formatting, and more.

Paste Content using AI

If you have your survey questions and answers already written outside of SurveyMonkey, simply Copy and paste your survey into SurveyMonkey and let AI do the rest.

Paste your content is powered by OpenAI/Azure OpenAI. We use machine learning and generative AI to convert your content into a survey to recognize the various survey elements within your document, of any format, and convert it into a survey.

To paste your survey content into SurveyMonkey:

Click Create survey. 
Select Paste your content as your starting point and click Create survey. 
To agree to use AI to create your survey, click Use AI. 
Copy your survey from your document and paste it into SurveyMonkey. Click Create survey.

Once your survey is created, be sure to review your survey. The import may result in inaccuracies and there may be limitations impacting the import. Review your survey design for accuracy, adjust any question types, add logic, or style your survey.

If you’re on the Basic (free) plan and your survey contains paid features, you’ll either need to upgrade to a paid plan or remove the paid features in order to send your survey.

Enabling Paste Your Content

When you choose Paste your content as your creation method, you need to select Use AI to utilize this feature. 

Paste your content will stay enabled and available to you until you clear your browser data. If you use a different device to access your survey, you will need to choose to Use AI from that device too to use Paste your content.

Limitations

At this time, any text formatting, titles or page descriptions, style elements, images or videos, page breaks, logic, and unsupported question types won’t be captured from your document and won't be imported. 

Your survey is created with the following question types: Multiple choice, Checkbox, Single Textbox, Comment box, Matrix/Rating scale, and Text.

A customer can paste and submit your survey up to 50 times per month.

Also, please don’t paste any sensitive information, like names, into SurveyMonkey. 

Usage is subject to SurveyMonkey's Acceptable Uses Policy, as well as additional third-party provider usage policies, and acceptable use and conduct policies.

Errors

If something goes wrong in converting your survey text to a survey, you’ll see an error message to provide you with info about what happened and what you can do.

How We Use Your Data

When Paste your content is enabled and used, your data is processed in the following ways: 

We use machine learning and generative AI to identify survey elements, format, and generate a survey from your pasted content within SurveyMonkey. 
We send the survey text you provide and an encrypted user ID to OpenAI or Azure OpenAI service to extract the survey structure, questions, text, comments, etc. and provide the feature.

Question & Page Randomization

SurveyMonkey
Question & Page Randomization

Using randomization can help reduce order bias and improve the quality of your data. One way to do that in SurveyMonkey is by using Question or Page Randomization to change the order in which people taking your survey see the questions.

Video Overview
Question Randomization

Question Randomization lets you change the order of any questions on a page in your survey. You can apply it to a specific set of questions, or all questions on the page.

Adding Question Randomization

To turn on Question Randomization:

Go to the Design Survey section.
Click Logic.
Click Question Randomization.
From the Select Page menu to choose the correct survey page and click Next.
For Format, Choose from the following options:
Randomize questions:questions will appear in a random order for each person taking your survey.
Flip questions:on average, half of the people taking your survey will see the question order flipped. For example, 3, 2, 1 or of 1, 2, 3.
For Questions Affected, apply to All questions on page or only Selected questions.
Click Apply to save.
(Optional) Repeat the steps to apply Question Randomization to other survey pages.

TIP! Use answer randomization to flip, sort, or randomize choices for an individual question.

Removing Question Randomization

To turn off Question Randomization:

Go to the Design Survey section.
Click Logic.
Click Question Randomization.
From the Select Page menu, choose the page you added randomization to.
For Format, select No Randomization.
Click Apply to save.
(Optional) Repeat the steps to remove Question Randomization from other survey pages.

If you have Skip Logic or Question & Answer Piping applied to your survey, using Question Randomization may lead to unexpected behavior.

Page Randomization

Page Randomization lets you rotate, flip, or randomize pages in your survey—all pages or a specific set of pages.

Adding Page Randomization:

To turn on Page Randomization:

Go to the Design Survey section.
Click Logic.
Click Page Randomization.
For Format choose from the following options:
Randomize pages: pages will appear in a random order for each new person taking your survey.
Flip pages: on average, half of the people taking your survey will see the page order flipped. For example, 3, 2, 1 or 1, 2, 3.
Rotate pages: the page order depends on what the previous person saw—the first page they saw is the last page the next person will see. For example,1, 2, 3, 4, 5, then 2, 3, 4, 5, 1, then 3, 4, 5, 1, 2.
For Pages Affected apply randomization to All pages in the survey or Selected pages.
Click Apply.

TIP! Block Randomization let's you randomize pages by group.

Removing Page Randomization

To turn off Page Randomization:

Go to the Design Survey section.
Click Logic.
Click Page Randomization.
For Format select No randomization.
Click Apply to save.

If you have Skip Logic or Question & Answer Piping applied to your survey, using Page Randomization may lead to unexpected behavior.

Showing Respondents Instant Results

SurveyMonkey
Showing Respondents Instant Results
Turning On Instant Results

Instant Results allows you to show your respondents a real-time summary of results when they complete the survey. This collector option is turned off, by default. You can turn on Instant Results from your collector options.

To turn on Instant Results:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Click the name of the collector and access the collector options. You may need to click Show advanced options.
Turn on Instant Results. Your changes are saved automatically.

TIP! Collectors are ways to send your survey. Each collector type works a little differently, so they all have different sets of options to choose from when you set them up. If you don't see this particular option in the collector type you're using, review the info on this page, and be sure to check out the help article about that collector type.

Previewing Instant Results

You can preview Instant Results by taking the survey through a test collector. When you preview your survey, you won't see Instant Results.

Who Sees Instant Results

Instant Results shows to respondents taking the survey through any collector where you turned on Instant Results. If you're using more than one collector to distribute your survey, you need to turn on Instant Results for each collector.

When Instant Results are turned on, any respondent who completes your survey by clicking the Done button at the end of the survey are directed to the Instant Results page.

If you added Skip Logic, Disqualification Logic, or Quotas to your survey, respondents who skip over questions in your survey may see Instant Results, depending on your logic settings. To ensure they don't see Instant Results, choose to close the survey window or to redirect respondents to a custom webpage.

Respondents can bookmark or copy and paste your Instant Results link and share it. To share a protected version of your survey results, create a password protected shared data page or results dashboard.

What Respondents See

Instant Results highlights the results of all the closed-ended questions collected at the time the respondent completed the survey or refreshed the page. See example »

If you added a Custom Thank You to your collector, your custom message appears at the top of the Instant Results page as long as the survey taker is logged into their SurveyMonkey account. If the survey taker isn’t logged in, the custom message doesn’t display on the Instant Results.

After clicking the secondary Done button at the bottom of the Instant Results page, respondents see the Survey End Page. Survey responses are submitted when a respondent clicks the Done button on the last page of your survey—respondents don't need to click the Done button on the Instant Results page to submit their responses.

Removing SurveyMonkey Branding

White Label URL

Paid feature
Log in to see if this feature is included in your plan.
Log in
Sign up free

You can remove SurveyMonkey branding that appears on the Instant Results page if you're using the White Label URL (research.net) on your collector.

Display Limitations

Instant Results is intended to be a quick snapshot of your survey results, so there are some display limitations to consider:

Instant Results doesn't display individual responses or open-ended responses, including Slider question responses.
Instant Results doesn't display if you add an image to an answer choice field.
Instant Results doesn't display for surveys with more than 15 closed-ended questions.
Instant Results doesn't display for surveys with more than 10,000 responses.
When you hit your account's response limit, Instant Results won't show any new responses.
Instant Results doesn’t display when using a Website Collector.
Instant Results doesn't display when using Kiosk Mode.
After you collect 100 responses, Instant Results may take up to 15 minutes to refresh and include new responses.
Edits you make to your survey design or collector options may take up to 15 minutes to display on the Instant Results page.
The chart types and display options used for Instant Results cannot be customized.
All variables included in any A/B tests you used may display on Instant Results.

TIP! To share more than 15 questions, customize charts, share open-ended responses, choose the questions you share, and more, you can create a shared data page to share your survey results.

SurveyMonkey Audience Panel

SurveyMonkey Audience Custom Balancing

SurveyMonkey
SurveyMonkey Audience Custom Balancing

Custom balancing lets you choose the breakdown of your responses in a SurveyMonkey Audience project. When you're getting responses from our Contribute, Rewards, or Global panel, you can use custom balancing to choose the distribution of completed responses you want from each gender or age group you're targeting. For example, get 80% of your completed responses from female respondents and 20% from male respondents.

To use custom balancing:

Create a Targeted Audience collector.
Under Basic Demographics, click Age or Gender.
Choose the Custom option. Any previously selected age or gender criteria is removed so you can use the custom balancing tool.
For Gender, use the slider scale to pick the percentage of responses you want from males and females.
For Age, click Edit and enter the minimum and maximum age range for each group you're looking to survey. You can target 2–8 different age groups. Next enter the percentage of complete responses you want from each group (the percentages must total 100%). Each age range should be 5 years or more (18–23 works, but 18–21 doesn't), and age groups can't overlap (you can't have both 18-30 and 25-35 as age groups). Click Save once you're done.
Take a look at your Project Details on the right side of the page to review your custom balancing selections and the additional cost per response.

TIP! Custom balancing restricts the pool of available people to take your survey, so you may have to buy a larger number of completed responses than you need. The exact number is variable and depends on: the number of age group, the size of each age group, the percentage of responses for each age group, and any custom gender balancing.

Completed Responses

Due to the nature of the system, the variability of response rates, and natural margin of error, we can't guarantee that you'll get the exact number of completed responses that you specified per gender and age. There's a fault tolerance of ±5 responses per gender group and age group. Read more about completed responses.

Using Both Age and Gender Balancing

You can use both custom age and gender balancing at the same time. When you do that, we combine the percentage of both gender and age balancing to determine the distribution of responses from each gender against each age group.

Let's say you're buying 500 completed responses and choose the following custom gender and age balancing settings:

Gender: Female 75%, Male 25%
Age: 18–29: 30%, When you do that, we combine the percentage of both gender and age balancing to determine the number of completed responses your project will receive: 70%

With these custom gender and age balancing options, the system calculates how many responses each gender + age group will get like this:

Completed Responses (500) * Female Responses (75%) * 18-29 Age Group (30%) = 113 responses
Completed Responses (500) * Female Responses (75%) * 30–39 Age Group (70%) = 263 responses
Completed Responses (500) * Male Responses (25%) * 18-29 Age Group (30%) = 38 responses
Completed Responses (500) * Male Responses (25%) * 30–39 Age Group (70%) = 88 responses

Sentiment Analysis

SurveyMonkey
Sentiment Analysis

Paid Feature: Sentiment analysis is available on some paid plans in the US and EU data centers. 

Sentiment analysis helps you understand the feeling or attitude expressed in your respondents' answers. It analyzes what people write and shows whether it's positive, negative, or neutral. Analyze the sentiment of any open-text question, except Multiple textboxes questions.

Video Overview
Using Sentiment Analysis

Sentiment analysis is on by default and analyzes all eligible responses from open-ended questions in your survey. If you turn it off, sentiments will be removed from all survey questions.

To view Sentiments analysis, scroll to an open text question on the Question summaries tab. From the dropdown in the question, go to the Responses tab to see how people feel.

Responses are categorized as Positive, Neutral, Negative, or Undetected, and a corresponding icon appears next to each response. If a response is categorized as Undetected, we didn't have enough information to categorize it.

If you need to edit a response's sentiment to be more accurate, hover over the sentiment icon next to the response you want to edit and select a new sentiment icon.

Turning Sentiment Analysis On or Off

To turn Sentiment Analysis on or off:

Go Analyze results.
Select Options from the top toolbar.
From the menu, select Data options.
Toggle Sentiment analysis.
Filtering by Sentiment

You can filter responses by sentiment within a question or across your entire survey.

Expand | Collapse
Filtering within a question

When you filter by sentiment within a question, you only see responses of that sentiment. For example, you can only see responses from people who responded positively.

To Filter by sentiment within a question:

Go to Analyze results.
Scroll to a question with text responses.
From the Responses tab, Filter by sentiment.
Select which sentiments you want to display.
Select Apply.

This shows you only responses categorized with that sentiment. You can also choose to display any responses with undetected sentiments.

Filtering across a survey

When you filter by sentiment across a survey, you're displaying responses to each question in your survey from people who responded to a question with a specific sentiment. For example, you can see how people who responded negatively to a question responded to the rest of your survey.

To filter by sentiment across an entire survey, create a Filter rule to Filter by sentiment.

Exporting Sentiments

You can export your survey with all responses or an individual question’s sentiment only. 

To export your survey results with all responses, with sentiment included:

Go to Analyze results.
Select Export from the top toolbar, and select + New export.
Select Question summaries, and choose XLS or CSV file format.
Select Open-ended responses, and select Export.
When your download is ready, a brief notification to Download appears to export the file to your computer. You can also find your files for 14 days by selecting Export and choosing Previous exports.

To export an individual question with sentiment included:

Go to Analyze results.
Find a question that uses Sentiment analysis.
Select the Export icon at the top of the tile.
Select PDF or XLS, or select More options to select CSV file format.
Select Export. When your download is ready, a brief notification to Download appears to export the file to your computer. You can also find your files for 14 days by selecting Export and choosing Previous exports.

Question Bank

SurveyMonkey
Question Bank

Question Bank is a library containing hundreds of questions you can add to your survey in seconds. These questions are written and certified by our very own survey methodologists. It's available to all SurveyMonkey customers—all you need to get started is a SurveyMonkey account and a survey to play around with.

Tip! Consider creating a Custom Question Bank for your team.

Browsing Questions

To browse Question Bank:

Go to the Design Survey section of your survey.
Click Question bank.
Click a category to open the Question Bank browser.
Search for questions by keyword or click Filters to refine the results by tags.

TIP! We also have pre-written survey templates you can use to create a survey. When browsing Question Bank, you'll see survey templates that use the types of questions you're browsing.

Adding Questions

To add a question:

Open the Question Bank browser.
Drag and drop or just click a question to add it to the preview.
In the preview, drag and drop questions in the order you'd like them.
Click + Add Questions.

Expand | Collapse
Why can't I re-order or delete questions?

If your questions are in a grey box in the Question Bank preview, it means you've already added them to your survey. Close the Question Bank browser to move them or delete them.

How do I put questions on different pages of the survey?

Once you close the Question Bank browser, you can add pages to your survey design and move questions wherever you'd like.

Editing Questions

Question Bank questions are written and certified by survey methodologists. Certain questions can be customized without the loss of certification—if you see drop-down menus in the question text, click to see options that may better fit the context of your survey. However, if you make additional edits to the wording of the question, it'll lose its certification and associated badge.

Badges

After you add a Question Bank question to your survey, you'll see it has a little badge when you hover over the question in your survey design. The badge is just for your reference—it means your question is certified and in some cases who we partnered with to write it—and it doesn't show to respondents.

Benchmarks

The benchmarks badge indicates whether a question is benchmarkable. Look for it when adding questions from Question Bank and turn on free Global Benchmarks or purchase Industry Benchmarks and view them in your survey results.

Your response data from any eligible Question Bank questions will be contributed to benchmarks on an de-identified and aggregated basis. You can opt out of benchmarks at any time by changing your privacy settings.

Restrictions
Feature
	
Restriction

Question and Answer Piping	You can pipe from a Question Bank question into a question you created. However, you can't pipe into a Question Bank question.
A/B Test	You can't add this feature to a Question Bank question.
Sort, Randomize, Flip Choices	You can't add this feature to a Question Bank question.
Add "Other" Comment Box	You can't add this feature to a Question Bank question.
Survey Language	Question Bank is only available when your survey language is set to English, German, Portuguese, Japanese, Spanish, French, Dutch, Italian, Danish, Russian or Korean.

Account Response Limits

SurveyMonkey
Account Response Limits

Each SurveyMonkey plan comes with a set number of responses a user, or team of users, can view. These limits work differently depending on your plan and billing cycle. To compare offerings, see plans and pricing.

TIP! A response is one survey takers’ submission to a survey. A response may have any status, including incomplete or deleted.

Per-Survey Limits

With per-survey response limits, you can view a set number of responses per survey according to your plan. To see a survey’s response count, go to Home.

Responses over the survey’s limit aren’t viewable and will be deleted. However, if you need access to specific over-limit responses to comply with legal obligations, such as to fulfill a data subject request, then please contact customer support.

You can immediately delete these responses over your account limit or we will automatically delete them 1 year after they were collected.

TIP! To view and keep access to all of your responses, upgrade to a paid plan.

Self-Serve Monthly and Annual Limits

If your plan has an account response limit, responses across all surveys are combined and counted each billing cycle. Unused responses do not roll over. If you exceed survey responses in a billing cycle, there will be an additional $0.15 USD charge per response:

All responses, including ones you delete, count towards your overage. 
You’ll receive a separate invoice for Billable Responses at your next billing date. 
You’re billed automatically to the payment method on file on the start date of the next billing cycle. Your next subscription and your overages are billed at the same time but as two separate charges. 
The response count is set back to 0 at the start of the next billing cycle or when your renewal invoice is paid.

TIP! You can check your response count from My Account. The charge per billable response depends on the currency in which you pay for your plan. 

Enterprise Annual Limits

Enterprise plans have annual response limits. Contact sales or your CSM to learn more about this option.

SurveyMonkey Audience Responses

SurveyMonkey Audience responses are not included in SurveyMonkey plans—this is a separate service you can use to buy respondents to take your survey.

Learn more: Buying Survey Responses

Per-Survey Limits

With per-survey response limits, you can view a set number of responses per survey according to your plan. To see a survey’s response count, go to Home.

Responses over the survey’s limit aren’t viewable and will be deleted. However, if you need access to specific over-limit responses to comply with legal obligations, such as to fulfill a data subject request, then please contact customer support.

You can immediately delete these responses over your account limit or we will automatically delete them 1 year after they were collected.

TIP! To view and keep access to all of your responses, upgrade to a paid plan.

Self-Serve Monthly and Annual Limits

If your plan has an account response limit, responses across all surveys are combined and counted each billing cycle. Unused responses do not roll over. If you exceed survey responses in a billing cycle, there will be an additional $0.15 USD charge per response:

All responses, including ones you delete, count towards your overage. 
You’ll receive a separate invoice for Billable Responses at your next billing date. 
You’re billed automatically to the payment method on file on the start date of the next billing cycle. Your next subscription and your overages are billed at the same time but as two separate charges. 
The response count is set back to 0 at the start of the next billing cycle or when your renewal invoice is paid.

TIP! You can check your response count from My Account. The charge per billable response depends on the currency in which you pay for your plan. 

Enterprise Annual Limits

Enterprise plans have annual response limits. Contact sales or your CSM to learn more about this option.

SurveyMonkey Audience Responses

SurveyMonkey Audience responses are not included in SurveyMonkey plans—this is a separate service you can use to buy respondents to take your survey.

Learn more: Buying Survey Responses

Tagging Responses

SurveyMonkey
Tagging Responses

Tagging Responses

Paid feature
Log in to see if this feature is included in your plan.
Log in
Sign up free

Create tags to categorize responses to questions with open-ended text responses. You can create rule-based tags, or tag responses manually. 

Once you add tags to your responses, they'll be visible in the survey's Question summaries tab or when viewing individual responses.

Rule-based Tagging

Enterprise Feature: This feature is only available in English and for Enterprise customers. Please contact our sales team to learn more.

Rule-based tagging lets you automatically tag responses based on keywords or phrases. For example, if there is a certain word in your responses you want tagged, the created rule will tag existing responses and any new responses that come in.

Rule-based tagging uses word stemming to find the root of your keyword. This allows us to tag other versions of it. For example, if you create a rule for the keyword Caused, we'll also look for Cause and Causing.

Tip! You can easily tell the tags apart by looking at them. Rule-based tags have colored outlines, while manual tags are filled in with color.

To create a rule-based tag from the Responses tab: 

In the Analyze results section, scroll to a question with open-ended text responses.
Go to the Responses tab.
In the Search Responses bar, enter keyword(s) or phrase(s). Your responses automatically filter.
Select + Create Tag.
(Optional) Edit tag label and color.
Select Save. 

To create a rule-based tag from the Theme management tab:

In the Analyze results section, scroll to a question with open-ended text responses.
Go to Theme management.
Select +New Theme.
In the Tag name bar, specify the name and color of the tag.
In the Keywords bar, enter the keyword(s) or phrase(s) to be automatically tagged.
Select Save.

Tip! Use the table of rules below to help you search for even more specific words or phrases.

Using Rules
Rules	Description	Examples
Response matches exact phrase	Use quotation marks to search for exact phrases. Search results must match exactly what you type between the quotes.	"yellow flowers"
Response matches multiple keywords or phrases	Type AND between words or exact phrases to find responses that match both words and/or phrases	rose AND carnation AND "yellow flower"
Response matches either keyword or phrase	Type OR between words or exact phrases to find responses that match either words or phrases.	rose OR carnation OR “red flower”
Response does not include	Type NOT directly in front of any word or phrase that you want to exclude from your search.	red flower NOT rose
Response starts with	Type * after a word to search responses starting with those letters.	flow* (results will show flows, flowers, flowing)
Response includes a typo	To locate responses that may include a typo, type part of the word, then ~, followed by the number of characters in the word.	flo~3 (to find responses with flower, but the word has typos like, flwoer, fleowr, folwer)

carn~5 (to find responses with carnation, but the word has typos like, carntaion, carnaiton, carntiaon)
Response combines the above rules	Use a combination of AND, OR, or NOT rules to search responses.	(red AND rose) OR (yellow AND rose)  AND NOT carnation
Manual Tagging

If you don’t want responses tagged automatically, you also have the option to tag responses one by one. To create tags for different forms of the same word, consider using Rule-based tagging instead (English only).

To create a manual tag:

Go to the Responses tab.
Use the checkboxes to select one or more responses.
Select the Tag button and choose an existing tag or create a new one.
Select Apply.
Managing Tags

To remove an applied tag from the Responses tab, select Clear next to the name of the tag.

The Theme management tab shows all the tags you created. You can edit, delete, or create new themes from this tab.

If a response is edited, any tags applied to that response will be removed.

Filtering by Tags

You can filter text responses by tag—either within a question or across your entire survey.

Expand | Collapse
Filtering within a question

When you filter by tag within a question, you're displaying all of that question's responses with a specific tag. For example, if you want to only see the responses you tagged "yellow flowers".

To filter by tags within a question:

Go to Analyze results.
Scroll to a question with text responses.
Go to the Responses tab.
Select Filter: by tag.
Select which tags you want to display.
Select Apply.
Filtering across a survey

When you filter by tag across a survey, you're displaying responses to every question in your survey from people who responded to a question with a specific tag. For example, if you tagged responses with "Complaint" and wanted to see how those people responded to the rest of your survey.

To filter by tag across an entire survey, create a Filter rule to filter by tag.

Exporting Tags

Exports

Paid feature
Log in to see if this feature is included in your plan.
Log in
Sign up free

You can export open-ended responses, as well as any tags you've added. To export survey results, you need a paid plan.

Expand | Collapse
Exporting an individual question

To export a single question and any tags applied:

Go to Analyze results.
Scroll to a question with text responses.
At the top of the question, select + Export or the download icon.
Select PDF or XLS format, or select More options for CSV format and export options.
Select Filters and rules.
Select Export.
Exporting all questions

If you tagged responses on multiple questions with text responses, you can export all questions and tags at once.

To export all questions and corresponding tags:

Go to Analyze results.
From the top toolbar, select Export, then + New export.
Choose an export format: PDF, PPT, XLS, or CSV.
Select Include open-ended responses and Filters and rules.
Select Export.
Exporting a tag

To export all responses with a specific tag added:

Go to Analyze results.
Create a Filter rule to filter by tags.
Create a Show rule to display the individual question.
Create a Saved view including both rules.
Export the Saved view.

Slack Integration

GetFeedback
Slack Integration

See your survey responses in real-time using our Slack integration. Your messages can display a custom subject line, the survey title, and the specific response that came through directly within a Slack channel message.

There are few different use cases where you might like to send a Slack message out as a notification:

Notify CSM of low CX score
Notify CSM manager upon escalation
Create a high scoring lead notification for sales/BDR
Create churn notification for CSM
Create support notification for technical help
Escalate support notification
Slack for Web, App, and Email Surveys

Push feedback from your web, app, and email surveys to Slack channels. You can integrate Slack with your surveys in both app.usabilla.com and app.getfeedback.com.

Connecting to Slack

To connect your account to Slack:

Go to Insights. From app.getfeedback.com or app.usabilla.com, select Insights from the left sidebar.
In the left sidebar, select the person icon, then select Integrations.
In the upper-right corner, select New Connection.
Name your connection, then select Add Connection.
Follow the prompts to connect your Slack account.

Once you’re connected, you’ll see your Slack connection listed on the Integrations page.

Setting up Slack Notifications

To set up Slack notifications:

On the left sidebar, select Automations.
Select New Automation.
Name the automation. This name will be visible in Slack.
Select Slack Notifications.
Select Continue to Data.
In the Data section, find the form you want to receive response notifications from. You can select multiple forms.
Select Continue to Conditions.
In the Conditions section, select All Responses or Responses that match conditions.
All Responses: you’ll get a Slack notification every time someone submits a response to the form you’ve selected.
Responses that match conditions: set logic and conditions to get Slack notifications for specific kinds of responses. For example, you can set conditions to only receive Slack notifications for responses with low NPS scores.
If you’re setting up notifications based on conditions, you’ll choose which data source, type of information, and logic you want notifications to be based on. You can add multiple conditions.
Slack for Email Survey Feedback (app.getfeedback.com)

Integrate your email, Salesforce, and Zendesk surveys with Slack. This integration is separate from the Insights integration and only works with app.,getfeedback.com surveys.

The app.getfeedback.com Slack integration can’t be used in private Slack channels.

Connecting app.getfeedback.com to Slack

To connect to Slack:

In app.getfeedback.com, select Integrations > Slack > Add connection.
Select Allow to add the integration to your Slack workspace.
Setting Up Slack Notifications

Slack notifications can’t be added to private channels.

To set up your notifications:

In app.getfeedback.com, go to your survey and select Actions. Make sure you’re in Draft mode.
Name the action.
Add a condition that triggers the notification. You can set conditions for:
The answer to a specific question
Merge fields
Response language
To add another condition, select Add Condition.
Select Post to Slack in the Select an option dropdown. If Post to Slack is selected before the integration is configured, you’ll see an error message.
Choose the Slack workspace you’ll post to. If you have only one Slack Workspace, we’ll select it for you.
Choose where to post the Slack Message: in a DM or public channel.
Check the box labeled Include Question and Responses in Slack Message.
Enter your Slack message.
Check the box labeled Include Questions and Responses in Slack Message if you'd like to show the text of the response notification.
Legacy Integration (app.usabilla.com)

This information is for our legacy Slack Integration. It applies to app.usabilla.com web buttons only.

To use the legacy Slack integration:

Make sure you’re logged in to Slack.
In app.usabilla.com, go to the Integrations page.
Select Slack.
Choose the button you want to set up the integration for.
Choose when you want a message to be pushed to Slack.
Select Add to Slack.
In the popup, select the Slack channel you want to post feedback in.
Select Authorize.

Your Slack integration is now set up. Feedback that matches your criteria will be pushed to your Slack channel.

Removing a Legacy Slack Integration

To remove a legacy integration:

In app.usabilla.com, go to the Integrations page.
Scroll to the Slack integrations section.
Select the integration, then select Remove integration.

Survey Permissions to Shared Surveys

SurveyMonkey
Survey Permissions to Shared Surveys

When a survey is shared, people are given a level of access to each section of the survey. A team member's default access level is determined by their seat type, but it may be possible to edit the level of permissions someone has. The highest level of access available to people outside of your team is View Only.

Default Access Levels

Each person you share with is given the highest level of access by default, based on their seat type's permissions.

Seat type	Default access levels
Enterprise user or Full Access seats
(Primary Admin and Full User roles)	Design Survey—Full Access
Collect Responses—Full Access
Analyze Results—Full Access
Contributor seats
(Analyst)	Design Survey—View Only
Collect Responses—View Only
Analyze Results—Full Access
People not on your team	Design Survey—View Only
Collect Responses—View Only
Analyze Results—View Only

While sharing a survey, you can click the Edit permissions icon to update the default access levels for each section of the survey for Full Users and Admins or Analysts you selected.

If you don't have any Analysts selected to share with, and you want to assign different access levels to each Full Access seat, select Set individual permissions and click the Edit permissions icon. You won't see this option if you have Analysts selected to share a survey with, but you can always Edit permissions later.

Managing Permissions

Depending on your plan type or your Team Sharing settings, you may or may not be able to edit the level of access other team members have to each section of the survey.

Access Levels: Design Survey
Access Level
	
Description

Full Access	Full Access permissions to view, create, edit, or delete anything in the Design Survey section.
View Only	People with View Only permissions can view the Design Survey section but can't see most survey settings like options, logic, or question settings. They also can't edit or delete anything in the Design Survey section.
Viewing Edits in Shared Surveys

You need to refresh the Design Survey page to see other people's changes.

There isn't a way to track changes, view live collaborative editing, revert changes, or see who's currently editing the survey.

TIP! Get feedback without giving access. Invite someone to comment on your survey design if you want to get feedback without giving them access to your survey in their account.

Access Levels: Collect Responses
Access Level
	
Description

Full Access *	Full permissions to view, create, edit, or delete anything in the Collect Responses section.

This access level is only available when Analyze Results is also set to Full Access.
View Only *	People can view the collector list and some information in each collector, but they can't edit collector options or send the survey to get responses.
No Access	No Access to the Collect Responses section.

* People you share your survey with may run into access level limitations due to certain collector type exceptions.

Exceptions
Expand | Collapse
Email Invitation and Text Message Collectors

Since contacts are unique to an account, only the creator of the Email Invitation and Text Message collectors can make edits and export contacts by CSV —even when you transfer a survey. Any shared Email Invitation or Text Message collectors will be View Only.


People can see the survey results from Email Invitation and Text Message collectors, as long as they have the right permissions for the Analyze Results section.

Web Link Collectors

People with View Only permissions to the Collect Responses section see a version of the survey link where the URL ending is replaced with asterisks (*). This is to prevent anyone without Full Access permissions from sharing the link to get responses.

Website Collector

People with View Only permissions to the Collect Responses section can't view Website Collectors (Popup Surveys, Popup Invitations, and Embedded Surveys). People need Full Access permissions to view Website collectors.

Transferred surveys with email collectors

If a survey with an Email invitation created is transferred, the new owner is granted Edit access to the collector.

Even if the original and new account share Contacts, recipient data is not overwritten when a survey is transferred.

The new owner of the transferred survey and collector can view and delete recipients from the collector, but they cannot edit the recipient data in the email collector.

Access Levels: Analyze Results
Access Level
	
Description

Full Access	Full permissions to view, create, edit, or delete anything in the Analyze Results section.

People will see any rules, saved views, custom charts, shared data pages, exports, or text analysis created by the survey owner or any others with Full Access permissions. You need to refresh the Analyze Results page to see other people's edits to the Analyze Results section.

Full Access in Analyze Results is only available when Collect Responses is also set to Full Access.
View Only	People can view the survey results in the Original View only.

People won't see any rules, saved views, custom charts, shared data pages, exports, or text analysis created by the survey owner or others, and they can't make any changes or create exports.
No Access	No Access to the Analyze Results section.

TIP! Share results with anyone! To share your survey results with a wider audience, create a shared data page or results dashboard and share the link anywhere.

Analyzing Results

Analyzing Results
Understanding Your Results

How to Analyze Results

View your results from the Analyze Results section of a survey. You can see a summary view of your data; browse individual responses; create custom charts; use filters to focus on specific data views and segments; and easily download your results in multiple formats.

Viewing Individual Responses

To view how a particular respondent answered your survey, click the Individual Responses tab in your survey results. At the top of each response, you'll see some respondent metadata, which is outlined in this article.

Survey Response Statuses

A survey response is one respondent's submission of a survey, whether they completed the survey or only partially completed it. In the Individual Responses tab of your survey results, each response has one of the following statuses: Complete, Partial, Disqualified, or Over Quota.

Missing Survey Responses

Responses are recorded in the Analyze Results section of your survey. Read these tips if you think you're missing some responses.

Response Quality

Response Quality uses machine learning to scan your survey results and flag low-quality responses.

Respondents Skipped Required Questions

When you analyze your results, you may see that some respondents skipped required questions. The respondent may have exited the survey early, skip logic may have skipped the respondent past the question, or the respondent may have taken the survey before you added the required question.

Thematic Analysis

Apply themes to responses to review and filter text responses quickly. This feature uses AI to apply themes with ease.

Analyze Multiple Surveys Together

Analyze results from multiple surveys and track data over time. Combine multiple surveys, perform longitudinal analysis on recurring surveys, and visualize questions in multiple ways - all in one place.

Get Quick Insights with Analyze with AI

Analyze with AI, powered by OpenAI, helps you quickly uncover insights in your survey results.

Insights

View how Insights automatically summarizes your survey data into key takeaways, common themes, and sentiments to help you analyze results faster.

Text Responses

Analyzing Text Responses

Find insights and trends in your text responses by tagging responses, creating a word cloud, or automatically detecting the sentiment behind each response.

Sentiment Analysis

Sentiment Analysis automatically categorizes your text responses to reveal the emotion behind what people are saying.

Word Cloud

Use the word cloud to see a visual representation of the most common words and phrases from your survey responses.

Tagging Responses

Create tags to categorize responses on questions with open-ended responses.

Viewing a Specific Comment in the Analysis

From the Individual Responses tab, view a respondent's specific comments. From the Question Summaries tab, click Responses to see a list of open-ended comments.

Thematic Analysis

Apply themes to responses to review and filter text responses quickly. This feature uses AI to apply themes with ease.

Charts & Data Tables

Chart Types

You can choose one of several chart types for each of your questions and customize the chart and data table for a question. The chart types available depend on the question type.

Customizing Charts and Data Tables

Charts, data tables, and basic statistics can be created for all closed-ended survey questions. Edit the display options to fine-tune the way your data displays—combine or hide answer choices or edit chart colors or labels.

Combining or Hiding Answer Choices

You can combine or hide answer choices in a chart for closed-ended question types with a single answer choice allowed.

Basic Statistics

Basic statistics show you the minimum, maximum, mean, median, and standard deviation for a closed-ended question. Basic statistics appear in a separate data table below the question chart

Statistical Significance

Turn on statistical significance while adding a Compare Rule to a question in your survey. Examine the data tables for the questions in your survey to see if there are statistically significant differences in how different groups answered the survey.

Can I assign numerical values to answer choices?

Display basic statistics to see the minimum, maximum, mean, median, and standard deviation for a question. You can also assign numerical values to answer choices for some question types.

Insights and Data Trends

Use Data Trends to assess how responses have changed over time. Send the same survey multiple times and see how responses compare.

Crosstab Reports

Crosstab reports let you choose questions and answer choices to display in a data table for easy comparison across multiple questions, and share them with other people.

Filters & Views

Using Rules to Break Down Survey Results

Filter, compare, and show rules allow you to break down your survey results and focus in on specific subsets of your data, so you can analyze your results in a way that's most meaningful to you.

Filtering Survey Results

Filter rules allow you to break down your survey results and focus on specific parts of your data.

Comparing Survey Results

Compare rules let you choose two or more answer options from a single question and view them as a side-by-side comparison.

Creating Views

A view is snapshot of your survey data made up of any rules that you apply to your survey results. You can create a Saved View to easily see sections of your data at any time, without having to recreate them.

Show Rules

Use show rules to focus on specific parts of your survey results.

Filtering by Open-Ended Comments or Text

You can Filter by Question and Answer to filter textboxes or comment boxes by specific words or phrases.

Excluding Respondents who Skipped Questions

Exclude respondents from survey results who skipped particular questions. Create a Filter by Question and Answer and select every answer choice—this removes respondents who didn't answer the question.

Sharing Results

Sharing Survey Results

Learn how to share your survey results, depending on how much access you want to give to other people and how much you'd like to customize your presentation.

Shared Data Pages

Create shared data pages to share your survey results and charts online. You can control who can access your shared data page and what data you want to include.

Results Dashboards

Create a customizable dashboard to present your survey results and insights. Add charts and text, then share your dashboard with anyone.

Getting Feedback on Surveys and Results

You can invite others to give feedback on your survey design by sharing your survey preview link or sending an invite to comment. Once you collect survey responses, you can use a Shared Data Page to invite others to give feedback on your survey results.

Exporting Results

Exporting Survey Results

Export survey data to download an offline copy of your survey results. There are several export formats: PDF, PPT, XLS, CSV, and SPSS

Export Examples

We have several export examples available if you want to see how an export looks before downloading. At this time, examples are available in English only.

XLS (Excel) Exports

Export your survey results to an Excel spreadsheet. The Summary Data export includes data tables with response counts and percentages per question. The Responses Data export breaks down results by respondent.

CSV Exports

Export your survey results to a CSV spreadsheet. The All Summary Data export includes data tables with response counts and percentages per question.

PDF Exports

Export your survey results as a PDF with charts and data tables. PDF exports are ideal for printing and sharing since they require no additional analysis or editing. Export all results or the results of an individual question or respondent.

PPT (PowerPoint) Exports

Export your survey results as a PowerPoint presentation to share with your friends or colleagues. The export includes charts and data tables.

Exporting Charts

Create custom charts of your data and download them to your computer or share them online.

SPSS Exports

Export your survey results to an SAV file to use in SPSS, a popular computer program used for statistical analysis.

Troubleshooting Exports

Many formatting issues are resolved by using the Text Import Wizard to open a CSV. Format cells to change the date or number format.

Exporting an Individual Question

You can download the chart and data of an individual question. Click Save As from the top-right of the question in the Question Summary tab.

Benchmarks

Benchmarks

Benchmarks give context to your survey results by allowing you to compare your results to others who used the same Question Bank questions as you.

Applying Logic

Page Skip Logic

SurveyMonkey
Page Skip Logic

You can apply Page Skip Logic to a page so that everyone that reaches the page is skipped to a specific destination later in the survey—like a later page or the end of the survey. Unlike Question Skip Logic, Page Skip Logic doesn't depend on respondents' answers to specific questions—it's simply activated when a respondent reaches that page, and clicks Next. If you have the Advanced Branching feature instead, it replaces Page Skip Logic, so you'll need to use Advanced Branching instead to achieve the same effect.

Video Overview

Adding Logic

To add Page Logic:

Go to the Design Survey section of your survey.
At the top of the survey page, click the Page Logic button.
Select Page skip logic from the menu.
If you don't see this option, you may have Advanced Branching instead, which replaces Page Skip Logic.
Choose one of the page options (described below).

To remove Page Skip Logic, follow the above steps to open the Page Skip Logic tab. Then click Clear from the right of the blue bar.

Test your logic! Preview the survey to test all possible logic paths before sending it out. Responses aren't recorded when previewing.

Page Options

You can choose one of the following pages to send respondents to:

Any page number - This will skip respondents to the designated page. You must move respondents forward through the survey, and not backward.
End of Survey - This will send respondents directly to the end of the survey, which will activate the Survey End Page you specified in the collector options. Their response will be considered COMPLETE when you view their individual response in the Analyze Results section.
Disqualify Respondent - This will send respondents to a disqualification page. You can customize the disqualification page in the Collector Options. Their response will be considered DISQUALIFIED when you view their individual response in the Analyze Results section.
Details
Skip Logic takes effect when a respondent clicks the Next button to advance through the survey.
Question Skip Logic overrides Page Skip Logic if both are applied on the same page.
It's important to only move respondents forward in a survey—if you send respondents backwards, it could create an endless loop and prevent them from completing the survey.
When Skip Logic is applied, we automatically renumber question and page numbers, if you have numbering turned on.
Troubleshooting

Enhanced Sensitive Data Protection

SurveyMonkey
Enhanced Sensitive Data Protection

Enterprise Feature: If you're interested, contact sales. If you already have an Enterprise account, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Enhanced Sensitive Data Protection Features
Is the Enhanced Sensitive Data Protection (ESDP) right for me?

If you are using SurveyMonkey to collect personal data (generally any information that can be linked to a specific individual, such as an individual’s name and/or contact details combined with sensitive information about that individual received), the Enhanced Sensitive Data Protection (ESDP) feature offers additional security benefits when using SurveyMonkey.

If you are a HIPAA “covered entity” (as defined by HIPAA), visit HIPAA Compliance and SurveyMonkey for more information on how you can collect and manage Protected Health Information through surveys.

Feature List
Feature	Action to keep data secure
Security reminders	We remind users with in-product messages that appear whenever they perform certain operations, such as exporting survey data that could potentially be shared with third parties.
Automatic logoff	We timeout user sessions after 30 minutes of inactivity.
Account safeguarding	We implement faster removal of data when an account is deleted.
Security Measures that SurveyMonkey Employs

We implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards that reasonably and appropriately protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the electronic data that we receive, maintain, and transmit.

These safeguards include:

Regular risk assessments of systems to ensure that safeguards remain relevant and effective.
Screening, authorization, and training of SurveyMonkey staff who come into contact with customer information.
Data backup plans.
Disaster recovery plans.
Systems are regularly monitored, updated, and patched.
Incident response plan that includes reporting of security incidents to affected covered entities.
All communications with SurveyMonkey servers encrypted with SSL.

For more information, see our Security Statement.

Enabling ESDP Features

[Enterprise only feature] If you're interested in adding ESDP to your account, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) directly.

Downgrades

Review the common questions below to understand how downgrades work for ESDP-enabled accounts.

Expand | Collapse
Can I downgrade my Enterprise plan to a lower plan type?

No. Once you enable ESDP-compliant features on your account or Enterprise team, it cannot be reverted back to a regular, non-ESDP-enabled account.

If you want to remove Enhanced Sensitive Data Protection features from your account, or if you want a lower plan, you must open a new account.

TIP! You can transfer surveys from one account to another. Check out the Security Tips section for best practices.

What happens if I don't renew my Enhanced Sensitive Data Protection account or team?

If you decide you no longer need to use SurveyMonkey and don't renew your account, your account will be placed into a suspended state. However, you will not be able to access your survey data or account directly (except for limited billing and account administration functions).

SurveyMonkey will retain a suspended account for a period of time in order to provide you with an opportunity to unsuspend your account by renewing it. If your account is suspended and you need access to your data or want to close your account, please contact us. At the end of the suspension period, SurveyMonkey will close your account and delete all data in it.

What happens if I close my account?

If you close your Enterprise team, the account will terminate at the end of your billing period.

SurveyMonkey always provides you with an opportunity to save a copy of your survey data before your account gets closed.

Enhanced Sensitive Data Protection Security Tips

Once you enable Enhanced Sensitive Data Protection on your account or team, follow these best practices when performing certain actions to help ensure that you're handling your data responsibly and securely.

Action
	
Security Tips

Exporting survey results	If you download survey results to your own computer, please make sure that those downloaded files are handled appropriately. We suggest that you secure those files by encrypting them and only transferring them under an encrypted connection.
Sharing surveys with others	When you share a survey, the people you choose to share it with will have access to view and possibly edit the survey, or access any collected survey responses. Remember to only share surveys with people who are authorized to work on that survey.
Transferring a survey to another account	If you must transfer a survey to a different SurveyMonkey account, make sure that you are certain that the receiving account is the one you intend to send it to. To transfer a survey, you must enter the exact username of that account. The transfer process cannot be undone without action by the receiving account holder.

If your survey contains sensitive data, it is your responsibility to ensure that such information is only disclosed to an appropriate recipient. This means that if you transfer this data to another account, it is crucial that account is also ESDP-enabled.
Collecting responses	We recommend that you use a Web Link Collector.

We do not recommend the use of an Email Invitation Collector. Email Invitation Collectors email survey invitations to contacts with a unique survey link tied to a contact's email address. If respondents are able to edit their responses, a contact of an email invitation could complete all or part of a survey and forward their unique survey link to someone else. This would allow the second contact to view the first contact’s responses, which may contain sensitive data.
Sharing survey results	Your survey results may contain sensitive data, so remember to only share survey results to authorized recipients.

Smart Notifications

SurveyMonkey
Smart Notifications

Enterprise Feature: If you're interested, contact sales. If you already have an Enterprise account, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Video Overview
Overview
How Smart Notifications Work

Smart notifications let you send email notifications to yourself or others when a survey response meets a set of conditions, called a trigger. Conditions can be based on specific survey answers or custom variable. Each trigger can have multiple conditions, which must all be met for a smart notification to send. Smart notifications won't trigger for disqualified responses.

Only survey owners can manage smart notifications and their conditions, but you can share smart notifications with others, too. We send an email to let them know.

Smart notifications are survey-specific. If you have multiple surveys you want to receive notifications for, you need to create smart notifications for each one. You can set up to 10 smart notifications per survey.

Tip! You can find your alert messages from the last 30 days in the Notification center.

What Emails you Get

When you create a smart notification, you can send email alerts to yourself and others. You and any recipients get an email every time a survey response is submitted that matches the trigger you set up.

The email has a link to view the individual response, which people can see without logging in to a SurveyMonkey account. The link stays active for 90 days after the notification is sent. 

These alerts also appear as messages in the Notification center.
TIP! If you're not getting alert emails, try these troubleshooting tips.

Managing Smart Notifications
Creating and Sharing Smart Notifications 

To create a smart notification:

From Home, select … next to the survey or go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Select Manage Notifications.
Select the + Create button next to Smart notifications.
Choose your trigger criteria. These are the question and custom variable conditions that need to be met for a notification to send.
(Optional) Select +Condition to add another condition to the same trigger. By default, this links your conditions with AND logic. If you want to use OR logic instead, select the AND button to change it. It's not possible to combine AND/OR logic in the same trigger. Repeat to add additional conditions to the single trigger.
Select Add Recipients to share the notification with others. When you share smart notifications with someone, they’ll get an email to let them know.
If you want to receive the notification, check the Include myself as a recipient box.
(Optional) Customize the subject line and message of your email so recipients know why they're getting the notification.
Select Save.
Adding Recipients to an Existing Notification

To add more recipients to an existing notification:

From Home, select … next to the survey or go to the Publish survey section of your survey. Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Select Manage Notifications.
Select the name of the smart notification you want to add someone to.
Select Recipients.
Select Add New.
Type in the email address of the person you want to share notifications with.
Select Share.

Tip! To get an email after every survey response without setting conditions, turn on instant notifications.

Stop Sharing Smart Notifications

To stop sharing a smart notification with someone:

From Home, select … next to the survey or go to the Publish survey section of your survey. Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Select Manage Notifications.
Select the name of the smart notification you want to remove someone from.
Select Recipients.
Select the trash can icon next to the people you want to remove.
Select Done.
Turning Off a Smart Notification

When you turn off a smart notification, it keeps the trigger conditions and recipient list stored, but you or shared recipients won’t receive alert emails when those survey conditions are met.

To turn off a smart notification:

From Home, select … next to the survey or go to the Publish survey section of your survey. Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Select Manage Notifications.
Toggle the smart notification off.

If you want to use the notification again, toggle it back on.

Deleting a Smart Notification

To permanently remove a smart notification and its trigger conditions from your account, you can delete it. It isn’t possible to resume a deleted smart notification.

To delete a smart notification:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Select Manage Notifications.
Select the name of the notification you want to delete.
Select the delete button at the bottom of the page.
Check the confirmation box.
Select Confirm.

Collecting Offline Responses

To download the survey you need to be the survey owner, or the survey owner needs to share the survey with you, and your device needs to be connected to the internet.

To download a survey:

Tap the Survey icon to go to the My Surveys screen.
Select a survey and tap the Down Arrow icon to download it.

Once your survey is downloaded, you can disconnect from the internet and start collecting responses by tapping the title of the survey.

Managing Offline Responses

You can view the Completion Status, Collector Name, Last Entry Date/Time and Time Spent for any collected responses, and edit or delete survey responses while disconnected from the internet.

To edit or delete a survey response:

Tap the Survey icon to go to the My Surveys screen.
Tap to see a list of survey responses.
Tap each response in the list to see the response details.
In the upper-right corner of the screen, tap the More icon.

Tap Edit to reopen the survey and edit responses, or tap Delete to remove the response from your device.

Uploading Offline Responses

Your device needs to be connected to the internet to upload the survey responses you collected in offline mode.

To upload responses to SurveyMonkey:

Tap the Survey icon to go to the My Surveys screen.
Tap the Upload/checkmark next to the survey you want to upload responses from.
In the bottom-right corner, tap the Upload/Cloud icon and choose to upload All responses or Complete responses only.
Tap Upload.

When you upload responses, they're permanently deleted from the device and moved into the Analyze section of the survey in SurveyMonkey.You can continue to collect more responses or tap X to remove the survey from your device.

Kiosk Mode

You can use kiosk mode to turn your device into a survey taking station, as long as you have an internet connection. Kiosk mode runs your survey in a loop—so each time someone finishes a survey, a new survey is ready for the next person to take.

To use kiosk mode:

Tap the Survey icon to go to the My Surveys screen.
Tap the name of the survey to open it.
Collect responses in the app. Responses will automatically sync with your SurveyMonkey account.

Tap the Profile icon to go to the My Account page and enable additional kiosk mode settings.

Account Settings

The My Account page displays the following information:

Username
Account email
Plan type
Kiosk Settings

With some paid accounts, you can enable the following settings for kiosk mode:

Inactivity Timer: Set an inactivity timer to loop the survey back to the beginning if the survey remains inactive for the set amount of time.
Passcode Lock: Set a passcode to prevent survey-takers from exiting the survey-taking experience. To exit the survey, you need to enter the 4-digit passcode.
Device Preferences

Device Name: Change your device nickname. This is visible to your team's Primary Admin.

Results Dashboards

SurveyMonkey
Results Dashboards

Results Dashboards are a great way to present your survey results. Customize your results, add charts and text, then publish to share your dashboard with anyone.

TIP! Results dashboards are best used to present results to others. Use multi-survey analysis dashboards to compare results from multiple surveys.

Building a Dashboard

To create a new dashboard, start by either adding charts from your survey in bulk or adding charts from individual questions one at a time. On most plans, you can add up to 20 supported questions, and if you're on an Enterprise plan, you can add up to 40.

Unsupported questions and settings
Incompatible Questions	Incompatible Charts and Settings
File Upload

Slider

Matrix of Dropdowns

Multiple Textboxes

Date/Time

Contact Info

Text or Image

A/B Tests

Click Map	Tags to categorize responses

Questions with more than 20 answer options

Questions with a Benchmark showing

Stacked bar charts for questions with more than 4 answer choices

Questions with more than 4 answer choices and a Compare rule applied

Questions with hidden or combined answer choices

"Other" comment fields

To add charts from the first 20 (or 40, on Enterprise plans) supported questions:

Go to the Analyze results section of your survey.
At the top of the page, select Add to > +New dashboard.
Enter a Title, and choose how you want to get started:
Build it for me: Include all compatible questions.
Start from scratch: Choose which questions to include.
Select Create.

To add a chart from an individual question:

Go to the Analyze results section of your survey.
Find a question you'd like to add to the dashboard.
Select the pin icon.
Select +New dashboard.
Enter a name for your dashboard.
Select Create.
Adding Charts

Once the dashboard has been created, you can add more charts to your dashboard.

To add charts:

Go to the Analyze results section of your survey.
Find the chart you want to add.
Select the pin icon.
Choose the dashboard you want to add the chart to.
Customizing Your Dashboard

Once you've added charts to your dashboard, you can customize how it looks.

To customize your dashboard:

From the Analyze results section, select Dashboards and crosstabs at the top of the page.
Find your dashboard, then select Edit.

Here are the things you can customize in your dashboard:

Change layout: Choose between Column and Grid layout in the toolbar.
Rearrange charts: Arrange your dashboard by dragging and dropping cards into rows and adding text cards to give your results more context. You can add up to three cards per row and 20-40 cards per dashboard, depending on your plan.
Customize visualizations: Find a chart, then click the three dots menu in the upper-right corner of the card, then toggle the options. If you are using the Column layout, you can choose to show the chart, the table, or both. If you are using the Grid layout, you can only choose to show the chart or the table.
View open-ended responses: For questions with open-ended responses, you can click the three dots (...) in the upper-right corner of the card to switch between List View to show all text responses at once, or Slide View to show text responses one at a time.
Note: Cards for open-ended responses only show the 50 most recent answers.
Remove charts: To delete a card from your dashboard, click the three dots (...) in the upper-right corner of the card and click the Delete button.

TIP! Customize your chart's display options and colors before adding them to a dashboard to make them stand out.

Sharing a Dashboard

When you're ready to share your results with people, publish and share your dashboard. If your survey is still open and collecting responses, the dashboard will update automatically as more people answer your survey.

When you share the dashboard link in messaging and collaboration apps, we’ll show the survey title, response count, and first chart in the message preview. The preview reflects the title, response count, and first chart from the time you share the link and won’t update automatically.

To publish your dashboard:

In the Analyze results section of your survey, select Dashboards and crosstabs at the top of the page.
Find the dashboard you want to share.
Select More Options.
Select Turn share link ON.
Select Preview to open the dashboard in another window.
Copy the link and share your dashboard anywhere.

It isn't possible to embed a dashboard on your website.

Adding Password Protection

Password Protect Shared Results

Paid feature
Log in to see if this feature is included in your plan.
Log in
Sign up free

You can password protect your dashboard. Anyone you share the link with will need to enter the password to access it.

If password protection is turned on before sharing the link, we won’t show the survey title, response count, or first chart in the message preview.

To password protect your published dashboard:

In the Analyze results section of your survey, select Dashboards and crosstabs at the top of the page.
Find the dashboard you want to password protect.
Select Preview.
At the bottom of the dashboard, select Dashboard Settings.
Select the toggle to turn Password protection on.
Enter a password.
Select Done.

You won't see Dashboard Settings at the bottom of your Dashboard if it isn't published yet. You can select Publish to turn link sharing on and control password protection.

Enforcing Single Sign-on (SSO) Authentication

(Enterprise only—if you're interested, contact sales) Enterprise customers with SSO enabled can enforce SSO authentication for these pages to further secure access beyond a static password. 

To require SSO authentication for your published dashboard:

In the Analyze results section of your survey, select Dashboards and Crosstabs at the top of the page.
Find the dashboard you want to protect.
Select Preview.
At the bottom of the dashboard, select Dashboard Settings.
Toggle on Single Sign-on. This limits access to people in your organization.
Select Done.
Turning Off Sharing

If you need to limit access to your dashboard after you've shared it, you can turn sharing off. Anyone you've previously shared the dashboard with won't be able to access the dashboard if they visit the link or try to refresh their browser.

To turn off sharing:

In the Analyze results section of your survey, select Dashboards and crosstabs at the top of the page.
Find the dashboard.
Select More Options.
Select Turn share link OFF.
Managing Your Dashboards

You can manage all of your dashboards from the Dashboards and crosstabs page.

Option	Description
Preview	After you publish a dashboard, see what it will look like to anyone who gets the link.
Edit	Make changes to your dashboard at any time. Any changes you make will take effect immediately.
More Options	Turn your share link on to publish it, or off to limit access. You can also delete your dashboard here. Deleting a dashboard won't affect or erase any survey results.
