Using SurveyMonkey for Salesforce

Salesforce

Paid feature
Log in to see if this feature is included in your plan.
Log in
Sign up free

Get the integration! SurveyMonkey for Salesforce is an Enterprise add-on. Contact Sales or your Customer Success Manager (CSM). Limitation: The integration setup is only available in English.

With SurveyMonkey for Salesforce, you can build automations to trigger surveys and push data back to Salesforce records for in-context analysis. Create reports, dashboards, and automate flows to take action on feedback.

When you integrate survey data with Salesforce, you can better understand, measure, and react to various customer interactions to improve the overall health of your business relationships.

Salesforce blocked the creation of new workflow rules in February 2023. You’ll need to build new automations using Flows or use the Migrate to Flow tool. You can still activate, edit, and deactivate existing process builder and workflow rules.

Before You Start

Create your survey and set up your Salesforce object before you create your mappings. Learn more in our Getting Started guide.

If your SurveyMonkey plan has Power and Casual seats, you need an Enterprise Power seat to access the integration. Learn more about seats and permissions.
You can use the Salesforce Integration license with the SurveyMonkey integration, but you need to enable certain permissions first. Learn more about recommended Salesforce permissions.
Access the Integration

All your mappings are saved to the Salesforce account you connect to. If the logged-in Salesforce account is deactivated, their mappings will stop working. Make sure to use an integration Salesforce account if possible.

You can connect multiple accounts, including sandbox environments. This process leverages OAuth 2.0 for a secure integration.

To access the integration:

Sign in to the Salesforce account you want to connect to SurveyMonkey.
In SurveyMonkey, go to the Connect Apps section of your survey.
Find Salesforce, then select Learn more to open the app.
Select Connect or Connect Sandbox to connect your Salesforce account. If you’ve signed in to Salesforce, we’ll automatically connect to your signed-in account.

Refreshing Sandbox environments: Your Salesforce connection will break when you refresh your sandbox environment. To keep your mappings, reconnect to your sandbox environment, then copy the mappings from your old connection to the new one.

Connect Your Survey to the Integration

To connect the survey you want to map to Salesforce:

After adding your connection, select your username.
On the My Mappings page, select Connect Survey.
Select a survey title from the dropdown. You can connect any survey you own or that has been shared with you with full access. Surveys are listed by title, not by nickname.
Select Next.
How Mapping Works

Mappings send your survey data back to Salesforce. You'll create mappings to send specific data, such as a response or survey metadata, to a Salesforce object.

Survey data collected after the mapping was created gets mapped, by default, but you can enable historical responses sync for a more comprehensive dataset.

Historical Responses Sync

If your surveys have been collecting responses since before you integrated SurveyMonkey and Salesforce, then contact your CSM to get access to sync historical responses mapped by the Managed or Custom object package. 

Completed historical responses are synced by default, and at the mapping level, you can check the box to include Partial responses.

Keep in mind, a historical sync is tied to one mapping action, connected to one survey, one collector, and one or more Salesforce objects. So, if your survey has multiple collectors, set up a mapping action for each.

To sync historical responses to Salesforce:

Contact your CSM to request access.
From Mappings, open a survey.
Select … under Actions.
Select Sync previous responses.
Select Sync responses.

Once your sync begins you can’t cancel it and it may take up to 4 hours if syncing a lot of data. Once it’s complete, a message and email notification confirms whether the sync was complete or failed.

Message	Description
All responses synced
	All historical responses successfully synced.

# of the total number of previous responses failed	If at least one response fails to sync, we say how many responses out of total responses failed. 

No responses met sync requirements 	If your mapping fails or the requirements of the sync can’t be met, then no responses are synced.

Managed Package

If you’re mapping with the Managed package, we recommend you upgrade to the latest Salesforce managed package to sync additional metadata to help you identify the actual survey response date, rather than rely on the date the record was synced to Salesforce.
Be sure to review the field-level security or permission set access for the new Response created date and response modified date fields, and add the new fields to the relevant Salesforce page layouts and reports, if needed.

You can choose from two mapping types:

Managed package: If you don't need customization, you can send all responses to the SurveyMonkey Response object. You'll need to install a small package in Salesforce. This option creates the mapping for you. Learn more about our managed package for Salesforce.
Custom object mapping: Build your own mappings to send data to custom or standard Salesforce objects. This requires more effort but lets you control where your survey data is sent in Salesforce. Use our field mapping guide to learn which Salesforce fields you can send survey data to.

For each mapping type, you can also select the following options:

Sync partial responses to Salesforce: Each time a respondent selects Next to move on in the survey, each answered question on that page will sync, rather than syncing upon survey completion
Disable active assignment rules on creating or updating Salesforce records: Active assignment rules aren't re-applied when Accounts, Cases, or Leads records are created or updated.
Object Mapping Actions

The table below describes the mapping actions you can use in your custom Object Mappings.

Mapping action	What it does
Create a new	Create a new record in the Salesforce object you choose for each survey response. This option doesn't check to see if the record already exists—it just creates a new record each time.
Update an existing	Use a query mapping to find existing object records. If an object exists, it's updated.  If the record doesn't exist or isn't found, the mapping fails and an entry is added to your Error log.
When you select this option, you can choose to Overwrite record fields that have existing values. This will replace existing data on your object. This can help you keep data current. However, if you need to revert these changes, you may need to manually update data later.
Update or create	Use a query mapping to find existing object records. If an object exists, it's updated. If it doesn't exist, a new record is created.
Mapping Types

After choosing your mapping action, you can set up your mapping. There are 3 mapping types you can use to map data to Salesforce.

Mapping type	What it does	Available for
Query mappings	Query mappings tell the integration how to find existing records. You can use a custom variable to map to a specific Salesforce Record ID.	❌ Create a new record
✅ Update existing records
✅ Update or create records
Survey content or data	Map your SurveyMonkey response and other metadata to the appropriate Salesforce object fields.
You can map any response field to one or more objects in Salesforce. If data fails to map, an entry is added to your Error Log.	✅ Create a new record
✅ Update existing records
✅ Update or create records
More data	Add more data to pass static values through to an object field each time a survey response comes in. For example, you can send a record type ID to designate which record type a survey should sync to if multiple exist for your object. Or, you can send a "survey taken" value, such as text or a checkbox, to track people who have taken your survey.	✅ Create a new record
✅ Update existing records
✅ Update or create records
Create Mappings

Build mappings for your survey.

If you create mappings on a shared survey, the owner won’t be able to see your mappings.

Custom Mapping
Create a New Record

Create a new standard or custom object record every time someone submits a survey. To create new object records:

Connect your survey to the Salesforce integration.
Select Add Object Mapping or the Edit icon to review your mapping selections.
In the first dropdown, select Create a new.
Select Select object to choose the object you want to map your responses to.
Select survey content or data to map to Salesforce. Map any survey questions and data to your object in Salesforce. You can select an existing or new Custom Variable to pass known info about a respondent through your survey (for example, Account ID or Case ID).
Certain Salesforce fields can only hold certain data types. Use our field mapping guide to make sure you map to compatible fields in Salesforce.
If you see an exclamation mark icon, there may be an error with your mapping. Hover over the icon to review the error.
(Optional): Add more data to map to Salesforce. You can map any static value back to Salesforce, such as the survey language or locale, or Record Type ID. This value will be mapped every time someone takes your survey.
Select Save Object.
(Optional): Once back on the Object Mappings page, select Disable active assignment rules on creating or updating Salesforce records.
Update Existing Records

pdate an existing standard or custom object when someone submits a survey. You have two options:

Update an existing: Find an existing record to update. If we can’t find an existing record, an error displays in the Audit Log.
Update or create: Find an existing record to update. If we can’t find an existing record, we’ll create a new one.

To update existing records:

Select Next.
Connect your survey to the Salesforce integration.
Select Add Object Mapping or the Edit icon to review your mapping selections.
In the first dropdown, select whether to Update an existing record or Update or create.
(Optional): Check the box to Replace any existing data in record fields. If you choose this option, we'll overwrite any existing values in your Salesforce fields with the survey data you map.
Select Select object to choose the object you want to map your responses to.
Add a query mapping. Query mappings, like a matching rule in Salesforce, tell SurveyMonkey how to find the record to update.
Select the source for your mapping. It’s best to map a * New custom variable to the appropriate record ID in Salesforce.
If you can't use a Salesforce record ID, you can use a field from your survey, like an email address, to find the matching record. However, the response will fail to sync if duplicate records are found.
Select the Salesforce field you want to place this data in.
Select survey content or data to map to Salesforce. Map any survey questions and data to your object in Salesforce. You can select an existing or new Custom Variable to pass known info about a respondent through your survey (for example, Account ID or Case ID).
Certain Salesforce fields can only hold certain data types. Use our field mapping guide to make sure you map to compatible fields in Salesforce.
If you see an exclamation mark icon, there may be an error with your mapping. Hover over the icon to review the error.
(Optional): Add more data to map to Salesforce. You can map any static value back to Salesforce, such as the survey language or locale. This value will be mapped every time someone takes your survey.
Select Save Object.
(Optional): Once back on the Object Mappings page, select Disable active assignment rules on creating or updating Salesforce records.
Managed Mappings
Map to the SurveyMonkey Response Object

Create a new SurveyMonkey Response object every time someone submits a survey. You’ll install our managed package to do this. The managed package makes it easy to send data to Salesforce and build Salesforce reports for survey responses. You can also customize Salesforce page layouts to better review survey data.

You’ll download the managed package while in SurveyMonkey. You don’t need to download anything from the Salesforce App Exchange.

To map to the SurveyMonkey Response object:

Connect your survey to the Salesforce integration.
Select Sync all responses to SurveyMonkey’s Response object. The first time you do this, you’re prompted to install the package in your Salesforce instance and provided with an installation link. When installing, we recommend selecting For All Users.
(Optional): Select Disable active assignment rules on creating or updating Salesforce records. This only applies if your mapping is updating fields directly on the case object.
Relate Records to SurveyMonkey Managed Package Responses

To relate the SurveyMonkey Response records to other records, add an object mapping for the object record you want to relate. The SurveyMonkey managed package already has lookups fields to Account, Case, Contact, Lead, and Opportunity objects, built-in. To relate to any other standard or custom object, you can create additional lookup fields on the managed package objects. You need to map to lookup fields on the SurveyMonkey Response object. 

Select Add Object Mapping or Edit to review your mapping selections.
Select Select an Action, then select Update an Existing.
Select Account, Case, Contact, Lead, or Opportunity. To associate your responses to a different object, you can add additional lookup fields to the SurveyMonkey Response object in your Salesforce setup.
Add Query Mappings to tell Salesforce how to find the related records. Use a Custom Variable to pass the Record ID from Salesforce.
(Optional) Add any survey field mappings to map survey fields to fields on this object.
Select Save Object.
(Optional) If you want to associate your survey responses to multiple objects, repeat steps 1 – 7. You can have one mapping per object.
Once back on the Object Mappings page, select Next.

Deployment Options

It isn’t possible to use a collector owned by someone else. If you want to use an existing collector, make sure to choose one that you created.

Choose how you want to send your survey. We offer three options:

Option to send your survey	Description
Web link pasted into your own email	Create a web link to send in an email from Salesforce or another provider. Web links are easy to set up and allow you to use Advanced Logic and Piping to customize your survey questions with Salesforce data. You’ll need to build your own email template in Salesforce or your other email provider.
Email invitation	Trigger a SurveyMonkey email invitation using a Salesforce flow. We'll help you create an Outbound message in Salesforce. Then, you'll need to create a Salesforce flow to send your survey.
Text	Trigger a SurveyMonkey web link invitation via Text to reach your customers on their mobile devices. Personalize your text with Salesforce data to boost response rates.

Send a Web Link in an Email

If you’re using Piping or Advanced Branching with custom variables, use the Web Link deployment option. A Web Link will let your Salesforce data inform your survey logic or customize your survey questions.

To use a web link:

Create your mapping.
On the Deployment Options screen, select Web link. Then, select an existing collector or create a new one.
Choose the object that will trigger your survey. Salesforce can send your survey when changes to an object meet certain criteria (for example, when a Case is closed or a Contact is 90 days old). You’ll use this object later when you create your Salesforce flow.
If you're not sending your survey from Salesforce, select None. I'm not using Salesforce Flows to trigger my survey.
Select Next.
Select the Salesforce objects to map to any custom variables you added. When you send the survey from Salesforce, we’ll pull in data from these fields in your web link. We’ll also sync this data to SurveyMonkey so you can filter responses and pipe data into your survey.  
(Optional): Select Add data to add more fields to your survey link. 
Select Select data to choose your Salesforce field. Choose the object with the field you want, then select the field. Then, select Save.
Select New custom variable to map the field to SurveyMonkey. Enter a Variable ID (this is visible in the survey URL). Then, enter a Variable label (a name for the variable so you can recognize it later). Then, select Save.
When you’re ready, select Generate link.
(Optional): If you want to hide custom variables from respondents, toggle on the Encrypt web link option and follow the instructions that appear on the screen. You’ll need to take several steps in Salesforce to set this up. This also protects your link so your customers can’t edit them. Learn more
Copy the URL. It includes the custom variables you chose to map to the object.
Go to Salesforce to complete the setup. Review the instructions below for help.
Complete the Salesforce Setup

If you’re sending your survey from Salesforce, create an email template and flow. You may need to contact your Salesforce admin for help.

To set up your email in Salesforce:

In Salesforce, build your email template and add your web link to the email body. 
Create an email alert using your email template. Make sure to use the object you chose to trigger your survey when you created your web link.
Create a flow that sends your email alert when conditions are met. Make sure to use the object you chose to trigger your survey when you created your web link. 

Example: You want to trigger a survey when someone closes a case. When you build your flow, choose Case as the object to trigger your survey. Select the Case object for your email alert. In Salesforce, create a flow that sends your email when a Case status changes to Closed. When the email is sent, the custom variables in the survey link will populate with data for the person receiving the email.

Send a SurveyMonkey Email Invitation

To send an Email Invitation from the SurveyMonkey for Salesforce integration:

Create your mapping.
On the Deployment Options screen, select Email. 
Select the object that will trigger your survey. Salesforce can send your survey when changes to an object meet certain criteria (for example, when a Case is closed or a Contact is 90 days old). You’ll use this object later when you create your email message and Salesforce flow.
Select Next.
Select the field on your object that holds the recipient’s email address. We’ll use this field to send your survey to the right people. For example, on a Case object, you might choose the “Contact Email” field.
Build your email:
Subject: Enter a subject line for your email.
Message format: Use our pre-built Template, or build a custom HTML message.
Customize email header: Toggle this setting on to choose a custom background color, select a font, add a logo, and make other visual changes to the email header. Maximum length is 255 characters.
Body: Enter the body text for your email message.
Insert custom data: Personalize your email message with data from fields on your Salesforce object or your SurveyMonkey contacts.
There’s a limit of 6 unique custom data tags, but you can use those tags as many times as you want. However, the Email, FirstName, and LastName fields from your SurveyMonkey contacts don’t count toward your total.
Embed first question: Toggle on to put the first survey question directly in the email. 
Hide SurveyMonkey branding: Remove the SurveyMonkey logo from your email.
Select Preview email to view your message. If you’re happy with your email, select Next.
Build your Salesforce outbound message. The outbound message tells SurveyMonkey when to send your email invitation. It includes the Salesforce data we need to send the email and map data back to Salesforce.
Select the Salesforce objects to map to any custom variables you added. When you send the survey from Salesforce, we’ll pull in data from these fields in your outbound message.
(Optional): Select +More data to add more fields to your outbound message.
Select Select data to choose your Salesforce field. Choose the object with the field you want, then select the field. Then, select Save.
Select New custom variable to map the field to SurveyMonkey. Enter a Variable ID (this is visible in the survey URL). Then, enter a Variable label (a name for the variable so you can recognize it later). Then, select Save.
When you’re done, select Build in Salesforce. We’ll create your outbound message in Salesforce. 
In Salesforce, create a flow to send your outbound message. Include the object you chose to trigger your survey. For example, if you chose the Case object to trigger your survey, create a flow for the Case object.
Save and test your flow. You can immediately check your collector in SurveyMonkey to confirm an email invitation is pending.
(Optional): Set up reminder and thank-you emails in your collector options. These can help increase your response rates by reminding respondents to take your survey.
Updating Your Email Message

To change your email message after your collector has received responses:

In SurveyMonkey, go back to the Salesforce integration.
Find the mapping for your survey. Select the 3 dots menu, then select Edit.
Go to the Deployment Options.
Select Next.
Edit your email.

Don’t edit or send the email from your survey’s collector options. This can cause your custom data fields and the email automation to fail. Use the Salesforce integration to edit your email.

Troubleshooting Email Invitations

There are a few common errors with email invitations. Here are a few things to try to fix email invitation issues.

Make sure the right fields were added to the Outbound Message. Some fields have similar names. Including the wrong field can cause the flow to fail.
Make sure your Salesforce account has permissions to send Outbound Messages.
Check your Outbound Message in Salesforce. If you see an error, confirm that your endpoint URL is correct. This should be the link you got in the last distribution step in SurveyMonkey.
Send a SurveyMonkey Text

Contact your CSM to enable text messages.

To use a text:

Create your mapping.
On the Deployment Options step, select Text. 
Select the Object that triggers your survey. Salesforce can send your survey when changes to an object meet certain criteria (for example, when a Case is closed or a Contact is 90 days old). You’ll use this object later when you create your text message and Salesforce flow. Your recipient’s contact numbers are pulled from a field on this object. 
Select Next.
Under Recipient contact no, select the phone field on your object to pull as the recipient’s phone number for the text. You can’t pull recipients from SurveyMonkey Contacts or manually enter numbers, unlike SurveyMonkey’s Text message collector.
Draft your Message and make sure to identify your company name in it.
(Optional): Insert custom data to personalize your text with data from your Salesforce object, like names or case IDs.
Depending on the length of your message, 1 or 2 texts will be sent to each recipient (max 2). 
While there’s no fixed character limit for your message, aim for less than 280 characters. If you include emojis, special characters, or code they take up additional character space and count towards your limit. Simply make your message shorter until you can save it.
There’s a limit of 6 unique custom data tags, but you can use those tags as many times as you want. 
(Optional): Toggle on Suppression list sync to select a checkbox field to identify any recipients who may have opted out. This way, you can exclude them from your text message.
Consider adding your company’s privacy policy to your survey and check the box to confirm that all SMS recipients have consented to receiving these text messages from me in accordance with applicable law, and I have identified my company in my message.
View the Previewed Message. If you’re happy with your text, select Save.
Select Test to send a test Text to a phone number. The Text may be split into 2 messages. We let you know how many texts will be used from your text balance, along with your remaining text balance.
Build your Salesforce outbound message. The outbound message tells SurveyMonkey when to send your text. It includes the Salesforce data we need to send the text and map data back to Salesforce.
Select the Salesforce objects to map to any custom variables you added. When you send the survey from Salesforce, we’ll pull in data from these fields in your outbound message.
(Optional) Select +Moredata to add more fields to your outbound message.
Select Select data to choose your Salesforce field. Choose the object with the field you want, then select the field. Then, select Save.
Select New custom variable to map the field to SurveyMonkey. Enter a Variable ID (this is visible in the survey URL). Then, enter a Variable label (a name for the variable so you can recognize it later). Then, select Done.
When you’re done, select Build in Salesforce. We’ll create your outbound message in Salesforce, and allow you to View in Salesforce.
In Salesforce, create a flow to send your outbound message. Be sure to include the object you chose to trigger your survey, earlier. 
Attach your outbound message as the Action of your flow. The outbound message created for this survey will be identified in Salesforce as [Survey Name].
Select Done.

To improve response rates, set up automated text reminders, custom survey URLS and other settings in SurveyMonkey.  

When your text is triggered to send, recipients see your custom message, the survey link, and the following opt out text, which isn’t editable: 

Reply HELP for info. STOP to opt out. Msg&DataRatesMayApply. 

Test Your Survey and Mappings

Take a test version of your survey to make sure your mappings work correctly. You can review mapping errors in the Audit Log.

Select Mappings near the top of the page to see a survey's audit logs or errors. You can select the iAudit log icon to view your successful syncs or select the !Error icon to view an error description.

Share Mappings with Your Team

Shared Mappings give your team visibility into your survey mappings for better collaboration.

Share Mappings

To let your team access your survey and mappings:

From SurveyMonkey, share your mapped survey with your team members. Make sure you give Full Access permissions to the Design Survey section.
From the SurveyMonkey for Salesforce integration, go to My Mappings and select the Shared toggle for surveys you want to make available.

Don't see the Shared column in My Mappings? Contact your CSM to activate the feature for your team.

View Shared Mappings

To view the team's shared mappings, hover over the down arrow next to Connected Accounts or My Mappings and select Shared Mappings.

Team members can Edit Shared Mappings but can't view the deployment options page. To get the invitation URL, team members can contact the survey owner.

Copy Mappings to Another Account

If you build mappings in a Sandbox account, you can copy them over to a production account. To copy mappings:

If you haven't already, add a connection for your other Salesforce account.
On the My Mappings page, check the box for the survey you want to copy.
Select Copy to Account.
Select the account to copy your mapping to.
Select OK.
Common Questions
Expand | Collapse
How do I tie my responses to a specific record in Salesforce?

First, check that you included Custom Variables in your survey mapping—either your survey field mapping or query mapping, depending on your mapping action.

If your variables are mapped, the merge fields in your survey URL may need to be updated if your sending platform's {Merge field} differs from Salesforce. For example, Pardot uses different merge fields than Salesforce. Check the {Merge field} in the survey URL and replace it with the correct merge field from your sending platform.

If you’re sending an Email Invitation, contact your CSM for assistance.

How do we keep the responses sync active if the user that set up the mappings leaves the company?

Don't delete a SurveyMonkey account or a Salesforce connection with an active Salesforce mapping, as this deletes the mappings permanently and survey data won't sync to Salesforce. Instead, if necessary, first reassign the SurveyMonkey account—this maintains all survey and integration data in the account. If the Salesforce connection a mapping is set up under will be deactivated, to avoid data loss, copy the mappings over to a new Salesforce connection/account.

To copy mappings over to a new Salesforce account:

Add a new Salesforce connection by logging into Salesforce and selecting Add account on the integration page (the Salesforce user you are logged in as will be added).
Go to Connected Accounts and select the username of the original Salesforce connection.
Select survey mappings and Copy to Account.
Select the new Salesforce connection.
The survey mappings are copied to the new connection. This doesn't include the sync data for original mapping.

You can now safely delete the original Salesforce connection or deactivate the user.

QR Code

SurveyMonkey
QR Code

A QR code is a 2D barcode that people can scan with their smartphone to open and take your survey. It's common to include QR codes on print media like pamphlets, posters, and receipts.

Survey owners or people with Full Access permissions can download a QR code for a survey when creating a Web link collector.

It isn't possible to download a QR Code if your weblink uses custom variables.

Download a QR Code

To download your QR code:

Create a Web Link collector.
Optional: Customize your URL ending. Since the QR code you download includes the URL ending in the file name, customizing the URL ending can make it easier for you to match it with the right survey and collector.
Click Download QR Code under the survey link.
If you don’t see this option under your web link, click Link Settings to find it.

The QR code downloads to your computer with the file name QR code_your-weblink-ending.png. It downloads to the maximum width and height (256x256).

TIP! If you want, you can use a third-party app to resize the width and height, or change the resolution of your QR code.

Options and Settings

The collector options you select affect both the survey link and the QR code—so the survey experience will be the same for people taking your survey from either place.

Analyzing Results

If you send out both the URL and the QR code to collect responses, you won't be able to filter your results by QR code only. You can only filter your results by the entire collector.

If you want to be able to filter by QR code only, make sure to only share the QR code and not the URL—then you can filter by collector.

Scanning a QR Code

Scanning a SurveyMonkey QR code with your smartphone or tablet opens the survey on the device so people can take the survey. Some phones already have QR code readers built in, or you can download a QR code reader app onto your device.

Benchmarks

Benchmarks

SurveyMonkey
Benchmarks

Paid Feature: Benchmarks are available on Advantage plans and higher. 

Benchmarks add context to your survey results by comparing your responses with others who asked the same Question Bank questions. Your survey results include benchmarks for the Question Bank questions you’ve used which have available benchmark data. 

We’re also working to continuously improve the benchmarks experience, which may be available for additional survey questions in the future.

Benchmark Data

Benchmark data comes from SurveyMonkey customers who use benchmark questions in their surveys. To calculate a benchmark, we aggregate the responses across surveys for each benchmarkable question, then average those responses to generate the question’s score.

To preserve privacy, responses for a given question are aggregated and de-identified to create a set of average statistics about that question—we don't disclose any individual responses, personal information, or organization names.

Check out our Privacy Notice for more on how SurveyMonkey handles your personal information and data.

Opting Out of Benchmarks

Opting out of benchmarks excludes your account’s survey responses from benchmark calculations. You’re able to opt out of benchmarks if your account is either:

An Enterprise account with HIPAA or ESDP features enabled
Previously opted out of benchmarks 

If you’re an Enterprise customer and have questions around opting in or out of benchmarks, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

If you’ve previously opted out of benchmarks, you can also use the steps below to opt in to including your responses in future benchmarks.

To opt out of benchmarks:

Log in and go to My Account.
Scroll to the Data Features section.
Select Edit next to Access to Benchmarks.
Select Off.
If you’d like to opt in to using benchmarks instead, select On.
Select Save.

If your responses are currently included, they’ll be removed when benchmark data next refreshes after you opt out. Opting out of contributing your survey responses to benchmark data will also remove your ability to view benchmarks when analyzing survey results.

Using Benchmarkable Questions

You can include benchmarkable questions in your survey by using our Question Bank, or with specific survey templates.

The benchmark icon indicates when a Question Bank question or template is benchmarkable.
Using Question Bank

Our Question Bank contains hundreds of questions created and certified by survey methodologists. 

To see the Question Bank questions with benchmarks available:

Go to the Design Survey section of your survey.
Select Question Bank.
Browse the available questions with the benchmark icon and add it to your survey.

Certain questions from our Question Bank will let you customize text using a dropdown menu. However, editing the question text outside the dropdown can invalidate the benchmark comparison, since respondents might interpret your question differently than the original version.

If you make additional changes to the question type, or the number of answer options for a benchmarkable question, it will remove the option to view that question’s benchmark in Analyze results.

Using Survey Templates

To see the expert templates with benchmarks available:

Select Create survey.
Select Pick a popular template.
Browse the available templates with the Benchmark icon. You can also check the Benchmarks checkbox to filter for Benchmarkable templates.

You don't need to use every question in the expert template, but the more benchmarkable questions you include, the more comparison data you'll see in your results. Some templates may have additional questions that aren't benchmarkable. Feel free to add, edit, or delete questions to customize and style your survey.

Viewing Benchmarks in Survey Results

You can see benchmarks in Analyze Results for any surveys with benchmarkable questions, once your survey has gathered at least one response.

If you use an NPS question in your survey, you’ll automatically see the global benchmark score below your summary data chart. You can use the Benchmarks toggle from the question settings to hide or show benchmarks.

For other benchmark question types, you can select the benchmark icon at the top of the question window to show the available benchmark alongside your survey results.

There are some limitations to keep in mind when using benchmarks with the following analyze features:

Exports — Benchmark data and charts aren’t included in exports of your survey results, results dashboards, or shared data pages.
Add a Filter or Compare rule — Your survey data is impacted by applied rules, but the benchmark data is not.
Save a View — If you save a View with benchmarks turned on, benchmark visibility is not saved as part of the view settings. You can show or hide benchmarks for each question independently when working in your saved view. Filter or Show rules applied are saved as normal.
Shared Surveys

Anyone with shared access to your survey can view benchmarks in Analyze. When you show or hide benchmarks for a question, those changes apply to everyone with access to the survey.

How to Reach a Target Audience

SurveyMonkey
How to Reach a Target Audience
Getting Started

When you buy survey responses with SurveyMonkey Audience, there are two great ways to make sure the right people take your survey:

1. Choose targeting options in a Target Audience collector.

2. Add screening questions with disqualification logic to your survey, and estimate a qualification rate.

ADD-ON PURCHASE: SurveyMonkey Audience responses are purchased separately from your plan subscription as a one-time survey add-on.

Targeting Options

Use the targeting options available in the Target Audience collector to send your survey to a specific audience. Our panelists have been sorted based on hundreds of targeting options so you can target your audience based on country, demographics, employment status, hobbies, religion, and more.

Check out our SurveyMonkey Audience preview page to view our available targeting options.

Screening Questions & Disqualification Logic

If you want to ask specific questions to find the right people to take your survey, in addition to our targeting options, you can add screening questions with disqualification logic to your survey.

For example, you want to find people who have shopped at a particular store in the last 30 days, or who have purchased premium whiskey in the last six months.

Screening Questions

Screening questions are closed-ended questions that you add to your survey design to either qualify or disqualify people from your target audience, depending on how they answer.

TIP! For examples and tips, check out our guide for using screening questions.

Disqualification Logic

You need to add disqualification logic to any screening questions in your survey. You’ll use question skip logic that’s set to skip to a disqualification page. Adding disqualification logic to your screening questions lets relevant survey-takers complete your survey, while people who don’t qualify for your target audience will skip to a disqualification page.

Be careful not to skip disqualified people to the End of Survey—these responses aren't disqualified and count towards the total number of complete responses you ordered.

Adding a Screening Question

To add a screening question with disqualification logic:

In the Survey Design section, add your screening question to the beginning of your survey.
From the Options tab, select Require an Answer to This Question.
From the Logic tab, add Question Skip Logic.
Chose to skip people who don’t qualify for your target audience to a Disqualification Page.
Qualification Rate

If your survey includes a screening question with disqualification logic, you need to select a qualification rate before you can complete your order. The qualification rate is the estimated percentage of people you expect to qualify for your survey based on your screening questions.

The qualification rate you choose affects the number of people we send your survey to. For example, if you want 100 complete responses and you estimate a qualification rate of 50%, we may send your survey to up to 200 panelists.

It's better to estimate a lower rate to make sure you get the total number of complete responses you requested.

You're responsible for understanding how the qualification rate will affect your order—we're not able to help you choose the appropriate qualification rate for your survey, but you can check out our tips below.

To buy responses, your qualification rate needs to be 10% or higher.

Expand | Collapse
How Qualification Rate Affects Your Project

To make sure you get the number of complete responses you ordered, we adjust the number of people we send your survey to based on your qualification rate.

A high qualification rate indicates the type of survey-takers you're looking for are easy to find, and you estimate a high percentage of panelists can qualify for your survey.
A low qualification rate indicates the type of survey-takers you're looking for are hard to find, and you estimate a low percentage of panelists can qualify for your survey. Lower qualification rates cost more per response since we have to send your survey to more people.

TIP! Use our SurveyMonkey Audience preview page to choose targeting options and qualification rates to better understand how your total cost is affected.

Estimated vs. Actual Qualification Rate

When you choose a qualification rate for your project, it's an estimation. Your actual qualification rate is calculated based on the number of people who qualified for your survey out of the total number of people who answered the screening questions.

If you already sent your survey, you can see your actual qualification rate in the Target Audience collector.

If the actual qualification rate is higher than your estimate, your project should complete on time with the number of complete responses you ordered.
If the actual qualification rate is lower than your estimate, you may not get all the complete responses you ordered since more people will be disqualified from your survey. To collect more responses, buy a new order using the actual qualification rate recorded for the survey.

To improve the chances of getting the number of complete responses you need, it's better to estimate a lower qualification rate than you expect. However, we aren't able to offer a refund if you misestimated your qualification rate.

Tips for Estimating Qualification Rate

Finding just the right people to survey can be a challenge for market research. If you don't know where to begin, don't worry—here are some techniques to help estimate qualification rate:

Check your company's market research data. Many companies already know roughly what to expect. Try asking colleagues if they know who would have access to data like this.
Do some quick research online. If you're targeting a well-researched population, there may be industry evidence documented online.
Run a small test project. You can get a better idea (within a margin of error of +/- 10%) of the qualification rate by surveying just 100 people. This strategy works best if you plan on buying a larger sample and don't mind spending a smaller amount to get a better idea of what your qualification rate might be.

Emailing an Embedded NPS Question

GetFeedback
Emailing an Embedded NPS Question

Embed a Net Promoter Score (NPS) question in your email to maximize participation. Survey respondents can select an answer, and we’ll automatically record their answer. We’ll also track any merge fields you included in your survey.

This article uses Net Promoter Score (NPS) as an example, but you can also use multiple choice, CSAT, CES, Polar Choice (Like/Dislike), and Rating questions.

For an embedded email question response to be automatically submitted, your survey must contain 1 question only. Otherwise, your respondents will need to answer any additional follow-up questions and select submit for their answers to be recorded.

Building Your NPS Survey

Create your survey, including any exit pages or redirects that you’d like that participant to see once the survey is completed.

Because NPS is a standardized question, you can’t change the question text. To customize the question text, recreate the NPS question using the Rating question type instead.

To create an NPS survey for your email:

Add an NPS question. From the survey builder, select Add Question, then choose Net Promoter Score.
Remove the title page from the survey. Hover over the title page and select X, then select Delete. If you keep the title page, the survey won’t be submitted when a respondent chooses their answer.
Set the theme for your survey. Select Themes from the left-side survey builder, then choose your theme. The survey theme determines the color of your embedded NPS question.
(optional) Add an exit page to display after a respondent submits your survey. Select Add Exit Page from the survey builder, then create your page. Your exit page will open in the respondent's web browser after they take your survey. If you don't add an exit page, we'll show a default GetFeedback page.
Creating Your NPS Email

Once your survey is ready, you can create your email. You can choose from a few methods to send your email:

Send to a list or Salesforce report in GetFeedback
Set up automated emails using Salesforce
Set up automated emails using Zendesk
Create an HTML email template to send from your email provider
Create a Visualforce email template to send from Salesforce
Create a Pardot email template

Each option allows you to embed an NPS question into your email. Choose the distribution option that works best for you.

When creating your email:

For your email call to action, choose your NPS question. This embeds the NPS question into your email body.
Set up your email details, customize the body text, and add merge fields as needed. Each email option allows you to add merge fields to track data and personalize your email.
When you’re ready, send your email. Recipients can now use the embedded NPS question to quickly take and submit your survey.

Sending a Survey via Text Message

SurveyMonkey
Sending a Survey via Text Message

ENTERPRISE FEATURE: Text Message Collector

Paid feature
Log in to see if this feature is included in your plan.
Log in
Sign up free
How It Works

The Text Message collector lets customers on the US Data Center text people with a US, United Kingdom (UK), Canadian (CA), or Australian (AU) phone number a link to take your survey. Survey takers can open the link to take your survey in any survey language on their mobile phone.

When using the Text Message Collector, don't enter landline phone numbers. Messages sent to landlines will fail to deliver and still consume a text message credit, even though the recipient does not receive the survey.

Sending texts via SurveyMonkey helps you reach a large audience quickly, avoid spam filters, and make your survey more accessible to people on mobile devices. Anytime texts are sent, credits are deducted from your team's text balance.

The Primary Admin controls which members of the team can use the Text Message collector. If someone doesn't have access, they won't see the collector in Publish survey. If a survey with a Text Message collector is shared with someone who doesn't have access, they can see the collector in their collector list, but won't be able to send or create text messages.

Tip! You’re responsible for ensuring your survey and text messages are compliant with privacy laws. Learn more about data collection and privacy best practices.

Overview

1. Contact your Customer success manager (CSM) to get set up to send Text messages collector, or contact sales if you're not an Enterprise customer yet.

2. Design your survey

3. Create a Text Message collector to send your survey

4. Survey takers open the survey link in the text message to take your survey in a mobile browser

5. Track your sent text messages and analyze your results

Create a Text Message Collector

To send your survey via Text Message:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Choose Send a Text. If you already have a collector for your survey, select Text Message.
Add recipients.
Click Edit to identify your company name in the Message.
Edit the collector Options.
Optional: Click Test to send a test text.
Click Send.
Check the box to confirm that all SMS recipients have consented to receiving these text messages from me in accordance with applicable law, and I have identified my company in my message.
Click Send Text.

You can't customize the number the text is sent from.

Message

Your message needs to include your company name but can't contain links. You can add special characters, code, or emojis, but they may take up additional character space and count towards your character limit. Texts sent per recipient lets you know if 1 or 2 texts will be sent to each recipient.

If you can’t Save your message, shorten your message until you can.

Recipients will receive your custom message, the survey link, and the following opt out text, which isn’t editable:

Reply HELP for info. STOP to opt out. Msg&DataRatesMayApply

Expand | Collapse
Text Message Language

In the Design Survey section, you can change your survey language. The opt out text is automatically translated to this language, but you need to provide your own translations for your survey title, questions, and answers.

Don't share personal information other than your company name

Don’t include any personal information, for example people’s names or other information that identifies a person or business, other than your company name. If you include personal information in the text message and receive a Right to be Forgotten request, you may have to delete the entire collector and all responses it collected in order to fulfill the request.

Options

Update the collector options to control the survey taking experience or add restrictions to the survey. To add your team's custom domain, click on Custom URL under Options and select On, show a custom URL for survey.

Add Contacts

Contacts need to have a US, CA, UK, or AU phone number. AU customers are only able to text AU numbers. There are a couple ways to add recipients to your text message:

Type or paste phone numbers into the Send To field and hit enter. You can also add contact groups.
Click Add Contacts to import new contacts, upload a CSV spreadsheet, import from another site, or copy and paste a list of phone numbers.

Any new phone numbers you enter or import are saved in Contacts. You can add up to 5,000 contacts per text message. After you send your text message, you won't be able to send more texts with the same collector. But you can create a new collector for the same survey to send more texts.

Tip! Use custom data to include info you know about your survey takers in the survey results.

Import Formatting

SurveyMonkey automatically updates the format of your contacts’ information to E.164 format to help you avoid import errors.

Your recipient phone numbers are updated in the Send To field to include the country code and your contacts’ phone numbers are updated in the Send To field to include the country code and contact name if custom data is saved in your account. All non-numeric characters are removed. You can manually enter or import a CSV file with phone numbers in these formats:

US and CA	UK	AU
+1xxxxxxxxxx	+44xxxxxxxxxx
(E.164 format)	+61xxxxxxxxx
(xxx) xxx-xxxx	0xxxx xxxxxx
(Local format)	0xxx xxx xxx
xxxxxxxxxx	011 44 xxxx xxxxxx
(International US outbound format)	011 61 xxx xxx xxx
xxx-xxx-xxxx		
Import options and troubleshooting errors
Manual and CSV Import

If you’re pasting information using the manual import option or importing a CSV file, list the data in this order: Email address, Phone number, First name, Last name, Custom 1, Custom 2, etc. You can leave a blank space between commas or in a column cell if you don’t have information for a contact. If you see an error about invalid contacts or that “something went wrong” when you add recipients or try to send a text message, it means your list wasn't formatted correctly or you added duplicate, opted out, or bounced phone numbers.

TIP! View an image of an example CSV to see correct formatting.

Email Import
You can use Gmail, Yahoo! Mail, LinkedIn, Office 365, or Outlook.com to import all your contacts. If you make changes to contacts in your email account, they're not reflected in SurveyMonkey. Your SurveyMonkey account is not synced to those applications.
To add only some contacts or to import contacts from another email provider or site, go to your email account and export the contacts you want as a CSV file, then import the file to SurveyMonkey.
Outlook.com, the free web-based email service formerly known as Hotmail.com, differs from the Microsoft Office Outlook mail application. To import contacts from Microsoft Office Outlook, first export your contacts into a CSV file, and then import the file. Or ask your IT department if your Outlook application is powered by Office 365.
Troubleshoot Import Errors

If you see an error about invalid contacts or that “something went wrong” when you add contacts or try to send a text message, it means:

Your list wasn't formatted correctly, or
You added a duplicate, opted out, or bounced phone number.

Tidy up your manual list or spreadsheet, then try to import again. Here are some tips:

Don't import a spreadsheet with more than 1,000 phone numbers. Break your text message contacts into multiple CSV files with less than 1,000 rows each and import them to multiple collectors. Or copy and paste the rows of the spreadsheet using the manual import option.
Delete the header row from your spreadsheet. 
Make sure you're using an accepted delimiter for the spreadsheet (colon, semicolon, pipe, comma, or tab), and that your character encoding is in Unicode ( UTF-8 or UTF-16).
If you're using a Mac, try saving your file as MS-DOS Comma Separated (.csv). Go to File > Save As > Format.
Preview and Send Your Text Message

As you update your message and options, the mobile preview on the right shows a preview of your text.

Test Your Text Message

You can send a test text to any US, CA, UK, or AU phone number. The survey link in the test lets you preview the survey without recording any responses. Sending test messages may use up to 2 texts from your text balance.

Send Your Text Message

When you're ready, click Send. Make sure you're following our Acceptable Uses Policy and check the box to confirm that all SMS recipients have consented to receiving these text messages from me in accordance with applicable law, and I have identified my company in my message. It's your responsibility to only send surveys to people who have agreed to receive texts from you. Then you can click Send Text.

You can send up to 50,000 text messages within a rolling 24-hour period. If you need to send more than 50,000 text messages, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

It isn't possible to schedule a text message to send later, send reminder or thank you texts, or invite more recipients on the same collector. But you can create a new Text Message collector to send more texts.

Track Contacts and Analyze Your Results
Track Responses and Recipients

See the number of texts you sent, whether any phone numbers bounced, and the number of responses you received in the Overview tab.

You can see a list of recipients added to the collector and their individual response status from the Recipients tab. Click All recipients to filter recipients. If you want to edit recipient details, you can make edits in Contacts.

Expand | Collapse
Opted out or bounced phone numbers

You can’t send messages to people who have opted out or bounced. You can check for opted out or bounced phone numbers in the Recipients tab.

People who’ve opted out or bounced at some point in the past can opt back in if they want to take your survey. After they opt back in, you need to create a new Text Message collector to send them the survey (the old collector will continue to list them as opted out or bounced).

Delete recipients

If a recipient requests their Right to Erasure, the account holder needs to delete all the recipient's personal and response data.

To delete a recipient from the collector:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Open the Text Message collector used to send your survey.
Click on the Recipients tab.
Click on the recipient's row.
Click on Remove recipient record.

This removes the recipient from the Text Message collector. When you receive a Right to Erasure request, we also recommend that you:

Delete the individual's response
Delete the recipient's contact
Analyze Results

From the Analyze Results section of your survey, you can browse, filter, and compare responses. You can filter by collector or custom data to narrow down responses.

If your contacts include custom data, you can see it in individual responses or in responses data exports, unless anonymous responses was turned on.

Tip! Recipient phone numbers aren't included in Analyze Results, so we recommend using custom data to see identifiable info like first name, last name, or other useful data.

Team Settings
Allow People to Send Surveys by Text Message

By default, no one on the team has access to send surveys by text message. The Primary Admin controls whether people on your team can send surveys by text message. They also choose who can send surveys by text message—their entire team or only specific people.

If only specific people are allowed to send texts, the Primary Admin or Admin needs to turn on this setting for individuals from Manage Users.

Steps to manage users

To allow specific people to send surveys by text message:

Select My Team from the top navigation.
Select Manage Users.
Click the user's row to View User Details.
In the Individual Settings section, click the toggle to Allow this person to send surveys by text message.

Team members with access can create Text Message collectors. If access is disabled later, the team member won't be able to send or create new Text Message collectors, but they can see their existing collectors.

Text Balance

The Text Balance is the shared number of text messages your team can send through the Text Message collector. You can see your team's Text Balance as you create your Text Message collector and in the collector Overview tab.

If you need to text your survey to more people than your Text Balance allows, reach out to your Primary Admin—they can work with their Customer Success Manager to increase the text balance.

What Survey Takers Can Do

To take a survey, people can tap the link in the text to open the survey in a mobile browser.

Tip! If you're getting text message invitations, learn why, how to opt in or opt out, and how to report spam.

AI Features in SurveyMonkey

SurveyMonkey
AI Features in SurveyMonkey

We provide AI and machine learning features to help you create better surveys, gather higher-quality data, and find insights faster.

Data security and privacy are built into the design of our AI and machine learning features.

How AI Feature Access Works

Feature availability depends on your plan type and where your data is stored. Your account settings show all features available to you.

AI features are included as part of the core SurveyMonkey experience. If you prefer not to use AI, you can still create, send, and analyze surveys as you always have without using these tools. 

Some accounts may have additional AI feature settings available in their Admin dashboard. If your account has these settings, see Accounts with AI Feature Settings below for more details. 

Accounts with AI Feature Settings

Some Team and Enterprise accounts may have access to settings that allow Primary Admins to manage feature access. If your account has these settings, here are the features your Primary Admin can currently manage:

AI Features to Create a Survey, including Build with AI and Importing surveys with AI
Sentiment Analysis
Response Quality
Survey Insights, including Analyze with AI and Insights
Thematic Analysis

To manage AI feature access for your team, if applicable:

Select My Team.
Select Team Summary or Settings.
Select AI and machine learning (ML) feature access.
Use the toggle and checkboxes to manage access
How Your Data is Processed

We're transparent about how our AI and machine learning features handle your data. Here's what happens when you use each feature.

Feature	Description
AI features to create a survey, including Build with AI and importing surveys with AI	This setting turns on features that help you build and improve your survey. These features allow SurveyMonkey customers to create surveys assisted by generative AI, utilizing the Azure OpenAI or OpenAI service.
To provide survey creation features, your survey prompts and an encrypted user ID are shared with the Azure OpenAI or OpenAI Service. These third-party providers don’t use this data to train their models.
Sentiment Analysis	Sentiment Analysis uses our proprietary machine learning models to classify text responses as positive, negative, or neutral.
Response Quality	Response Quality uses our proprietary machine learning models to scan your survey data and flag low-quality responses. 
Survey Insights, including
Analyze with AI and Insights	This setting turns on features that help you get insights into your survey. These features use the Azure OpenAI service or OpenAI to deliver insights. When you use these features, your survey data—including survey title, survey questions, and response data—are shared with the Azure OpenAI service or OpenAI to generate insights about your survey. Any questions or prompts you enter are shared with OpenAI or Azure OpenAI. These third-party providers don't use this data to train their models.
Thematic Analysis	SurveyMonkey's Thematic Analysis feature uses AI to analyze, group, and summarize your open-ended responses. The feature processes your question and response text using a combination of a self-hosted Anthropic model and Azure OpenAI or OpenAI. Your data isn't used to train any of these providers' AI models. We also mask common data types, like phone numbers and social security numbers, to reduce exposure of potentially sensitive data.

OneDrive Integration

SurveyMonkey
OneDrive Integration

SurveyMonkey's integration with Microsoft OneDrive lets you store a file of your survey or results in OneDrive. You can then share this asset just like you would any other file in OneDrive.

Install the integration from our App Directory. The integration setup is only available in English.

Sharing a SurveyMonkey File from OneDrive

You can share your .survey or .results files just like you would any other file in OneDrive. However, what the person you're sharing with can see when they open it depends on the permissions they have for the survey in SurveyMonkey.

If you're sharing a .survey or .results file with someone who is a Full access collaborator on your SurveyMonkey team, they'll have access to the survey or results within their SurveyMonkey account. If you're sharing it with someone who isn't on your team, .survey files will open in a preview and test view and .results files will open as a shared data page.

To share a survey or results:

Install the OneDrive integration.
Choose Surveys or Surveys + Responses.
Search for and select the survey you want to share with OneDrive.
To share responses, select a collector or Select All for all collectors.
Click Select a folder to choose the OneDrive location to save the survey or responses to.
Log into OneDrive to view the survey or individual responses where you saved them.
Select the three dots (...) next to a survey or response to open and view it within SurveyMonkey.

TIP! Creating a survey you want to share with your SurveyMonkey team? Learn how to manage viewing and editing permissions.

Tracking & Anonymity

Tracking Respondents

SurveyMonkey
Tracking Respondents

Before you send your survey, decide if you want to track who’s taken your survey or if you want to keep responses anonymous.

You need to set up your survey to track respondents before you send it out. It's not possible to start tracking responses after the survey is sent.

Ways to Track Respondents
Tracking Method	Description
Email Invitation Collector (Recommended)	

Sending an Email Invitation is the best way to track respondents. An Email Invitation lets you track:

How many people opened your email
How many people clicked through to the survey
Who responded to your survey


Web Link Collector	

When you use a Web Link collector to send your survey, you can use these tracking options:

Add the Name or Email address question to your survey design and make it required so people must submit an identifier with their survey response. Add Custom Variables to your survey design to pass known information through a survey link and into your survey results.
If you have an Enterprise team with SSO enabled, turn on Respondent Authentication. This means respondents need to log in through SSO to access your survey and their profile information is tracked with their response.


Text Message Collector
(Enterprise only)	A text message collector tracks the number of texts you sent, whether any phone numbers bounced, the number of responses you received, and individual response status from the collector’s Overview and Recipients tabs.
Recipient phone numbers aren't included in Analyze Results, so we recommend using custom data to see identifiable info like first name, last name, or other useful data.
Embedded Survey Collector	When using an Embedded Survey, it is not possible to track respondents unless you ask for identifying information within the survey questions.
If you want to embed a survey and track respondents, you can use a Web Link collector with Custom Variables and embed it yourself by using an iframe or another method that works with your existing setup.
IP Address	By default, most collectors track the IP address of your respondents as response metadata. However, if you turn on Anonymous Responses, your respondents’ IP addresses won't be tracked.
If you want to track other identifying information, make sure to also choose another tracking method.

Turning On Response Editing
Response Editing Options
How are responses saved?
Hiding the Previous Button
Editing Responses in Your Results
Help
Sending Surveys
Collecting Responses

Editing Survey Responses

SurveyMonkey
Editing Survey Responses

You can allow respondents to edit their responses later. You can also edit a respondent's response in your results.

Turning On Response Editing

To allow respondents to edit or change their survey responses:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Click the name of your collector.
From the collector options, click Response Editing.
Choose one of the available Response Editing options for your collector type.

Accepting Payments limitation Respondents won't be able to edit their responses after they submit a payment, even when response editing is on.

Response Editing Options

You can allow people who take your survey to edit their responses either while completing the survey or after they submit the survey, or you can prevent respondents from editing their responses after they submit them.

The available Response Editing options depend on the collector type you're using.

Expand | Collapse
Web Link or Website Collectors

The Multiple Responses setting affects your Response Editing options when using a Web Link collector or Website collector.

Multiple Responses is Off

If you allow one response per computer, you can allow editing even after the survey is submitted.

In order for this setting to work properly, the respondent must use the same device and web browser they used to start the survey on because a cookie is stored in the respondent's browser that remembers their survey responses.

Option	Description
On, until survey is completed or exited	Respondents can change their answers on any survey page until they complete the survey or exit the survey. Respondents can return to the survey to pick up where they left off and/or edit previous responses until they click the Done button or until you close the collector.
On, always	Respondents can change their answers on any survey page even after they complete the survey. Respondents can return to the survey to pick up where they left off and/or edit previous responses until you close the collector.
Off	Respondents can’t change their answers once they leave a survey page.After respondents submit a survey page by clicking Next or Done, the Previous button is hidden. Respondents can continue to access the survey to pick up where they left off until they click the Done button or until you close the collector.
Multiple Responses is On

If you allow multiple responses per computer, you can allow editing during the survey, but not after the survey is submitted or exited.

In order for this setting to work properly, no cookie is stored in the respondent’s browser to remember their survey responses. If the survey is accessed from the same browser multiple times, the collector registers each time as a new respondent.

Option	Description
On, until survey is completed or exited	Respondents can change their answers on any survey page until they complete or exit the survey. If respondents exit the survey and go back to it, it records a new response—it doesn't update their existing response.
Off	Respondents can’t change their answers once they leave a survey page.After respondents submit a survey page by clicking Next or Done, the Previous button is hidden. Respondents can continue to access the survey to pick up where they left off until they click the Done button or until you close the collector.
Email Invitation Collector

If you're using an Email Invitation Collector, the Multiple Responses setting doesn't affect your Response Editing options.

A respondent can edit their survey responses from any computer since their responses are tied to their email address and not a cookie in their browser.

Option	Description
On, until survey complete	Respondents can change their answers on any survey page until they complete the survey. Respondents can return to the survey to pick up where they left off and/or edit previous responses until they click the Done button or until you close the collector.
On, always	Respondents can change their answers on any survey page even after they complete the survey. Respondents can return to the survey to pick up where they left off and/or edit previous responses until you close the collector.
Off	Respondents can’t change their answers once they leave a survey page.After respondents submit a survey page by clicking Next or Done, the Previous button is hidden. Respondents can continue to access the survey to pick up where they left off until they click the Done button or until you close the collector.
Target Audience Collector

If you buy survey responses using SurveyMonkey Audience, your survey is sent through the Target Audience Collector.

We remove the Previous button from surveys sent when they're sent through Audience, so it's not possible for respondents to go back to previous pages to edit their responses. Additionally, if a respondent exits the survey, they can't access it again or pick up where they left off.

How are responses saved?

Responses are saved and submitted when a respondent clicks the Next or Done button on each page of the survey, or when they answer the first question embedded in an email invitation if In-email Response Capture is turned on and the question doesn’t have an Other Textbox or Comment field. Responses don’t automatically save as each question is answered—they are saved and submitted page by page as respondents progress through the survey.

TIP! If the survey is a single page, all responses are submitted at once when a respondent clicks the Done button. If the respondent doesn’t click the Done button, they will need to take the survey again to submit their responses.

Hiding the Previous Button

If you choose to turn Response Editing off, respondents can still edit answers when they're on a given survey page, but not on previous pages—the Previous button is hidden from respondents when they're taking your survey.

However, when previewing your survey design, you'll still be able to use the Previous button to go back and edit responses because collector options aren't active when using a preview link.

TIP! If you don't allow response editing, edit the survey introduction to explain to respondents that they won't be able to go back to edit previous pages once they have submitted them.

Editing Responses in Your Results

Edit a survey response from the Individual Responses page in your survey results. You can edit responses from both the Table and Single view.

To edit a response in Table view:

Go to the Analyze Results section of your survey.
Click the Individual Responses tab.
Find the response you want to edit. You can select a column header to sort responses by that column.
Click the Edit button on the right side of the table. The survey will open in a new browser window or tab, based on your settings.
Go through each page, editing the answers as needed.
Click the Done button on the survey to save the response.

To edit a response in Single view:

Go to the Analyze Results section of your survey.
Click the Individual Responses tab.
Use the left and right arrows to find the response you want to edit.
Click the Edit button in the upper-right corner of the grey box containing the respondent's metadata. The survey will open in a new browser window or tab, based on your settings.
Go through each page, editing the answers as needed
Click the Done button on the survey to save the response.

Editing a survey response in a table or single view reassigns it to the end of the data list. For example, if you edit response #5 in a list of 10 survey responses, our system lists the response as #10.

Getting more surveys (iOS only)

Here are some tips for getting matched with the most possible surveys so you can get rewards faster.

Complete your profile

When your profile is 100% complete, we can match you with more surveys that are relevant to you.

To complete your profile:

Go to your profile and check if it's complete.
Click Complete profile.
Answer questions about yourself.
Turn on push notifications

Surveys only stay open for a certain amount of time, so push notifications help you make sure you don't miss a new survey opportunity.

To turn on push notifications:

Open Settings on your device.
Scroll through your list of apps and tap Rewards.
Tap Notifications.
Toggle Allow Notifications on.
Getting more surveys (Android only)

Here are some tips for getting matched with the most possible surveys so you can get rewards faster.

Complete your profile

When your profile is 100% complete, we can match you with more surveys that are relevant to you.

To complete your profile:

Go to your profile.
Check if your profile's complete. If not, tap Complete profile.
Answer the questions about yourself.
Turn on push notifications

Surveys only stay open for a certain amount of time, so push notifications help you make sure you don't miss a new survey opportunity.

To turn on push notifications:

Open Settings on your device.
Tap Apps.
Tap Rewards in the list of your apps.

Select Show notifications.

Deleting your account

You can delete your SurveyMonkey Rewards account from the My account page.

To delete your account:

Tap the Profile icon to go to the My account page.
Tap My account.
Tap Delete account.
Enter your password and tap Delete account to confirm.
Credits and rewards
Earning credits

You'll earn credits each time you complete a survey, as long as the responses aren’t flagged for poor response quality.

You'll also earn credits every 3rd time you get disqualified from a survey. You may be disqualified from surveys if you don't match the target audience.

Redeeming credits for rewards

Any time you have $5 or more in credits, you can redeem your credits for a reward. You can always check how many credits you have on the rewards page.

To redeem credits for a reward:

Click the Trophy icon to go to the Rewards page.
Click Donate or Redeem.
The first time you redeem credits, we'll ask you to go through phone verification to make sure you're not a robot.
Once you complete verification, click Donate Now or Redeem Now.
Check your email. If you redeem credits for a gift card, you get an email with a claim code you can use to add the gift card to your Amazon.com account. If you redeemed credits for a donation, you get confirmation that the donation was completed.
Reward options

There are two reward options to choose from:

Gift Card: Choose between Prizeout or an Amazon.com Gift Card. If you redeem $5 in credits, you'll get a $5 gift card.
Prizeout Instant Gift Cards lets you choose from hundreds of gift card options on Prizeout's platform.
Amazon.com Gift Cards give you access to millions of eligible goods and services at Amazon.com.
Donation: We match donations, so if you redeem $5 in credits, SurveyMonkey will donate a total of $10 to the charity you selected.

To change your reward option:

Click the Trophy icon to go to the Rewards page.
Click Change in the upper-right corner of the card.
Choose a reward option—Gift Card or Donation.
Click Confirm.
If you choose Donation, select a charity from the list.
