Getting a Web Link for Your Survey

SurveyMonkey
Getting a Web Link for Your Survey

The Web link collector lets you share a URL or QR code linking to your survey. You can send or post your survey anywhere you want—like on social media, in an email (using your own email client), or print it on a newsletter.

By default, your survey URL will look something like this, with a string of letters and numbers at the end:

https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/P58B9BX

TIP! Download a QR code for your survey to print on pamphlets, flyers, or posters.

Getting a Web Link

Once you go to Publish Survey, you can send your survey using the default web link provided or by choosing another collector option.

From the Web link section, you can:

Copy the URL to use the default link.
Select Settings, then Customize to change the URL ending, domain, or subdomain.
You can’t set up a recurrence if you customize the web link.

To create a new Web link:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Select Add new collector +.
Select Share a link.
Choose your collector options.
(Optional): Customize the web link.
(Optional): Edit the nickname of the collector by selecting the pencil icon—nicknames don't show to respondents.
Sharing Your Link on Social Media or Email

Use the icons below the URL to share your survey on Facebook, X, LinkedIn, Microsoft Teams, or WhatsApp, or send using your own email client.

The Thumbnail Image & Text collector option lets you customize how your survey title, description, or image displays on social media or messaging apps.

Expand the social media section for additional details on posting your survey there.

Expand | Collapse
Facebook

To post your survey link to Facebook:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Create a Web link collector.
Choose your collector options.
Select the Facebook icon.
Facebook opens in a new window and you may need to log in.
Add a note to the post or leave it blank. You can edit your post at any time in Facebook, but it isn’t possible to change the default image associated with the Facebook post.
Select whether to post your survey to your News Feed or Your Story, and edit the audience dropdown to choose who can see your post. Learn more about privacy settings in Facebook's Help Center.
Select Share.

To view or edit your post, open Facebook in a new tab.

Managing your Facebook Survey

The Facebook Sharing collector option controls whether your Facebook friends can post your survey on their Timeline or share it with their network.

When Facebook Sharing is On, your friends will be able to edit the Facebook message associated with the post and share it, but the SurveyMonkey headline and message can’t be edited.

When Facebook Sharing is Off, friends won’t see the Share option, but they may still be able to copy and paste the survey link from their browser to share on their own.

X

To post your survey link to X:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Create a Web link collector.
Choose your collector options.
Select the X icon.
Edit your post. You won’t be able to edit your post once it’s shared.
Select Post.

The X window closes automatically. To view your post, open X in a new tab.

LinkedIn

To post your survey link to LinkedIn:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Create a Web link collector.
Choose your collector options.
Select the LinkedIn icon.
Choose your Post settings (who can see your post).
Customize your post or message.
Select Post.

The LinkedIn window closes automatically. To view your post or message, open LinkedIn a new tab.

WhatsApp

To send your survey in WhatsApp:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Create a Web link collector.
Choose your collector options.
Select the WhatsApp icon.
Choose the contact you want to send the survey to.
Add a custom message to go with your survey link. 
Select Send. 
Microsoft Teams

Select the Teams icon to open Microsoft Teams and Share the survey with a person, group, or channel. You can add a personalized message to the survey link and select Share.

If it’s your first time connecting SurveyMonkey to Teams, you may need to select My Surveys from the SurveyMonkey Chat and select Continue to Authorize the app connection. 

Once connected, you’re able to utilize all the functionality of the Microsoft Teams integration.

Web Links are Public Links

Your survey link is a public link, meaning that anyone who has it will be able to access your survey and complete it. Web crawlers and search engines can also find and list your survey online.

Collector Options

It isn't possible to transfer or reuse a SurveyMonkey generated URL ending.

Depending on your plan, you can create a Custom URL ending or use the White label URL to remove SurveyMonkey branding from your web link. If you customize the URL after you send the survey out, both the old link and the new link will work.

You can’t create a Custom URL Ending if you have the Recurrence collector option turned on.

Tracking Respondents

If you want to track respondents, choose the tracking method you want to use before sending your survey.

By default, Web link collectors record IP addresses. However, this information can't really help you track respondents. Instead, you can add required questions to your survey to collect identifying information from respondents, or you can use Custom variables.

Or, you can use an Email invitation instead of a Web link to track respondents.

Create a Copy of a Web Link

Copying a web link creates a new link for you to share a previous survey at a different time or with new respondents.

To create a copy of a Web link collector:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Select ... next to the Web link collector you want to copy.
Select Copy collector.

A new Web Link starting with Copy of is added to the Publish survey section of your survey.

Most of your customized collector options apply to the copied web link. To review and edit your collector options before sending your survey, select Edit collector from the survey's three dot dropdown.

Copied Collector Options
Collector option	Copied from original web link
Custom Thank You	✅
Survey End Page	✅
Multiple Responses	✅
Response Editing	✅
Anonymous Responses	✅
Instant Results	✅
Response Limits	✅
IP Restrictions	✅
Custom Disqualification	✅
Thumbnail Image and Text	❌
Recurrence	❌
Respondent Authentication	❌
Cutoff Date and Time	❌
Password Protection	❌

Enterprise Features

Enterprise Settings

SurveyMonkey
Enterprise Settings

Enterprise Feature: If you're interested in an Enterprise plan, contact sales.
Default Respondent Authentication and Anonymous Responses settings are available to all Enterprise customers. The other features in this article are Enterprise add-ons—contact your Customer Success Manager to add it to your team.

If you’re the Primary Admin of an Enterprise team, you can access the Settings section in My Team to set default settings and permissions for your entire team.

Manage Collectors and Collector Settings

You can set default collector types and collector options for your entire Enterprise team, control whether people can change these default selections, and allow or restrict the types of collectors your team can use to send surveys.

The default settings are applied to all future collectors your team creates. Existing collectors—including recurring surveys—don't change, but can be edited to match the default settings.

Collector Types
Expand | Collapse
Restrict collector types

This Restrict Collector Types setting lets you choose the collector types your team can use to send surveys. If a collector type is disabled, your team will see it greyed out in the Collect Responses section.

Any existing and open collectors created before the default settings were made can be used until they're closed.

To restrict the collector types your team can use:

Select My Team from the top navigation.
Select Settings.
Click Collectors.
Scroll to the Restrict Collector Types section.
Uncheck the collector types you don't want your team to use.
Select the collector types you do want your team to use. At least one collector type must be selected.

You can’t disable the Target Audience collector.

Allow people to send surveys by text message

The Primary Admin controls whether people on your team can send surveys by text message. By default, no one on the team has access to send surveys by text message.

To let people send surveys by text message:

Select My Team from the top navigation.
Select Settings.
Click the Collector tile.
Under Text Message Collector, click the toggle to Allow people to send surveys by text message.
Select whether your Entire team or Specific people can send surveys by text message.
If you select Specific people, the Primary Admin or an Admin can turn on this setting for individuals in Manage Users.

Team members you give access to can create Text Message collectors. If you disable access later, team members won't be able to send or create new Text Message collectors, but they can see their existing collectors.

Collector Settings

Whether or not team members can change these settings in individual collectors depends on whether the default settings were locked in Settings or conflict within a web link collector.

Expand | Collapse
Respondent Authentication

The Respondent Authentication setting on the web link collector is available to teams with SSO enabled. When Respondent Authentication is enabled, survey takers are required to log in through SSO to access the survey, and their responses are tracked with this SSO metadata.

You can set the default Respondent Authentication collector option for all new web link collectors.

Once you select a default setting, you can choose to lock it so no one on your team can change it.

To set the team default:

Select My Team from the top navigation.
Select Settings.
Click Collectors.
Under Respondent Authentication (Web Link Collector Only), toggle Set a team default.
Toggle Turn Respondent Authentication on or off by default.
(Optional) Check Lock default setting so no one on your team can change your preferred setting.

If the default settings for Respondent Authentication and Anonymous Responses are both On, the default options on web link collectors will update.

Anonymous Responses

The Anonymous Responses setting lets you control the level of anonymity for any collector type. Enabling this default setting helps enforce company policies or prevent users on the team from capturing info like Personally Identifiable Information (PII).

You can set the Anonymous Responses team default to one of the following:

Not anonymous—all available respondent info is included in results.
Partially anonymous—applies to Email Invitations only. Custom data is passed through to results, but all other respondent info is excluded. Any other collector types default to fully anonymous.
Fully anonymous—no respondent info is included in results.

Once you select a default setting, you can choose to lock it so no one on your team can change it.

To set a team default:

Select My Team from the top navigation.
Select Settings.
Click Collectors.
Under the Anonymous Responses section, toggle Set a team default.
Select a default anonymity setting—Not anonymous, Partially anonymous, or Fully anonymous.
(Optional) Check Lock default setting so no one on your team can change your preferred setting.

If the default settings for Respondent Authentication and Anonymous Responses are both On, the default options on web link collectors will update.

How Respondent Authentication and Anonymous Responses work together

Because the Respondent Authentication feature always records the SSO profile information for everyone that takes the survey, responses can't be anonymous when Respondent Authentication is turned on.

So, while you're able to turn on both Respondent Authentication and Anonymous Responses by default in Settings, both of these settings won't actually be reflected in new Web Link collectors your team creates. Instead, Respondent Authentication will remain turned on, and responses won't be anonymous.

If Respondent Authentication is unlocked and Anonymous Responses is locked, people in your team can turn off Respondent Authentication, and the Anonymous Responses setting will automatically update to match the locked default setting.

What Your Team Will See
Expand | Collapse
Collector Options

The team's default settings are automatically applied to new collectors. If the default setting is locked, team members can't change the setting. If unlocked, team members can change it, but we recommend keeping the default selected by your Admin.

Anyone on the team can update existing collectors to match the team’s default preference, but if the default setting is locked, team members won't be able to change it back.

If the default settings for Respondent Authentication and Anonymous Responses are both On, the default options on web link collectors will update.

Available collectors

Team members can see all collector types in the Collect Responses section. If a collector type is greyed out, it can't be used to send your survey because the Primary Admin disabled it.

Roles and permissions

You can create custom roles that will give team members more or less access, depending on how they use SurveyMonkey. Give seats on your team access to certain features, and administrative functions in the following permission areas: Manage users, team-wide settings, manage team credits, team library, Division management, and advanced access and permissions.

Response Manager

If a respondent asks you or someone on your team to erase their response data, you can search across your team and filter by Email Invitation and Text Message collector metadata to find and delete applicable responses. Depending on where you and your respondents are located, you may be required to respond to requests from people who ask to exercise their data privacy rights.

To find and delete survey responses:

Select My Team from the top navigation.
Select Settings.
Click Survey response management.
Click Search responses.
In the new tab Response Manager, filter your team's responses by at least one of these criteria: Email, First name, Last name, or Custom field.
(Optional) Filter your team’s responses by Date.
Click Apply Filters.
Click Delete Responses.
Confirm you want to delete responses.

Filters let you search for respondent metadata—results won't include responses where name or email was collected as survey data.

Permissions to Buy Responses

Your Enterprise Team may use Budgets instead to manage credits.

You can restrict users in your team from buying SurveyMonkey Audience responses unless they get your approval.

To set permissions to buy responses:

Toggle Users can buy responses without Admin approval on or off

Off	Users can't buy SurveyMonkey Audience responses without your approval. Users need to request Audience Credits and you can transfer credits to the user so they can purchase responses.

When a user requests credits, you’ll get a notification email. You can manage all credit balances from the Manage Credits tab.

Accessibility When Using SurveyMonkey

SurveyMonkey
Accessibility When Using SurveyMonkey

SurveyMonkey encourages web accessibility and provides tools to help you create more accessible  surveys. This article offers tips for creating surveys with Section 508 and Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2 (WCAG2) in mind. 

To start off, get to know some common accessibility terms, and learn how you can create accessible surveys or use assistive technology to navigate SurveyMonkey surveys.

Download SurveyMonkey's Accessibility Conformance Report - VPAT v2.5 - WCAG 2.2 Level AA (updated September 2026) »

Accessibility Terms

Here are common accessibility terms, their acronym, and description:

Term and Acronym	Description
508 Compliance	Section 508 is a United States (US) federal law addressing accessibility of digital technology developed, bought, maintained, or used by federal agencies.

Web Content Accessibility
Guidelines 2
(WCAG2)	WCAG2 is a set of internationally used guidelines for making digital content more accessible to people with disabilities.

The guidelines help you evaluate the accessibility of your survey or form based on 4 accessibility principles:

Is my survey Perceivable? Is info easy to see or hear, or access via other human senses?
Is my survey Operable? Ensure it’s clear to navigate and interact with, since anyone should be able to move around the survey, even if they cannot use a mouse and instead use their voice or a keyboard.
Is my survey Understandable? Make sure survey content and structure isn't confusing, it's easy to read.
Is my survey Robust? Will screen helper technology, like software that reads the screen out loud or magnification tools to zoom in on text, work with your survey.

Voluntary Product 
Accessibility Template
(VPAT)	This is a template companies use to log how their product supports accessibility standards.
A completed VPAT is called an Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR).

The Scope: The product and features evaluated.
The Test: How the product was evaluated against accessibility criteria.
The Results: Which criteria the product supports, partially supports, or does not support, with explanations.
Customers can use a completed VPAT to learn how a product supports accessibility when evaluating software.

Accessibility Conformance Report
(ACR)	The ACR describes how the assessed survey-taking experience supports the accessibility criteria listed in the report. 

Download SurveyMonkey's
Accessibility Conformance Report - VPAT v2.5 - WCAG 2.2 Level AA (updated September 2026) »

Assistive Technology
(AT)	Any software, hardware, or tool that helps a person with a disability use a computer or complete a task.

Some include:

Screen readers which reads the text on a screen out loud for users who are blind or have low vision.
Screen magnifiers zoom in on parts of a screen to make text and images much bigger for users with low vision.


Americans with Disabilities Act
(ADA)	The ADA is another US civil rights law addressing accessibility. SurveyMonkey isn’t evaluated on our ADA accessibility.

Compliance with Section 508 and WCAG2

You can use  SurveyMonkey’s features and the checklist below to help create more accessible surveys with Section 508 and WCAG2 standards in mind. Accessibility also depends on your survey content, questions, and settings. 

What is an accessible SurveyMonkey survey?

An accessible survey:

Is designed so that people with varying hearing, movement, sight, and cognitive abilities can complete it.

Enables respondents using screen magnifiers to successfully complete the survey.

Has the text elements to enable a survey taker to successfully navigate and complete a survey using a screen reader—assistive software that converts on-screen text into audio using a text-to-speech (TTS) system.

Can be completed using voice recognition software.

Doesn't require a mouse or keyboard to complete.

Creating Accessible Surveys
Themes and Color Contrast

Accessible themes are designed with color contrast and brightness in mind to help more people use your survey, including people with colorblindness.

Our default survey theme, Catalyst, along with Heritage or Arctic themes, support accessible survey design. Avoid adjusting the colors or style settings of the theme without checking the effect on color contrast.

Look for the accessible survey icon to help you choose a theme.

Custom Themes

To keep surveys accessible, please don’t make changes to accessible themes. 

If you create a custom theme, you can use a tool like the Tanaguru contrast finder to check whether the color combinations meet  WCAG 2.2 Level AA standards for contrast ratios.

Accessible Surveys Checklist

To help make your survey more accessible, make sure you:

✅ Use an accessible theme, displayed with an accessibility icon.

✅ Choose question types and settings with accessibility in mind.

❌ Avoid these question types and settings:
Matrix of Dropdown menus question type
Click Map question type
Accepting payments page
Multilingual Surveys— People using a screen reader won't be able to select their preferred language from the dropdown menu
Forced Ranking setting for a matrix/rating scale question type

✅ Images and videos need alternative text (alt text). Images can't be seen or read by all, so add a short description of the image to be stored in the code for assistive technology's use
Our various features all let you add alt text:

Image choice question
Freestanding survey images
Image A/B Tests
Logo

Videos in your survey should include closed captions, text displayed on a video showing what people say and describe sounds,like [music playing] or [door slams]) for people who are deaf or hard of hearing.

❌ Don't include images that blink or flash. If using animated content in your survey, check that it meets the time refresh requirements.

✅ Clearly identify required questions in text.
By default, requiring a question adds an asterisk next to the question. Keep the asterisk, but don’t rely on it alone to explain which questions are required.  You can also use a survey introduction to let respondents know that the question is required.

✅ Set your Star rating question icons to black, and check how they appear to respondents.

✅ Write clear error messages for respondents who enter an invalid response to a question with answer validation applied or skip a required question.
This way, an error message appears  to guide them. Customize the error text so that people know specifically how to answer the question, so they can move forward in the survey.

✅ Place text fields close to row labels on Multiple Textboxes or Matrix/Rating Scale questions, adjust the question layout to keep the Labels and Text fields close together.
When a row label is positioned far away from the text field, it may cause issues for screen magnifiers. 

✅ Use Page titles for Heading 2 (H2). If you want to use an H2 in your heading rank, turn on page titles. See below for details on Headings.

✅ Use the Email Invitation or Web Link to send your survey. 

❌ Other ways of sending your survey may not be accessible. Check accessibility before using another method.

❌ Don’t set your Survey Format to the One Question at a Time or Conversation survey format, as these aren’t accessible.

❌ Don't edit default Navigation buttons without checking how the new labels work with a screen reader.
By default, navigation buttons are labeled Previous, Next, and Done, which work well with screen readers.

❌ Don't password protect your survey.
The page to enter a password isn't accessible.

Taking Surveys with a Screen Reader
Screen Readers We Support
JAWS
NVDA
VoiceOver
TalkBack

Screen reader experiences can vary by question type and survey settings - see exceptions listed in the accessible surveys checklist.
For the best survey taking experience, we recommend using the most updated version of one of our supported browsers.

Headings

The table describes what each heading level represents in a SurveyMonkey survey. Some headings may not work as expected with a screen reader. Please check your preferred screen reader's manual to learn how to navigate surveys.

Heading Level	Description
Heading 1	Survey title
Heading 2	Page title
Heading 3	Page description
Heading 4	Navigate between error messages and questions in a survey
When taking a survey, you can use your screen reader to navigate the list of questions by navigating between elements at heading level 4. Heading structure can vary.
If you receive error messages when submitting a page, use your screen reader to navigate heading level 4 to move between questions with error messages. Some error messages may not be announced as expected.

SurveyMonkey surveys don't use heading levels 5 and 6.

Feedback

SurveyMonkey is dedicated to helping people create surveys that are accessible. If you have feedback on how we can do better, please complete the SurveyMonkey Accessibility Feedback Form.

While we may not be able to respond to your feedback directly, your comments can help us identify areas to improve.

Customizing Survey Links

SurveyMonkey
Customizing Survey Links

When sending out your survey, you can customize your survey link by using a Custom URL Ending, as well as changing the Domain, and changing the Subdomain.

Custom URL Ending

Custom URL Ending

Paid feature
Log in to see if this feature is included in your plan.
Log in
Sign up free

You can create a Custom URL Ending to make your link more relevant to your survey and respondents. The URL ending is the part of the URL that comes after the /r/ in a survey link. By default, SurveyMonkey randomly generates a string of numbers and letters.

www.surveymonkey.com/r/your_custom_ending

You can use a Custom URL Ending only for Web link collectors. It's not available for other collector types.

You can't customize your URL ending for Web Links with the Recurrence collector option turned on. If you create a Custom URL Ending, the Recurrence is automatically disabled—and vice versa.

To create a Custom URL Ending:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Click the Web Link or Social Media Collector you want to edit.
Click Customize of Link settings to the right of the survey link.
Enter a Custom URL Ending (100 characters or less).
Click Save.
Expand | Collapse
Supported Characters
Alphanumeric characters (A to Z, a to z, and 0 to 9)
Hyphens (-)
Underscores (_)

Spaces or special characters are not accepted.

Transferring a Custom URL Ending

You can transfer a Custom URL Ending to another one of your Web Link Collectors. However, the same URL cannot be used on two collectors at once.

To transfer a Custom URL Ending:

Go to the Web Link you wish to transfer the URL to.
Click Customize.
Type in the Custom URL Ending. Click Save.
Click Transfer URL. The URLs for both collectors will update.

It isn't possible to transfer a SurveyMonkey generated URL ending.

Deleting a Collector with a Custom URL Ending

If you delete a collector with a Custom URL Ending, you may not be able to use it on a future collector. If you'd like to re-use a Custom URL Ending, we recommend not deleting the collector until you transfer the Custom URL Ending to a new collector.

Tip! If you customize the URL after you send the survey out, both the original link and the customized link will work.

Changing the Domain

White Label URL

Paid feature
Log in to see if this feature is included in your plan.
Log in
Sign up free

You can also change the domain of your survey link to use the White Label URL. You can choose the domain research.net to create a White Label URL for your survey.

www.research.net/r/your_custom_ending

Your Default Domain

When you change your default domain preference, new collectors you create will use the domain you select. Existing collectors aren't affected.

To change your default domain preference:

Click your Profile circle in the upper-right corner of your account.
Click My Account from the drop-down menu.
Scroll to General Preferences.
Next to Survey Domain, click Edit to change your preference. This change applies to future collectors you create. You'll need to manually update the domain for existing collectors.
Changing the Subdomain

Enterprise Add-On: Requesting a custom subdomain is only available to customers on Enterprise. If you're interested, contact sales. If you already have an Enterprise account, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

You can also change the subdomain of your survey link to make your organization more recognizable to respondents, if your data is stored in the US or EU data centers.

https://customsubdomain.surveymonkey.com/r/your_custom_ending

https://customsubdomain.research.net/r/your_custom_ending

You can then choose this to be your default domain preference by following the steps above in Your Default Domain.

If your data is stored in the CA data center, your URLs display the country prefix instead of the subdomain (e.g. ca.research.net).

Your Collector's Domain
Web Link

To change the domain of your survey link:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Click the name of the collector.
Click Customize to the right of the survey link.
Click the down arrow to choose your preferred domain.
Click Save.
Email Invitation

When you use the White Label URL in an Email Invitation Collector, both the survey link and the URL respondents see in the From field of the email invitation use research.net.

To change the domain of your survey link:

Go to the Publish survey section of your survey.
Click the name of the collector.
Go to the collector options. If you've already sent an invitation, go to the Options tab. When sending your first invitation message in the collector, you'll choose collector options after composing your message.
Click Custom URL and change your preference.

This will affect any new messages you send. It's not possible to change the survey link of messages that were already sent.

Text Message

If you're a Primary Admin or Admin of an Enterprise team, you can enable your team's custom domain when using the Text Message collector. To add your team's custom domain, click on Custom URL under Options and select On, show a custom URL for survey.

Other Collector Types

It's not possible to directly edit the domain of an existing survey link in other collector types. Please edit your default domain and create a new collector to ensure the White Label URL is being used.

SurveyMonkey App FAQs
General
What features are included in the SurveyMonkey app?

After creating your account, we may ask you questions to better understand you or your organization's goals—like your company name or industry. Your profile let us personalize recommendations and your experience to better fit your use case.

Use the app to create new surveys, or monitor existing surveys.

The app includes the following features:

Edit

Create a survey from scratch, a template, or Build with AI
Add, edit, or delete questions
Add prewritten questions from our Question Bank
Add descriptive text or images
Choose to show or hide the survey title, page title, question numbers, or exit link
Change the survey language
Change the theme colors
Move questions
Add or delete pages

Send

Send web link collectors via your mobile email client, Facebook, Twitter, or text. Or, just copy the link from the app to distribute in other ways
Allow multiple responses per device
Use kiosk mode to collect responses directly on your device

Analyze

View pie charts, donut charts, or bar graphs of your results
Filter responses
Show or hide certain questions
Browse individual responses
Share responses

Managing surveys

Use folders
Delete surveys

Account
Authenticating your account (Android only)

If you're having trouble authenticating your account on your Android device, you may need to change your default browser to Chrome for the authentication process to complete.

Check your phone manufacturer’s website for more info on how to change your default browser.

Upgrading Your Account (iOS only)

You can upgrade to a Standard monthly or Standard annual plan within the SurveyMonkey app. If you are interested in upgrading to an Advantage, Premier, or Enterprise plan, you can from our desktop site.

Upgrading to Standard activates paid features such as unlimited questions and unlimited filters. You can also access the full set of Standard features when you access SurveyMonkey on our desktop site.

To upgrade in the app:

From the Home screen, tap the three lines icon to access the menu.
Tap Upgrade.
Tap either the Monthly or Annual option to go to the iTunes Store.
Complete your purchase in the iTunes store.

You can only upgrade one account for your Apple ID. If you need to upgrade additional accounts, please do so on our desktop site.

Upgrading from Standard to a Higher Plan

If you've already purchased a Standard plan through the iOS app and would like to upgrade your account to a higher plan type, please contact support. Since in-app purchases are handled by iTunes billing rather than SurveyMonkey, our support team needs to help you upgrade your account.

Upgrading Your Account (Android only)

You can no longer upgrade your account in-app for Android devices.

To make changes to your plan, you can upgrade your account on the desktop site. Once you upgrade, you can download the app in Google Play, and log in with your SurveyMonkey username and password.

SurveyMonkey and Privacy Rights

SurveyMonkey is complying with applicable privacy regulations like the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA). Our features can help you to comply when using SurveyMonkey.

SurveyMonkey account holders within or outside of the EU may be required to respond to requests from people who ask to exercise their privacy rights.

Learn more about SurveyMonkey and Privacy Rights.

Canceling Auto Renew (Android only)

You can cancel auto-renewal on the My Account page:

Log into your account at www.surveymonkey.com
Click your username in the upper right corner.
Click My Account.
Click the Billing Details tab.
Under Billing Profile, click Cancel next to Auto-renew.
Click Cancel Auto-Renew.

The account will downgrade to the free Basic plan at the end of the billing period. If your account is HIPAA-enabled, the account will instead go into a suspended state at the end of the billing period. See SurveyMonkey's cancellation policy for more information on canceling your account.

Canceling Auto Renew (iOS only)

I purchased my paid plan through the SurveyMonkey app.

If you wish to cancel auto-renewal, you can manage your subscription through the Apple App Store: http://support.apple.com/kb/ht4098

I purchased my paid plan on the SurveyMonkey website.

If your purchased your paid plan on the SurveyMonkey website, you can cancel auto-renewal on the My Account page:

Log into your account at www.surveymonkey.com
Click your username in the upper right corner.
Click My Account.
Click the Billing Details tab.
Under Billing Profile, click Cancel next to Auto-renew.
Click Cancel Auto-Renew.

The account will downgrade to the free Basic plan at the end of the billing period. 

If your account is HIPAA-enabled, the account will instead go into a suspended state at the end of the billing period. See SurveyMonkey's cancellation policy for more information on canceling your account.

Adding and Managing Team Members

If you are an admin for a SurveyMonkey team plan you can use your mobile app to add and manage users on your team. SurveyMonkey team plans let you collaborate on surveys with other users.

If you don’t have a team plan, learn how to create one and read more about how team billing works.

From your Home screen you can use the Team Status panel to:

Add new users to your team
View how many seats you’ve used and how many are available
View the number of active users on your team
View the number of users whose invites are pending

From the Team Update panel you can see how many invites haven’t been accepted and send invite reminders.

To invite a new user:

Either tap Add Users from your Home screen or tap a from the My Team screen.
Enter an email address for the user you want to invite.
Tap Send Invitation. If you haven’t already purchased a seat, you’ll be asked to confirm the purchase. You’re billed team overages for each invitation sent that exceeds the number of seats available on the team.

Tip! You can use the web app to create and manage a team sign up page.

From the My Team page you can manage and view your team’s members.

Tap on a Pending user to:

Resend their invitation email
Copy their invitation link
Cancel the invitation

Tap on an Active user to:

Reassign their account along with all of the surveys and data contained within it to another user. You’re not charged for reassigning accounts.
Permanently delete their account along with all of the survey and data contained in it. This frees up a seat on your team.
Changing Your Username, Email, or Password

To change your username, contact email, or password:

From the Home screen, tap the Account icon.
Tap the field you want to update to change it.
Create
Expand | Collapse
Move, Copy, or Delete Questions or Pages

Questions

To move, copy, or delete a question:

On the Edit screen, tap the settings icon in the upper right corner.
Tap Copy, Move, or Delete.
To move a question: Tap and hold the three lines next to the question you want to move, and drag and drop the question into the desired position in the survey.
To copy a question: Swipe left on the question you want to copy, and tap Copy.
To delete a question: Swipe left on the question you want to delete, and tap Delete.

Pages

To move a page:

On the Edit screen, tap the page numbers at the bottom of the screen.
Tap and hold the page number you want to move.
Drag the page to the desired position.

To delete a page:

On the Edit screen, tap the page count at the bottom of the screen and select the page you want to delete.
Tap the page count at the bottom of the page again and select delete.
Changing the Survey's Theme and Display Options

The SurveyMonkey app offers some ability to change the look and feel of your survey. You can choose from a selection of pre-made color themes, and configure a few display options to show or hide certain elements of the survey, like the survey title or question numbers.

NOTE: You can't customize themes on the SurveyMonkey app. Please log into your account on our desktop site to customize the name, colors, and typography of your survey theme.

To change a survey's theme:

On the Edit screen, tap . in the upper right corner.
Tap Color Themes.
Tap the preferred color scheme to apply it to your survey.

To show or hide the survey title, page title, or question numbers:

On the Edit screen, tap the Settings icon in the upper right corner.
Tap Display Options.
Tap the toggle next to each survey element to show or hide that element.
If the toggle is green (on), that element shows to survey takers when they take your survey.
If the toggle is white (off), that element is hidden from survey takers.
Tap Save.
Adding and Editing Questions

To add a question to a survey:

On the Edit screen, tap the circled Plus icon.
Tap the question type you want to add.
Enter the question text and answer choices.
Tap Save.

To edit a question:

On the Edit screen, tap the question you want to edit.
Make your changes.
Tap Save.

You can currently add the following question types on the SurveyMonkey app:

Multiple Choice
Dropdown
Comment Box/Paragraph
Matrix/Rating
Image
Text

You can edit all question types with the app, except A/B Tests (Random Assignment).

To access all available question types and options, log into your account at www.surveymonkey.com.

Creating and Previewing a Survey for Mobile

As you create your survey, keep in mind that many of your survey takers may take the survey on their phone or tablet. It's important to consider how the survey appears on a mobile screen, and how that can affect mobile completion rates.

When creating a survey for mobile survey takers:

Use simple multiple choice question types.
Be as clear and concise as possible; avoid long descriptions.
Limit the number of answer options so that all choices are visible on the screen at the same time.
Limit your use of the Comment Box/Paragraph question. Open-ended question types have a negative impact on mobile survey completion rates.
Distribute questions over multiple, short pages, rather than creating just a few, long pages.
If you add an image, keep in mind that mobile users' limited network download speed can cause the image to load slowly.
Preview the survey on your own mobile device before sending it to survey takers.

To preview your survey:

On the Edit screen, tap the Settings icon in the upper right corner.
Tap Preview & Test.
Fill out the survey as though you were a survey taker. This helps you confirm that the design is set up correctly, and help you find any parts of the survey you may want to edit or fix.

You can read more about the data behind these tips on our blog: How to Keep Your Survey Takers Happy on Mobile (English only)

Sending Surveys
Expand | Collapse
Run Your Survey in a Loop with Kiosk Mode

With Kiosk Mode you can turn your device into a survey taking station. When Kiosk Mode is running, your survey runs in a loop, returning to the beginning of the survey each time a response is collected. In order to run a survey using Kiosk Mode, the survey needs to be set to Allow Multiple Responses.

To run a survey in kiosk mode:

Click the Surveys icon. 
Select the survey you want survey takers to take.
Tap Send.
Turn on Multiple responses per device.
Tap Kiosk Mode.
Select whether you want to Continue without Screen Lock or Continue with Screen Lock. With screen lock on, your SurveyMonkey password needs to be entered into the device to exit Kiosk mode.

To exit Kiosk mode:

Tap the X in the top corner of your survey
Tap Close Kiosk Mode. If you have Screen Lock on, you’ll also be prompted to enter your SurveyMonkey password.
Sending Your Survey to Survey Takers

You can send a web link collector to survey takers using the SurveyMonkey app or collect responses directly on your device. 

To send a survey link:

Tap the Surveys icon. 
Tap the survey you want to send.
Tap Send. If there are multiple collectors on the survey, you’re prompted to choose an existing web link collector.
Select from the following options for sending your survey:
Tap the Survey Link and choose Copy Link or Open in Safari. 
Send via Email - Create an email message in your default mail client. The survey link is included in the body of the message. This is different than SurveyMonkey's email collector which allows you to send and track survey takers using SurveyMonkey's mailer. To use SurveyMonkey's email collector, log into our desktop site.
Send via Text - Send your survey link to others via SMS or iMessage.
Share to Facebook - Share your survey link on Facebook.
Share on Twitter - Share your survey link on Twitter.

If your survey takers are using a shared computer (e.g. in a computer lab), or if each of your survey takers needs to submit multiple surveys, tap the toggle next to Multiple responses per device to allow multiple responses per device.

To collect responses on your device:
Tap the Surveys icon. 
Tap the survey you want to send.
Tap Send. 
Select Kiosk Mode to collect responses directly on your device.

Once the Kiosk Mode survey is completed, you can choose to either Return to Start to enter a new response, or Close Kiosk Mode to return to the app.

The Kiosk Mode options control whether or not your SurveyMonkey password is required to return to the app:

Continue without Screen Lock - You’re able to return to the SurveyMonkey app without having to enter your SurveyMonkey password. This option is ideal if you are using Kiosk Mode to manually enter your own responses.
Continue with Screen Lock - You need to enter your SurveyMonkey password in order to return to the app. This option is ideal if you plan to collect responses in a setting where the survey takers are using your device.
Analyzing Surveys
Expand | Collapse
Sharing Your Results

You can create a Shared Data link to share your results online.

To create a Shared Data link:

Tap the Surveys icon. 
Tap the survey whose results you want to share.
Tap Analyze.
Tap the Three dots icon in the upper-right corner.
Tap Share Data. Tap Add Link to create a new page or tap an existing share link to edit it.
Configure the settings at the bottom of the screen.
Choose an option for sending the share link. You can also tap the link itself to Copy link or Open it in your mobile browser.

Log in to your account on www.surveymonkey.com to access more Shared Data settings.

Disabling or Deleting Share Links

When someone tries to access a disabled or deleted share link, they see a message that the shared data is unavailable. 

To disable a share link:

On the Share Data page, tap the shared data link you want to disable.
Under Settings, tap the toggle next to Status: Enabled. This turns the status to Disabled.

You can tap the toggle again to reactivate the link at any time.

To delete a share link:

On the Share Data page, swipe left on the shared data link you want to delete.
Tap Delete.
Viewing and Filtering Survey Responses

You can view a summary of your survey results or browse individual responses.

To view a summary of your survey results:

Tap the Surveys icon. 
Tap the survey whose results you want to view.
Tap Analyze.

You can change the chart type shown for a question by tapping on it. If you have a Net Promoter Score question in your survey, your score is be presented on a gauge chart. You cannot change this chart type in the app.

Tapping on a question also lets you create a filter on your results. Paid customers can filter survey results for closed-ended questions. Mobile filters create a quick view of your data and cannot be saved. To use saved filters, login to your SurveyMonkey account on our desktop site.

To browse individual responses:

On the Analyze screen, tap the Respondents icon at the top of the screen.
Choose the individual response you want to view from the list.
From there, you can tap the arrows to browse through the other responses.
Managing Surveys
Expand | Collapse
Managing Survey Alerts

If you have Survey Alerts turned on, we send you push notifications and emails when you receive new responses. You can turn survey alerts off for individual surveys.

If you turn off push notifications for the SurveyMonkey app, you will no longer receive email alerts.

There are two kinds of survey alerts:

All Surveys: Receive alerts when you get your first response to a new survey and on days you get responses to any active survey.
New Surveys Only: Only receive alerts when new surveys get their first response.

To manage survey alerts:

Tap the Profile icon. 
Tap New Responses under Notifications.
Select which kind of alerts you want.
Tap Done.

To turn survey alerts on or off for an individual survey:

Tap the Surveys icon. 
Tap the survey whose results you want to view.
Toggle New Response Alerts under Settings.
Closing a Survey to Stop Collecting Responses

To stop collecting responses, you must close all collectors on the survey. If there are any open collectors on the survey, the overall survey status remains open.

To close a collector:

Tap the Surveys icon. 
Tap the survey whose results you want to view.
On the Summary page, you can close your survey by changing the survey status:
If there is only one collector, tap the toggle next to Survey Status Open.
If there are multiple collectors, tap Status: Open. Tap the toggle next to the collector(s) you want to close.

When survey takers try to access the survey through a closed collector, they see a closed survey message. If you need to edit or customize the closed survey message, you can login to your SurveyMonkey account on our desktop site.

TIP! To re-open the collector, tap the Closed status.

Taking Surveys
Taking Surveys with SurveyMonkey Contribute

SurveyMonkey Contribute is no longer available in the SurveyMonkey app, but you can still access your account at contribute.surveymonkey.com.

If you want to take surveys on your mobile device, download the SurveyMonkey Rewards app for iOS or Android. SurveyMonkey Rewards lets you take surveys to earn gift cards or donate to your favorite charity.

Accepting Payments with PayPal

SurveyMonkey
Accepting Payments with PayPal

Paid feature: Accepting payments via PayPal is only available on some paid plans—see what's on your plan.

Let your respondents make payments via PayPal right within your form or survey. You can either assign prices to a single question to charge different amounts per answer option, or charge a fixed price for your entire form.

Connecting to PayPal and adding a payment page

PayPal is a third-party payment processor that lets you securely accept and manage payments online. You'll need to connect a PayPal Business or Personal account before you can add the payment option to your form to accept payments. Only the form owner can connect their PayPal account. You can't connect a PayPal account to surveys that are shared with you. 

Form creators can learn more about PayPal’s merchant fees associated with accepting payments. 

Creating Your Form to Accept Payments

Payment pages display at the end of your form. This means people need to complete your form in order to see the payment page. For a quick payment experience, try to make a short and simple form.

Prices must be a whole number between $1-$10,000 in most accepted currencies.

To create a form that accepts payments with PayPal:

Create a survey. From the Design Survey tab, select Options, and then select Payment. 
Select PayPal as the payment processor to collect payments.
If it’s your first time adding the PayPal Payment option, select Connect to PayPal and follow the instructions to log in or sign up.
Once connected into PayPal, select the Currency you wish to collect payments in.
Under Payment amount, select to assign the:
Same amount for everyone—all users are charged the same amount regardless of their responses.
Enter a Description for the payment and a Price. 
Payment linked to a question—people are charged based on the answer they select or enter in the payment question.
Select the Payment question you want to assign payment prices to.
You can assign prices to Multiple Choice, Dropdown, or Image Choice questions, or
You can assign a minimum or maximum amount to a Single Textbox question so the respondent can pay an amount they choose.
Enter the Price per answer option.
Add prices to each answer option.
Select Save.
A Payment page gets added to the end of your form.
If you wish to update the language on the Payment page, you can select Submit your payment to update the text displayed to respondents.


PayPal is free and easy to set up, but if you have any issues connecting your accounts you can reach out to the PayPal support team.

You can select Manage account from the side panel to open My Account to manage PayPal from Linked Accounts.

You can preview the form to see prices appear on the question and the PayPal checkout display, however it isn’t possible to test making a payment and no transactions can be processed while previewing.

Editing a form that accepts payment 

Changes to prices or currency will go into effect immediately for new responses. Editing a question with payment associated may be limited if this form already has responses.

TIP! If you have a limited amount of tickets or items that you want to accept payment for, you can add a quota to your form. Once the quota has been met, the form closes and respondents won't see the payment page.

Turning Off Payments

You can stop accepting payments from your form at any time by closing your form.

If you delete the form question associated with payments after you’ve collected responses, you will also delete any transaction records from previous payments in the Analyze Results section. You'll always be able to see your complete transaction record in your PayPal account.

If you disconnect your PayPal account in My Account, you won't be able to collect any additional payments from your forms or surveys.

Currency Options

Forms creators can only charge in the following currencies: AUD, CAD, CHF, EUR, GBP, HKD, JPY, NOK, NZD, SEK, SGD, and USD. People taking your survey have plenty of options to pay.

Collecting Responses

After you design your form, create a collector to send it out and start accepting payments. You can send a form with a payment page using any collector type, except for Audience, Mobile SDK, and Offline Mode.

After a respondent submits a payment, they won't be able to return to the form even when Response Editing is on.

Viewing Payment Transactions and Responses

When someone submits a payment through your form, PayPal collects all of the details from the payment page, which means SurveyMonkey never saves or stores any credit card numbers.

You can go to the Analyze Results section of your form to see the transactions made along with responses in your Question summary or Tabular view. You'll find them at the very bottom of your form results.

The Payment Summary shows:

PayPal’s Charge ID 
The amount paid
The date and time
The item description
The respondent's first and last name
The transaction status

This is only a snapshot of each payment taken at the time the form is completed. To view real-time purchase totals, make refunds, and transfer funds to your bank account, log in to PayPal.

Making a Payment

When someone submits a payment through your form, they'll receive an email from PayPal confirming their transaction. Transactions appear on their credit or debit card statements with the name of your form.

SurveyMonkey's platform allows you to integrate with third-party payment processors. Some of these payment processors may require Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) under the EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2). People in Europe who submit payment through your form may need to provide additional authentication. It's not possible to disable this authentication when payment processors require it.

If someone runs into issues making payment, they can reach out to PayPal or the form owner for assistance.

Managing Brand Assets in the Library

SurveyMonkey
Managing Brand Assets in the Library

Library

Paid feature
Log in to see if this feature is included in your plan.
Log in
Sign up free

The library is where team members can find and use shared assets to create surveys. These shared assets include images, documents, templates, themes, and questions.

Primary Admins and Admins can add or manage items in the team library and set default assets to be automatically added to new surveys that teammates create. To review access levels for other roles, see Team Roles or Enterprise Team Roles.

If your Enterprise team has Divisions, you can also access division libraries that have additional survey controls.

Video Overview
Items in the Library

The library is a collection of shared resources that some team members, depending on their roles, can use when they creating surveys.

Images: Add approved visual assets to use in surveys—like your company's logo.
Themes: Choose a survey theme that best reflects your organization.
CSS theme (Enterprise only): Add CSS for a custom survey theme that matches your visual assets, fonts, colors, and style preferences.
Templates: Turn a custom survey into a standard template so your team can reapply the format in new surveys.
Documents: Provide team members with guidelines and resources for creating surveys for your organization.
Questions (Enterprise only): Add company questions to a Custom Question Bank so team members will add them to surveys in a consistent format.
Presentation template (Enterprise only): Apply a custom template to your team’s PPT presentation exports for survey results.
Adding Items to the Library

Primary Admins and Admins can add new items to the library.

To add a new item to the library:

Select My Team from the main navigation and select Library.
Select + New Item (Add item).
Choose the item you want to add:
Image and document: Browse for the image or document on your computer, or import it via URL.
Theme: Select an existing custom theme from the list. If you don't have any custom themes, create a new one.
CSS theme (Enterprise only): Select Copy code and paste in your preferred CSS editing tool. Make customizations to the code and then see a preview by adding it to the box under Customize theme and selecting Generate preview. Once you’re happy with the theme, select Save.
Template: Select an existing survey from the list. If you don't have any surveys, create a new one. Every aspect of the survey design will be included in the template—all questions, the theme, logic, options, and images. If the survey you choose uses a custom theme that's not yet in your library, that theme will also be added to the library.
Question (Enterprise only): Add a new question in the Design Survey section. Once the question is saved, hover over it and click Library to save it to the library.
Presentation template (Enterprise only): Upload a PPTX file containing the template you want applied to the presentation exports. To create a custom template for your PPT exports, download and make changes to this sample PPTX file. Open the file, navigate to View, and click Slide Master. Modify the first slide (parent slide) of the Slide Master to reflect your desired font size, font color, footer, header, background color or image, and other options. Any changes made to other slides will not be reflected in PPT exports. For additional help creating a custom template, you can review Microsoft's resource on creating a PowerPoint template.
Add a Title (Name) and Description that will help team members understand how and when to use the item in their own surveys.
For some items, choose if you’d like to make the item a team default. Learn more about setting default assets.
Upload Requirements
Type	Size	Format
Image	2 MB or less	JPG, PNG, or GIF
Document	16 MB or less	DOC, DOCX, or PDF
Presentation template	2 MB	PPTX
Managing Existing Items in the Library

In the Library, Primary Admins and Admins can manage existing items by clicking the three dots to the right of the item and choosing an action from the menu. The actions available depend on the item type.

Action	Description
Edit details	Change the title (Name) and description of the item to give more context to team members when they visit the library.
Remove	Remove the item from your library. This doesn't affect any surveys that already use that item. If you remove a theme or template, the custom theme or survey it's based on will remain in your account.
Download	Download images and documents to your computer.
Preview	Preview images and documents in the library.
To preview a document, download it to your computer.
To preview a template, choose Edit details and click Preview Survey under the survey details.
Set as default	Set a default logo or theme, or presentation template to survey's your team creates.
Setting Default Assets

Primary Admins and Admins can set defaults to be used in all new surveys the team creates.

Tip! First add items to the Library, to then use them as the team default setting.

To manage default assets:

Select My Team from the main navigation and select Library.
Select Set defaults
Choose the asset you want as default for the Team:
Logo
Theme
Template*
Text*
End page*
Presentation*
(Optional) Set Restrictions for the team.
(Optional) Click the toggle to turn Division Admins Permissions on and off.
Select Apply.

*Enterprise only.

If you're interested in these Enterprise-only features, get in touch with our sales team. Existing customers, please contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

When adding a new image, theme, CSS theme, or presentation template, select the default option to have it applied to all new surveys in your team.

To set an existing asset as a default, click the three dots to the right of the item and select the default option.

Creating Surveys with Default Items

When a default is set for the team and someone creates a new survey, the default item is automatically applied. Existing surveys aren't changed.

If your Enterprise team has access to Divisions, your Admins may have restricted access to remove or edit default items.

Using Items from the Library in Surveys

To use items from the library in surveys, select My Team from the main navigation and then Library to browse, preview, or download library items.

For instructions on how to use each type of item in the library, see the relevant section below.

Expand | Collapse
Themes and CSS themes

To apply a team theme to a survey:

In the Design Survey section, click THEMES in the left sidebar.
Select Teams.
Select the theme you want to apply.
Images

To add an image from the library to a survey:

In the Design Survey section, add a Logo, Image, or Image A/B Test to your survey.
Select Upload File.
Under the From Library tab, select the image you want to use.

If adding an image to question text or answer choice field, you'll need the library image's source image URL. From the Library, right-click the image to open the image source URL in a new tab and copy the URL from the address bar. Add the image to your survey using the formatting toolbar.

Templates

To create a new survey from a team template:

Select My Team. 
Select Library.
Optional: Look for the template or choose Filter to narrow down library options.
Select the three dots (...) next to the template you want to use and select Create survey.

In the Design survey section, you can make any edits you want before sending out your survey. Any edits you make are unique to your survey and won't affect the template in the team library.

Similarly, if an Admin makes edits to the template in the library after you created your survey, it won't affect your existing survey.

Documents

Documents can't be added to surveys, but you can download them to your computer.

To download a document to your computer:

Select My Team from the main navigation and select Library.
Select the three dots next to the document you want to download.
Select Download.

You can't preview documents within SurveyMonkey.

If you need to attach a document to a survey, host it on a third-party site and add a hyperlink to your survey.

Questions

Everyone in your Enterprise team can search and browse company questions in the Custom Question Bank and add them to their surveys.

Presentation

Follow the steps to export your survey results as a PPT.

Division Libraries and Survey Controls

Enterprise Feature: Only available on some Enterprise plans. If you're interested, contact sales. If you already have an Enterprise account, contact your Customer Success Manager.

How It Works

When your team has Divisions—sub-groups within your team that can be managed independently of one another—each division can have its own division library with its own set of assets. A division library allows each division to have unique assets that are different from the assets in the team library and other divisions.

Division members can use the assets from the team library or their division library, which ensures all surveys meet either the team's or division’s unique branding needs.

The assets that team members can see, manage, and use depend on their role, if they belong to a division, and whether those assets have additional default settings or restrictions. Only the Primary Admin and Admin have full access to view, add, and manage the team library and all division libraries.

Primary Admins and Admins can:	Division Admins can:	Users can:
View, add, or manage assets in the team library (as described earlier in this article) or any division library

Click a division name to view the assets in that division library and set defaults for that division

Set team and division defaults
Allow Division Admins to override the asset settings for their division

Create surveys without any restrictions	View assets from the team library

View, add, or manage assets (except adding questions) for the division libraries they manage

Click a division name to view the assets in that specific division library

Set defaults for the divisions they manage, if given permission by the Primary Admin

Create surveys using the assets they have permission to use from the team library or division libraries they manage	View the assets from the team library and division library, if they are assigned to a division

Create surveys using the assets they have permission to use from the team library or division library
Expand | Collapse
Team Library vs. Division Libraries

The team library is for everyone on the team. A division library is only available to the people assigned to that division. If someone is not assigned to a division, they only have access to the team library.

If an asset is Set as default for a Division, that setting overrides the team default.

Limitation: It’s not possible to add Custom Questions to a Division Library. 

Navigating the Library

On the Library page, there's a Library dropdown to navigate between the team and division libraries.

The Filter button lets anyone narrow down their library by item type. Primary Admins, Admins, and Division Admins can also Filter to display items from specific libraries.

Setting Default Division Assets

From the Library page, Primary Admins and Admins can click Set team defaults to set a default logo, theme, template, or intro text for all new surveys the team creates.

Primary Admins, Admins, and Division Admins can Set division defaults. If an asset is Set as default for a Division, that setting overrides the team default.

After adding a default team or division asset, Primary Admins and Admins can set further restrictions. Assets can have:

No restrictions—team members can remove or replace the default asset
Restrictions to logos or themes in the library—team members can choose to replace the default asset with another asset in their library
Restriction to only the default asset—team members can only create surveys with the default asset

There's also a toggle to Allow Division Admins to override the asset settings for their division. If the Division Admin is given permission, they can add and manage assets for their division libraries. If they aren’t allowed, they can only view their division libraries.

When division defaults differ from the Team default, Primary Admins, Admins, or Division Admins can click Reset to Team Defaults to revert the asset and its restrictions back.

Tip! You can select the size and position of a default logo and choose to restrict whether users can edit your selections.

Creating Surveys

The assets that team members can use for creating new surveys depend on their role, if they belong to a division, and whether those assets have default settings or restrictions on them.

When creating surveys, Division Admins and Users can only see the assets they have permission to view and use. Primary Admins and Admins don’t have any restrictions as they create surveys so they can add new assets to libraries as they need.

If an asset is set as a default, it's automatically added when a new survey is created. Depending on the restrictions set, the team member may or may not have the ability to remove or update the asset.

Survey Tooltips

SurveyMonkey
Survey Tooltips

Tooltips give survey takers more information about a specific word or phrase in your survey. For example, you can use a tooltip to define a word in your survey people may not be familiar with or give extra context about how to answer a survey question.

Adding a Tooltip

You can add one tooltip per survey question or additional survey text block. It’s not possible to add a tooltip to answer text, the survey title, or intro paragraphs.

To add a tooltip:

Go to the Design Survey section of your survey.
Click a question or additional text field.
Highlight the text you want to add a tooltip to.
Click the Tooltip icon in the formatting toolbar.
Enter your tooltip text.
Click OK.
Deleting a Tooltip

To delete a tooltip:

Go to the Design Survey section of your survey.
Click the question or additional text.
Highlight the text with the tooltip.
Click the Tooltip icon in the formatting toolbar.
Click the Delete icon.
What Survey Takers See

Words with tooltips added are underlined. Survey takers can hover over the word to read the tooltip.

Build Surveys with AI

SurveyMonkey
Build Surveys with AI

Build with AI, powered by the Azure OpenAI service and OpenAI, makes it easy and quick to create a survey.

To create a survey, type a prompt that includes your survey goals but excludes sensitive information. With a click of a button, we'll generate a survey for you. You can choose to use it and edit it, re-generate a new survey with an edited prompt, or start over with another survey creation method.

How Your Data is Processed

Build with AI uses the Azure OpenAI service and OpenAI to generate your survey. Your data isn't used to train the Azure OpenAI service or OpenAI models. Learn how this feature processes your data.

Avoid including any sensitive information in your prompts—you are responsible for the information you enter into Build with AI. Please note that the Azure OpenAI service and OpenAI do not use prompts in connection with Build with AI to train Azure OpenAI service and OpenAI models or improve OpenAI’s service offering.

Feature Availability and Settings
Build with AI is only available to some customers in the supported regions.
Build a Survey with AI

To create a survey with Build with AI:

Select Create Survey.
Select Build with AI.
Enter a prompt. We recommend using one of the examples as a template, but you can also write your own prompt from scratch. 
If you use the SurveyMonkey app, you can choose to use voice commands or type your survey prompt.
Submit the prompt to generate a survey.
Preview your survey. If you want to use it, select Continue to edit and customize the survey. Otherwise, you can Try another prompt or start over with another survey creation method.
Limitations

Survey prompts can be up to 50,000 characters long.

You can submit up to 25 AI-generated survey prompts per hour. The number of prompts per hour may be lower before signing into SurveyMonkey.

Your Survey Content

AI-generated surveys may include any of the following question types:

Multiple choice
Checkbox
NPS
Name
Email
Address
Phone
Single Textbox
Matrix/Rating Scale
Ranking
Star Rating

Once you choose to use the survey and you're customizing it, you can add in other question types. If your survey includes paid question types, you can upgrade to keep them or remove them to send your survey for free.

Certain survey use cases are not permitted—for details, please see SurveyMonkey's Acceptable Uses Policy, as well as additional third-party provider usage policies, and acceptable use and conduct policies.

How to Write a Prompt to Generate a Survey
State your goal (e.g., we want to improve the employee experience).
Describe what you want to know (e.g., we need to survey our employees about pay, benefits, hours, workload, and culture).
Provide general context describing who is sending the survey (e.g., we're a large sporting goods manufacturer).
Specify what demographic or company information you want to know about your respondents (e.g., business industry and size, or age and gender).
Be specific and as detailed as possible about the desired context, outcome, length, or style. 
Be precise—avoid ambiguity or vagueness.
Iterate on your prompt until you get a survey draft you can work with.

If your prompt contains unsafe content, you may receive an error or be unable to create an AI-generated survey for up to an hour. You can create a survey in another way or wait to retry Build with AI with an edited prompt.

Mobile App Experience

When using Build with AI in the SurveyMonkey app, you can use voice commands to create your survey prompt rather than typing it out. The app uses native OS speech-to-text to capture your voice prompts. Voice prompts are not stored in SurveyMonkey – only the prompt’s text output is stored.

Once survey questions are proposed on the preview page, you can Continue to edit and customize your survey. Or, select Try another prompt to revise your prompt.

Combining or Hiding Answer Choices

SurveyMonkey
Combining or Hiding Answer Choices

You can combine or hide answer choices in a chart for closed-ended question types with a single answer choice allowed.

Combine Answer Choices

To combine or hide answer choices:

Go to the Analyze Results section of your survey.
Scroll to the chart you want to hide answer choices from.
Click the answer choice from the data table below the chart.
Select either Exclude from total or Hide and recalculate. We'll recalculate the data for you. (If you don't see the option, the feature isn't available for the question type.)
If combining, select the answer choices and rename the label.

You can also filter by combined answer choices. To uncombine or unhide answer choices, click the appropriate answer choice and select Uncombine data or click Show beneath the data table.

Combining and hiding answer choices only affects the display of your charts—it doesn't affect the raw data or survey design. These combined labels can't be used to create filters, compare rules, or show rules.

Hide Answer Choices with No Responses

Hide answer choices that didn't receive any responses from your chart. If you hide zero-response answer choices, they won't appear in PDF or PowerPoint exports of summary data.

To hide answer choices that didn't receive any responses:

Go to the Analyze Results section of your survey.
Scroll to the chart you want to hide answer choices from.
Select Customize, then go to the Display Options.
Select Zero-response answer choices.

The following question types aren't supported: Best/Worst Scale, Matrix, Matrix Dropdown, NPS, Ranking, Slider, Star Rating

Help
Integrations

Automate with Quick Actions in Connect

SurveyMonkey
Automate with Quick Actions in Connect

The Connect apps section of your survey is the place to connect your survey data to your business apps to automate data sharing, collaborate smarter, and save time. Automating with quick actions helps to improve information sharing, iterate on survey feedback, and save time.

Connect can only handle surveys that are a maximum of 100 pages or 100 questions. Complex matrix questions are limited to 100 rows, 100 columns, and 100 choices.

Quick Actions

Quick actions are simple automations that connect SurveyMonkey responses to popular business apps, like:

Post notifications to Slack or Microsoft Teams to share targeted data with the right people, as responses roll in. Posting to these apps can help surface new ideas, channel feedback, or escalate something so teams can take action faster.
Export responses to Excel or Google Sheets to share in-the-moment data with your team, which you can merge with other key data for deeper insights.
Data selection and filtering

When setting up quick actions, you can choose whether to act on all response data or target responses when a respondent selects a specific answer.

Targeting the response data helps you channel the right survey data to the right people, making your quick action more relevant, usable, and efficient.

What’s the difference between apps with quick actions and integrations?

You can find all apps with quick actions in Connect apps, along with some integrations. 

The lightweight quick actions let you easily automate useful tasks, like creating notifications for visibility, further analysis, or prompt follow-up action. Setting up quick actions could improve your team’s collaboration and amplify your impact, all within SurveyMonkey. 

Only some integrations are accessible from Connect apps, but all integrations are available in the SurveyMonkey App Directory. You may need to install these integrations outside of SurveyMonkey. There are 200+ pre-built integrations helping you connect with popular CRMs, marketing automation tools, and BI platforms.

Navigating the Connect Apps tab

From the Connect apps Discover tab, search or browse the quick actions or explore some integration offerings.

Select Manage to monitor or edit any quick actions you’ve already set up. 

Managing your Quick Actions 

Within the Connect apps space, you can manage and monitor all your actions, in one place. Selecting the green toggle will deactivate the action, but remain listed as a connected app that you can tap to re-activate. You can select the three dots menu (...) to edit a quick action’s set up, or Delete or Reauthenticate the app.

If you want to manage an integration you previously installed, select the SurveyMonkey App Directory’s tile that’s specific to that integration.
